title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
猗歟盛哉夫我
國家每三歲一貢士而試期率在
子午卯酉之歲永為定制以十
干十二支相配甲子寔歲紀之
始
太宗文皇帝定鼎北都據此形勝壯
大雄偉已有定勢而十三藩
punctuated: 猗歟盛哉！夫我國家每三歲一貢士，而試期率在子午卯酉之歲，永為定制。以十干十二支相配，甲子寔歲紀之始。太宗文皇帝定鼎北都，據此形勝，壯大雄偉，已有定勢，而十三藩
translation_en: Ah, how splendid! Our dynasty presents scholars as tribute once every three years, and the examinations generally fall in the years of zi, wu, mao, and you—the Rat, Horse, Rabbit, and Rooster—as a permanently established rule. The ten Heavenly Stems are paired with the twelve Earthly Branches, and jiazi is indeed the beginning of the cycle of years. Emperor Wen, Taizong, established the seat of government in the northern capital. Taking advantage of its commanding terrain, he secured a position of imposing strength and grandeur, while the thirteen provinces…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之輔
京師乃天下首地士生于斯當此
歲紀之始而應此首地之試其
遭際可謂盛矣攄誠奮庸此其
時也仰惟我
皇上勵精宵旰孜孜每于退
朝之際
===
召見大臣諏詢治道羣臣莫不忻
躍仰戴以為唐虞都俞之美復
見于
今日矣邇者考察内外庶臣嚴黜
罰以儆有位務期舍舊從新以
共成雍熈之治天時人事蓋有
若符契然者間有一二不職有
punctuated:
之輔。京師乃天下首地，士生于斯，當此歲紀之始而應此首地之試，其遭際可謂盛矣！攄誠奮庸，此其時也。仰惟我皇上勵精宵旰，孜孜每于退朝之際，召見大臣，諏詢治道。羣臣莫不忻躍仰戴，以為唐虞都俞之美復見于今日矣。
邇者考察内外庶臣，嚴黜罰以儆有位，務期舍舊從新，以共成雍熈之治。天時人事，蓋有若符契然者。間有一二不職有
translation_en:
…as its supports. The capital is the foremost place in all the realm. For scholars born here to sit the examination in this foremost place at the beginning of this cycle of years—their fortunate circumstances may indeed be called splendid! Now is the time to give full expression to their loyalty and exert themselves in service.
We reverently consider how our Emperor devotes himself tirelessly to government, from early morning until late at night. Whenever he withdraws from court, he diligently summons his great ministers and consults them on the way of governing. All his ministers rejoice and look up to him with reverence, believing that the admirable exchanges of counsel and assent in the days of Yao and Shun have appeared again today.
Recently, officials serving both within and outside the capital have been evaluated, with strict dismissals and punishments to admonish those in office. The aim is to abandon old ways and adopt new ones, so that together they may bring about harmonious and prosperous rule. Heaven’s timing and human affairs seem to fit together like the matching halves of a tally. Occasionally there are one or two derelict officials …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
司具疏以聞
詔下黜罰如例此可見
聖明超越尋常萬萬而爲吾人臣者
當益加脩飭之時乎適順天府
鄕試以考試官請
上以命學士臣瀾左諭德兼侍講臣
貴往主文柄臣等聞
命相與言曰人材之高下進退之
當否世道之隆汚係焉况科目
仕進階梯治理之原尤所當謹
今日濫預竊自榮幸而感激圖報
實有兢惕不任者旣
陛辭入院提調則府尹臣琦府丞
臣佐監試則御史臣淮臣壽同
punctuated:
司具疏以聞，詔下黜罰如例。此可見聖明超越尋常萬萬，而爲吾人臣者，當益加脩飭之時乎！

適順天府鄕試，以考試官請，上以命學士臣瀾、左諭德兼侍講臣貴往主文柄。臣等聞命，相與言曰：「人材之高下，進退之當否，世道之隆汚係焉。况科目，仕進階梯，治理之原，尤所當謹。今日濫預，竊自榮幸，而感激圖報，實有兢惕不任者。」

旣陛辭入院，提調則府尹臣琦、府丞臣佐，監試則御史臣淮、臣壽，同
translation_en:
…the responsible officials submitted memorials reporting the matter, and an imperial decree ordered dismissal and punishment according to the established regulations. This shows that His Majesty’s sagacity surpasses the ordinary ten thousandfold. Is this not a time when we, his servants, should redouble our efforts at self-cultivation and discipline?

It happened that Shuntian Prefecture requested Examiners for its Provincial Examination. His Majesty therefore commanded his servants Lan, Academician, and Gui, Left Mentor and concurrently Expositor-in-waiting, to go and preside over the selection of examination compositions. On receiving the command, we said to one another: “The flourishing or decline of the moral order depends upon the quality of men of talent and whether their advancement or rejection is appropriate. Moreover, the examinations are the ladder to official service and the source of good government; they demand particular care. Undeservedly entrusted with this responsibility today, we privately count ourselves honored and fortunate. Yet, moved by gratitude and intent on repaying this favor, we truly feel an overwhelming apprehension.”

After taking leave of His Majesty and entering the examination compound, we were joined as Proctors by his servants Qi, Prefect, and Zuo, Vice Prefect; examination supervision was entrusted to his servants Huai and Shou, Investigating Censors; the Associate …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考官則敎授臣容敎諭臣用臣
世傳臣瑞臣大霖臣璣訓導臣天麒臣
春暘臣大恒以至受卷彌封謄錄對
讀諸執事皆遴選以充此定規
也試畢有錄列中式士子之氏
名貫址所治之經及三場文字
之詞理俱到者刻以示後此定
===
式也取士之數至百三十五人
而止此定額也守其定規則各
司其事而不敢越倣其定式則
各有其序而不敢紊遵其定額
則取士雖衆而不敢加臣等於
此復何爲哉亦惟竭心思校閱
以求合乎定論庶幾以塞吾責
punctuated: 考官則敎授臣容、敎諭臣用、臣世傳、臣瑞、臣大霖、臣璣、訓導臣天麒、臣春暘、臣大恒，以至受卷、彌封、謄錄、對讀諸執事，皆遴選以充，此定規也。試畢有錄，列中式士子之氏名、貫址、所治之經，及三場文字之詞理俱到者，刻以示後，此定式也。取士之數，至百三十五人而止，此定額也。守其定規，則各司其事而不敢越；倣其定式，則各有其序而不敢紊；遵其定額，則取士雖衆而不敢加。臣等於此復何爲哉？亦惟竭心思校閱，以求合乎定論，庶幾以塞吾責。
translation_en: …the Associate Examiners were your servants Rong, a prefectural school instructor; Yong, Shichuan, Rui, Dalin, and Ji, county school instructors; and Tianqi, Chunyang, and Daheng, assistant instructors. All functionaries, down to those receiving examination papers, sealing identifying information, transcribing papers, and checking the transcriptions against the originals, were carefully selected to fill their posts. These are the established regulations. After the examination, a record is compiled listing the successful candidates’ names, places of registration and residence, and the Classics they specialized in, together with compositions from the three sessions distinguished in both expression and reasoning. It is printed to show to posterity. This is the established format. The number of candidates selected reaches one hundred and thirty-five and goes no further. This is the established quota. By observing the established regulations, each attends to his own duties and dares not exceed them; by following the established format, each matter has its proper order, which no one dares disrupt; by adhering to the established quota, although many candidates are selected, no one dares increase their number. What further role, then, remains for us, your servants? Only to devote all our mental energies to evaluating the papers, seeking to accord with settled judgments, in the hope of thereby discharging our responsibility.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然詞理有純駁惟擇其明暢者
取之况各專一經未敢自以爲
有定見也設有奉職不謹假公
售私者萬一敗露則
國有定法在可不懼哉諸士子躬
逢
盛際其所謂攄誠奮庸者固不必
===
求之於窮居定業之外惟慎名
檢重交際以求無愧于古聖賢
之定則而已若然不惟不負斯
科斯地之選而于主司豈不亦
與有光哉
翰林院學士奉議大夫江瀾謹
序
punctuated:
然詞理有純駁，惟擇其明暢者取之。况各專一經，未敢自以爲有定見也。設有奉職不謹、假公售私者，萬一敗露，則國有定法在，可不懼哉？諸士子躬逢盛際，其所謂攄誠奮庸者，固不必求之於窮居定業之外，惟慎名檢、重交際，以求無愧于古聖賢之定則而已。若然，不惟不負斯科斯地之選，而于主司豈不亦與有光哉？
翰林院學士奉議大夫江瀾謹序。
translation_en:
Yet expression and reasoning vary in their soundness; we select only those essays that are clear and fluent. Moreover, each of us specializes in a single Classic, and we dare not presume that our judgments are definitive. Should anyone discharge his duties carelessly or exploit public office to advance private interests, and should this happen to be exposed, the state has established laws in force. Can we fail to fear them?
You candidates have the good fortune to live in a flourishing age. What is called giving full expression to your sincerity and exerting yourselves in service need certainly not be sought beyond pursuing your settled vocation while living in obscurity. You need only safeguard your reputation and conduct, and take your dealings with others seriously, seeking to stand without shame before the established standards of the ancient sages and worthies. If you do so, you will not only prove worthy of selection in this examination and this place: will not the officials presiding over it also share in the honor?
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Lan, Academician of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Deliberation.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
四書
知者樂水仁者樂山知者動仁者靜知者
樂仁者壽
故君子尊德性而道問學
其君用之則安富尊榮其子弟從之則孝
弟忠信
易
君子行此四德者故曰乾元亨利貞
===
謙亨君子有終
極天下之賾者存乎卦鼓天下之動者存
乎辭
乾天也故稱乎父坤地也故稱乎母
書
知人則哲能官人安民則惠黎民懷之能
哲而惠何憂乎驩兜何遷乎有苗何畏
乎巧言令色孔壬
先王顧諟天之明命以承上下神祇社稷
punctuated:
四書
知者樂水，仁者樂山；知者動，仁者靜；知者樂，仁者壽。
故君子尊德性而道問學。
其君用之，則安富尊榮；其子弟從之，則孝弟忠信。

易
君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」
謙，亨，君子有終。
極天下之賾者存乎卦，鼓天下之動者存乎辭。
乾，天也，故稱乎父；坤，地也，故稱乎母。

書
知人則哲，能官人；安民則惠，黎民懷之。能哲而惠，何憂乎驩兜？何遷乎有苗？何畏乎巧言令色孔壬？
先王顧諟天之明命，以承上下神祇、社稷
translation_en:
Four Books

The wise delight in water; the benevolent delight in mountains. The wise are active; the benevolent are still. The wise are joyful; the benevolent are long-lived.

Thus the gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning.

If their ruler employs them, he enjoys peace, wealth, dignity, and glory; if his sons and younger brothers follow them, they become filial, respectful toward their elders, loyal, and trustworthy.

Book of Changes

The gentleman practices these four virtues; hence it is said: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness.”

Qian (Modesty): success. The gentleman carries matters through to completion.

What fathoms the profound complexities of all under Heaven resides in the hexagrams; what sets all under Heaven in motion resides in the statements attached to them.

Qian is Heaven and is therefore called father; Kun is Earth and is therefore called mother.

Book of Documents

To understand people is wisdom, enabling one to appoint them to office; to bring peace to the people is benevolence, and the common people cherish such a ruler. If one can be wise and benevolent, what cause is there to worry about Huandou? What need is there to banish the Youmiao? What cause is there to fear those of glib speech, ingratiating looks, and great cunning?

The former kings kept Heaven’s bright mandate constantly before them, thereby serving the spirits above and below and the gods of soil and grain…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
宗廟罔不祗肅
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧
德威惟畏德明惟明
詩
雞既鳴矣朝既盈矣匪雞則鳴蒼蠅之聲
東方明矣朝既昌矣匪東方則明月出
之光
我田既臧農夫之慶
君子萬年介爾昭明
===
有来雝雝至止肅肅相維辟公天子穆穆
春秋
滕侯薛侯来朝隱公十一年滕子来朝桓公二年
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子
盟于踐土公朝于王所公會晋侯
齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯陳子莒子邾子秦
人于溫天王狩于河陽壬申公朝
于王所諸侯遂圍許俱僖公二十八年
晋韓厥帥師伐鄭仲孫蔑會齊崔杼曹人
punctuated:
宗廟，罔不祗肅。
六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧。
德威惟畏，德明惟明。

詩
雞既鳴矣，朝既盈矣。匪雞則鳴，蒼蠅之聲。東方明矣，朝既昌矣。匪東方則明，月出之光。
我田既臧，農夫之慶。
君子萬年，介爾昭明。
有来雝雝，至止肅肅。相維辟公，天子穆穆。

春秋
滕侯、薛侯来朝，隱公十一年。滕子来朝，桓公二年。
公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土。公朝于王所。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于溫。天王狩于河陽。壬申，公朝于王所。諸侯遂圍許。俱僖公二十八年。
晋韓厥帥師伐鄭。仲孫蔑會齊崔杼、曹人
translation_en:
…and the ancestral temples: toward none did they fail to show reverence and solemn respect.
The six ministers divided their duties, each leading his subordinates to guide the governors of the nine provinces.
When virtue inspires awe, it is truly to be feared; when virtue gives illumination, it is truly enlightening.

Book of Odes
“The cock has already crowed; the court is already full.” “It is not the cock that is crowing, but the buzzing of flies.” “The east is already light; the court is already thronged.” “It is not the east that is light, but the radiance of the rising moon.”
Our fields have yielded well: this is the farmers’ joy.
May you, noble lord, live ten thousand years; may your radiant glory be made great.
They come in harmony, arriving with solemn reverence. Those assisting are the lords; the Son of Heaven is grave and dignified.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The Marquis of Teng and the Marquis of Xue came to pay court. Eleventh year of Duke Yin. The Viscount of Teng came to pay court. Second year of Duke Huan.
The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and they made a covenant at Jiantu. The duke paid court at the king’s place of residence. The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and a representative of Qin at Wen. The Heavenly King went hunting at Heyang. On the renshen day, the duke paid court at the king’s place of residence. The assembled lords then besieged Xu. All these entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.
Han Jue of Jin led an army to attack Zheng. Zhongsun Mie met Cui Zhu of Qi and a representative of Cao…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
邾人杞人次于鄫襄公元年
晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵昭公元年
禮記
是天子之事守也故天子祭天地諸侯祭
社稷
天垂象聖人則之
此所以祭先王之廟也所以獻酬酳酢也
所以官序貴賤各得其宜也所以示後
世有尊卑長幼之序也
===
是故君子貌足畏也色足憚也言足信也
第貳場
論
天地之帥吾其性
詔誥表內科道
擬漢文帝賜天下今年田租之半詔二年
擬宋改封孔子後文宣公世愿爲衍聖公
誥至和二年
擬宋儒臣葉采進近思錄集解表淳祐十二年
punctuated:
邾人、杞人次于鄫。襄公元年。
晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵。昭公元年。

禮記
是天子之事守也，故天子祭天地，諸侯祭社稷。
天垂象，聖人則之。
此所以祭先王之廟也，所以獻酬酳酢也，所以官序貴賤各得其宜也，所以示後世有尊卑長幼之序也。
是故君子貌足畏也，色足憚也，言足信也。

第貳場
論
天地之帥，吾其性。

詔誥表內科道
擬漢文帝賜天下今年田租之半詔。二年。
擬宋改封孔子後文宣公世愿爲衍聖公誥。至和二年。
擬宋儒臣葉采進近思錄集解表。淳祐十二年。
translation_en:
…the men of Zhu and Qi encamped at Zeng. First year of Duke Xiang.
Xun Wu of Jin led an army and defeated the Di at Dalu. First year of Duke Zhao.

Record of Rites
“These are the duties entrusted to the Son of Heaven. Thus the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and the regional lords sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain.”
“Heaven displays its signs; the sages take them as their models.”
“This is how sacrifices are performed in the temples of former kings; how wine is offered, exchanged, presented after eating, and offered in return; how official ranks and distinctions of high and low each receive their proper place; and how later generations are shown the ordering of honored and humble, elder and younger.”
“Therefore, the gentleman’s bearing inspires awe, his expression commands reverence, and his words merit trust.”

Second Session
Discourse
“That which commands Heaven and Earth is my nature.”

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials [the following characters, 內科道, are unclear here: ?]
Compose a hypothetical edict of Emperor Wen of Han granting everyone in the empire remission of half of the current year’s land tax. Second year of his reign.
Compose a hypothetical Song proclamation changing the title of Shiyuan, a descendant of Confucius, from Duke for Propagating Culture (Wenxuan gong) to Duke for Perpetuating the Sage (Yansheng gong). Second year of the Zhihe era.
Compose a hypothetical memorial by the Song Confucian official Ye Cai presenting his Collected Explanations of Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsilu jijie). Twelfth year of the Chunyou era.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
子孫違犯教令
良賤為婚姻
卑幼私擅用財
毆受業師
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問自古帝王平治天下必有要道以為之
===
本不徒以之淑其身而又垂訓子孫以
為不易之法盖嘗伏覩我
太宗文皇帝御製聖學心法矣其憂深其慮遠
其所采皆聖賢之嘉言信乎萬世
聖子神孫保位修德之龜鑑也然其綱有四而
不知以何者為之要其目三十有一而
不知以何者為之先
鴻猷大旨之攸存造端託始之深意其可得
而聞歟學焉而果得其要其於古帝王
punctuated:
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限；子孫違犯教令；良賤為婚姻；卑幼私擅用財；毆受業師。

第叄場
策〔五道〕
問：自古帝王平治天下，必有要道以為之本，不徒以之淑其身，而又垂訓子孫，以為不易之法。盖嘗伏覩我太宗文皇帝御製《聖學心法》矣。其憂深，其慮遠，其所采皆聖賢之嘉言，信乎萬世聖子神孫保位修德之龜鑑也。然其綱有四，而不知以何者為之要；其目三十有一，而不知以何者為之先。鴻猷大旨之攸存，造端託始之深意，其可得而聞歟？學焉而果得其要，其於古帝王
translation_en:
Legal judgments 〔five items〕
An official exceeds the time limit for reporting to his post; children or grandchildren disobey instructions; a person of free status and a person of servile status marry; a junior family member privately uses family property without authorization; a pupil strikes the teacher under whom he studies.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔five questions〕
Question: Since ancient times, emperors and kings who have brought peace and order to the realm have necessarily taken an essential Way as their foundation. They have used it not merely to cultivate themselves, but also to transmit instructions to their descendants as an unchanging rule. We have reverently perused the Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), imperially composed by our Emperor Taizong Wen. His concerns were profound and his deliberations far-reaching; everything he selected consisted of excellent sayings of sages and worthies. Truly, it is a guide and mirror through which his sagely sons and divine descendants may preserve their throne and cultivate virtue for all generations. Yet it has four principal divisions, and we do not know which is the most essential; it has thirty-one topics, and we do not know which should come first. May we hear where its grand design and central purport lie, and the profound intention underlying its beginnings and foundations? If, by studying it, one truly grasps its essentials, then, in relation to the emperors and kings of antiquity …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之治亦可得而並歟然漢武好文學而
能為栢梁之詩元帝善史書而又能知
音律之妙與夫魏文之下筆成章明皇
之文譽自負皆今昔所共推以為知學
焉者是書悉棄弗取何歟將務其大而
小者固不可得而兼歟抑學得其要則
其小者不必事也儒先之論乃有謂帝
王之學與韋布不同者而又有謂與常
人同者何歟有勸其君正心由于好學
===
者而又有謂學亦有邪正之别者何歟
此我
祖宗貽謀之大人臣格心第一事也講之而不
豫辯之而不明而可乎故于諸士子大
比之秋敢首舉以為問其敬陳之母讓
問君子欲訥于言而亦有不得已者自孔
孟沒若董子于漢韓子于唐石徂徠歐
陽子于宋凡有所辯皆所以息邪距詖
闢異端以正人心也而我朱子則疑若
punctuated:
之治亦可得而並歟？然漢武好文學，而能為栢梁之詩；元帝善史書，而又能知音律之妙；與夫魏文之下筆成章、明皇之文譽自負，皆今昔所共推以為知學焉者。是書悉棄弗取，何歟？將務其大，而小者固不可得而兼歟？抑學得其要，則其小者不必事也？儒先之論，乃有謂帝王之學與韋布不同者，而又有謂與常人同者，何歟？有勸其君正心由于好學者，而又有謂學亦有邪正之别者，何歟？此我祖宗貽謀之大、人臣格心第一事也。講之而不豫，辯之而不明，而可乎？故于諸士子大比之秋，敢首舉以為問。其敬陳之，母讓。

問：君子欲訥于言，而亦有不得已者。自孔孟沒，若董子于漢、韓子于唐、石徂徠、歐陽子于宋，凡有所辯，皆所以息邪距詖、闢異端以正人心也。而我朱子則疑若
translation_en:
…could one also equal the governance of the ancient emperors and kings? Yet Emperor Wu of Han delighted in literature and could compose the Bailiang Terrace poem; Emperor Yuan was skilled in scribal writing and also understood the subtleties of musical pitches. Emperor Wen of Wei produced polished compositions as soon as he set brush to paper, and Emperor Minghuang of Tang prided himself on his literary reputation. All have been acclaimed, past and present, as men who understood learning. Why does this book exclude them all, taking nothing from them? Is it that, in attending to what is great, one cannot also encompass lesser things? Or, once one has grasped the essentials of learning, need one no longer concern oneself with its lesser aspects? Among the judgments of earlier Confucian scholars, some hold that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of men in plain cloth, while others hold that it is the same as that of ordinary people. Why is this? Some urged their rulers to rectify their minds through a love of learning, while others maintained that learning itself could be either deviant or correct. Why is this?

This is a matter of great importance in the plans our imperial ancestors bequeathed to posterity, and the foremost duty of a minister in rectifying his ruler’s mind. Can it be acceptable not to study it beforehand or to distinguish its principles clearly? Thus, in this autumn of the triennial examination for you candidates, I venture to raise it as the first question. Respectfully set forth your answers, without demur.

Question: The gentleman wishes to be restrained in speech, yet there are times when he cannot remain silent. Since Confucius and Mencius died, such men as Master Dong in the Han, Master Han in the Tang, and Shi Culai and Master Ouyang in the Song have undertaken their arguments to quell pernicious doctrines, resist misleading assertions, and refute heterodox teachings, thereby setting people’s minds right. Yet our Master Zhu seems as though…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有異焉者夫眉山二蘇氏横浦張無垢
東萊呂舍人與夫龍川之陳象山之陸
皆吾儒之傑然者其非異端比也明矣
然易解有辯老子解有辯中庸解有辯
大學解有辯漢唐堯舜三代之論治有
辯無極太極之論理有辯何其不憚煩
也豈好己之道勝乎將亦有不得已者
存乎然則其所謂不得已者果何謂乎
朱子之書今天下家傳而人誦之然徒
===
誦其言而不知其心則亦奚取於學為
也願舉其槩推其意以極論其所以不
得已者此大儒衞道之功與尋常無用
之辯者異是不可默矣
問昔賢用世之迹布在方策者衆矣姑舉
其一二大者論之同一為相也寛大好
禮不親細事者世以為知大體固也則
自校簿書者非歟同一為將也軍中夜
驚堅臥不起者世以為真將軍固也則
punctuated:
有異焉者。夫眉山二蘇氏、横浦張無垢、東萊呂舍人，與夫龍川之陳、象山之陸，皆吾儒之傑然者，其非異端比也明矣。然《易解》有辯，《老子解》有辯，《中庸解》有辯，《大學解》有辯，漢唐堯舜三代之論治有辯，無極太極之論理有辯，何其不憚煩也？豈好己之道勝乎？將亦有不得已者存乎？然則其所謂不得已者，果何謂乎？朱子之書，今天下家傳而人誦之，然徒誦其言而不知其心，則亦奚取於學為也？願舉其槩，推其意，以極論其所以不得已者。此大儒衞道之功，與尋常無用之辯者異，是不可默矣。

問：昔賢用世之迹，布在方策者衆矣。姑舉其一二大者論之。同一為相也，寛大好禮、不親細事者，世以為知大體，固也；則自校簿書者非歟？同一為將也，軍中夜驚、堅臥不起者，世以為真將軍，固也；則
translation_en:
…seems to have been different in this respect. The two Su masters of Meishan, Zhang Wugou of Hengpu, Secretariat Drafter Lü of Donglai, Chen of Longchuan, and Lu of Xiangshan were all outstanding figures among our Confucian scholars. Clearly, they cannot be classed with adherents of heterodox teachings. Yet Master Zhu disputed the Explanation of the Changes, the Explanation of the Laozi, the Explanation of the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Explanation of the Great Learning. He disputed discussions of government concerning the Han and Tang, Yao and Shun, and the Three Dynasties, and discussions of principle concerning the Limitless and the Supreme Ultimate. Why did he so little shrink from the trouble? Was it because he liked his own Way to prevail? Or were there also considerations that left him no choice? If so, what precisely were these compelling considerations? Today Master Zhu’s writings are handed down in households throughout the realm, and people recite them. But if they merely recite his words without understanding his mind, what benefit do they derive from learning? Please present the main outlines and explore his intentions, discussing fully why he could not refrain from these disputes. This great Confucian’s achievement in defending the Way differs from ordinary, useless disputation; it cannot be passed over in silence.

Question: Many accounts of worthy men of former times serving in public life are recorded in books. Let us select one or two major examples for discussion. Consider two men who both served as chief councilors. One was magnanimous, valued ritual propriety, and did not personally attend to minor matters. The world regarded him as understanding the larger concerns of government, and rightly so. Does that mean that the other, who personally checked registers and documents, was wrong? Consider two men who both served as generals. When a nighttime alarm arose in camp, one remained firmly in bed and did not rise. The world regarded him as a true general, and rightly so. Then …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
單騎見虜者非歟同一為世臣之胄也
羲皇上人恥事二姓節則高矣而韓亡
事漢自取萬户之封者不幾于忍歟同
一布衣之舊也白衣山人共濟艱難功
則偉矣而不拜諫議遂還富春之隱者
無乃大忘世歟同一科舉取士也或在
貞元時而名士畢收或在嘉祐時而名
士見黜其好惡不相反歟同一為執政
所引薦也或在神宗時而不就侍講或
===
在徽宗時而就祕書其趨向之異若此
何以謂其淵源之同歟或以請罷條例
司而去或以為條例司官而不去其在
熙寧之時同而行胡不同歟或起為門
下侍郎而拜或起為尚書僕射而不拜
其在元祐之時同而志胡不同歟或沮
王諸呂而杜門十年或潜授五龍而取
日虞淵其為大臣同而去就則不相似
也然則孰為得人臣之正歟或累召不
punctuated: 單騎見虜者非歟？同一為世臣之胄也，羲皇上人，恥事二姓，節則高矣，而韓亡事漢，自取萬户之封者，不幾于忍歟？同一布衣之舊也，白衣山人，共濟艱難，功則偉矣，而不拜諫議，遂還富春之隱者，無乃大忘世歟？同一科舉取士也，或在貞元時而名士畢收，或在嘉祐時而名士見黜，其好惡不相反歟？同一為執政所引薦也，或在神宗時而不就侍講，或在徽宗時而就祕書，其趨向之異若此，何以謂其淵源之同歟？或以請罷條例司而去，或以為條例司官而不去，其在熙寧之時同，而行胡不同歟？或起為門下侍郎而拜，或起為尚書僕射而不拜，其在元祐之時同，而志胡不同歟？或沮王諸呂而杜門十年，或潜授五龍而取日虞淵，其為大臣同，而去就則不相似也。然則孰為得人臣之正歟？或累召不
translation_en:
…was the one who rode alone to meet the enemy, then, in the wrong? Both were descendants of families that had served their rulers for generations. The one who styled himself a “man of the age of Fuxi” considered it shameful to serve two ruling houses: his integrity was indeed lofty. But the one who, after the fall of Han 韓, served Han 漢 and secured for himself a fief of ten thousand households—did he not verge on callousness? Both were old friends of their sovereigns from their days as commoners. The mountain recluse in a commoner’s white robes helped his sovereign through adversity: his achievements were indeed great. But the one who declined appointment as Remonstrance Grand Master and returned to seclusion at Fuchun—had he not forgotten the world altogether too much? Both examinations selected men for office. In the Zhenyuan era, all the celebrated scholars were taken in; in the Jiayou era, celebrated scholars were rejected. Were their preferences not opposed?

Both men were recommended by those directing the government. One, under Shenzong, declined appointment as Expositor; another, under Huizong, accepted a post in the Palace Library. With their inclinations differing so greatly, how can their intellectual origins be called the same? One left office after requesting the abolition of the Regulations Commission; another served as an official of that commission and did not leave. Both lived in the Xining era: why did their conduct differ? One was summoned to become Vice Director of the Chancellery and accepted; another was summoned to become Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and declined. Both lived in the Yuanyou era: why did their intentions differ?

One opposed making the members of the Lü clan kings and kept his doors shut for ten years; another secretly instructed the “five dragons” [?] and retrieved the sun from the depths of Yuyuan. Both were great ministers, yet their withdrawal and service were unlike. Which, then, fulfilled the proper duty of a subject? One, though repeatedly summoned, did not…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
起而隱居教授或聞召輒起而官為學
士其為名儒同而出處之異亦甚矣不
知以孔氏家法律之孰為近于道歟嗟
夫天下之事變無常而理則有定如此
而是則不如此而非如此而可則不如
此而否固未有不居一於此者若諸賢
者乃同為後世之所重何邪其固有優
劣高下之可議而不能同邪將時殊勢
異行於前者不可襲于後邪抑君子之
===
所為衆人固不識邪夫人必考乎古而
後能達諸今必明諸心而後能善其事
苟有經濟之心者必嘗擬議於斯矣願
明以告我
問為學必以孔孟為師語治必以唐虞為
的學固所以致其治也唐虞之治論者
謂以敬天勤民為首蓋能敬天則可成
格天之功能勤民則可致安民之績此
其治之盛所以不可及也然傲予之嘆
punctuated:
起而隱居教授，或聞召輒起而官為學士，其為名儒同，而出處之異亦甚矣。不知以孔氏家法律之，孰為近于道歟？嗟夫！天下之事變無常，而理則有定。如此而是，則不如此而非；如此而可，則不如此而否，固未有不居一於此者。若諸賢者，乃同為後世之所重，何邪？其固有優劣高下之可議而不能同邪？將時殊勢異，行於前者不可襲于後邪？抑君子之所為，衆人固不識邪？夫人必考乎古而後能達諸今，必明諸心而後能善其事。苟有經濟之心者，必嘗擬議於斯矣。願明以告我。

問：為學必以孔孟為師，語治必以唐虞為的。學固所以致其治也。唐虞之治，論者謂以敬天勤民為首。蓋能敬天，則可成格天之功；能勤民，則可致安民之績。此其治之盛所以不可及也。然傲予之嘆
translation_en:
…respond to the summons, but instead lived in retirement and taught; others rose to serve whenever summoned and held office as academicians. They were alike in being renowned Confucian scholars, yet differed greatly in their choices between service and retirement. Judged by the standards handed down in Kongzi’s school, which came closer to the Way? Alas! Affairs in the world change without constancy, yet principle is fixed. If acting thus is right, acting otherwise is wrong; if acting thus is acceptable, acting otherwise is not. Surely no case fails to fall on one side or the other. Why, then, have all these worthy men alike been esteemed by later generations? Were there indeed differences of merit and standing among them that admit of judgment, so that they cannot be ranked equally? Or did times and circumstances differ, making it impossible to follow in a later age the conduct of an earlier one? Or is the conduct of the gentleman simply beyond ordinary people’s understanding? One must examine antiquity before one can comprehend the present, and attain clarity in one’s own mind before one can handle affairs well. Anyone with an interest in ordering the state and bringing relief to the people must surely have reflected on these matters. Please explain them clearly to me.

Question: In learning, one must take Kongzi and Mengzi as teachers; in discussing government, one must take Tang and Yu—the reigns of Yao and Shun—as the standard. Learning is precisely the means of bringing about such government. Those who discuss the government of Tang and Yu say that revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people were its foremost concerns. For revering Heaven enables one to achieve the merit of moving Heaven, while diligently caring for the people enables one to accomplish the work of bringing them peace. This is why the excellence of their government cannot be equaled. Yet the lament, “He is arrogant toward me”…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
寔形於堯阻飢之憂乃聞于舜豈其道
至大雖聖人有所未能歟抑其治之不
可及者固在于此歟三代之時無容議
矣嗣是而後若不俟災異常畏上天之
鑒臨較之因歲飢荒始令捕蝗于山東
者德孰為盛當慶曆治平之日而聽納
不倦較之當導化經綸之時而日中不
食者事孰為難其恊心輔理之臣亦可
得而聞歟其於格天安民之道果能無
===
愧于古否歟夫嚴事鬼神固所以為敬
天也而商之賢臣則曰黷于祭祀時謂
弗欽何歟審若是則創太乙之祠飾天
書之詐者固非所以為敬矣彼漢室中
興之君乃有封禪之失其亦不知所以
為敬歟其臣亦有諫之者否歟躬親庶
政正所以為勤民也而周之元聖則曰
庶獄庶慎文王罔敢知何歟審若是則
衡石程書衛士傳餐者固非所以為勤
punctuated: 寔形於堯，阻飢之憂乃聞于舜。豈其道至大，雖聖人有所未能歟？抑其治之不可及者固在于此歟？三代之時，無容議矣。嗣是而後，若不俟災異，常畏上天之鑒臨，較之因歲飢荒始令捕蝗于山東者，德孰為盛？當慶曆治平之日而聽納不倦，較之當導化經綸之時而日中不食者，事孰為難？其恊心輔理之臣，亦可得而聞歟？其於格天安民之道，果能無愧于古否歟？夫嚴事鬼神，固所以為敬天也，而商之賢臣則曰：「黷于祭祀，時謂弗欽。」何歟？審若是，則創太乙之祠、飾天書之詐者，固非所以為敬矣。彼漢室中興之君，乃有封禪之失，其亦不知所以為敬歟？其臣亦有諫之者否歟？躬親庶政，正所以為勤民也，而周之元聖則曰：「庶獄庶慎，文王罔敢知。」何歟？審若是，則衡石程書、衛士傳餐者，固非所以為勤
translation_en:
…was indeed expressed by Yao, while concern over distress from hunger was heard from Shun. Was their Way so vast that even sages could not accomplish everything? Or was this very concern what made their government unsurpassable? The age of the Three Dynasties needs no discussion. Among those who followed, consider one who, without waiting for disasters or anomalies, constantly stood in awe of Heaven’s scrutiny. Compared with one who only ordered locusts caught in Shandong when famine struck, whose virtue was greater? To listen to and accept counsel tirelessly in the days of Qingli and Zhiping, or to go without food at midday while guiding moral transformation and ordering the realm—which task was harder? May we also hear about the ministers who assisted their government with united purpose? In their way of moving Heaven and bringing peace to the people, could they truly stand without shame before the ancients?

Surely reverent service to spirits is a means of respecting Heaven. Yet a worthy minister of the Shang said: “To profane sacrifices through excess is called irreverence.” Why? If this is indeed so, then founding a shrine to Taiyi and embellishing the fraud of the heavenly writings certainly did not constitute reverence. Yet the ruler who restored the Han dynasty committed the error of performing the feng and shan sacrifices. Did he too fail to understand how to show reverence? Were there any among his ministers who remonstrated with him?

Personally attending to the various affairs of government is precisely a means of diligent service to the people. Yet the great sage of Zhou said: “As for the many judicial cases and the many matters requiring care, King Wen did not presume to take personal cognizance of them.” Why? If this is indeed so, then setting a quota for documents by their weight and having guards pass in meals certainly did not constitute diligence…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣彼有宋勵精之主乃有新法之弊豈
亦不知所以為勤歟其臣亦有救之者
否歟若之何為敬天之要若之何為勤
民之方意者唐虞之世自有至論而彼
皆未之悉歟諸士子皆誦法孔孟者其
講唐虞也素矣盍罄所懷以著于篇執
事者願有聞也
問兵戎國之大事而將則三軍之司命又
治兵戎者之要也故曰無必勝之兵有
===
必勝之將然一技不遺而羣策並屈古
之人孰無是心哉顧求之任之有未易
者維師尚父時維鷹揚將惟其武者用
之歟則善戰無前者或譬之養虎舉邊
引去者或目之蒼鷹武而不義不可用
也詩書禮樂惟卻穀可亦惟其有文者
是用歟則作文賦者有河橋之敗負時
名者有陳濤之奔文而無實不可用也
無已則老而諳練者是求歟又恐其不
punctuated:
矣。彼有宋勵精之主，乃有新法之弊，豈亦不知所以為勤歟？其臣亦有救之者否歟？若之何為敬天之要？若之何為勤民之方？意者唐虞之世自有至論，而彼皆未之悉歟？諸士子皆誦法孔孟者，其講唐虞也素矣，盍罄所懷以著于篇？執事者願有聞也。
問：兵戎，國之大事，而將則三軍之司命，又治兵戎者之要也。故曰：「無必勝之兵，有必勝之將。」然一技不遺，而羣策並屈，古之人孰無是心哉？顧求之任之，有未易者。「維師尚父，時維鷹揚」，將惟其武者用之歟？則善戰無前者，或譬之養虎；舉邊引去者，或目之蒼鷹。武而不義，不可用也。「詩書禮樂，惟卻穀可」，亦惟其有文者是用歟？則作文賦者，有河橋之敗；負時名者，有陳濤之奔。文而無實，不可用也。無已，則老而諳練者是求歟？又恐其不
translation_en:
…indeed. Yet the energetic ruler of the Song brought about the abuses of the New Policies. Did he too not understand how to be diligent? Were there any among his ministers who sought to remedy this? What is essential to revering Heaven? What is the proper way to labor diligently for the people? Might the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun itself offer the definitive teaching, which these rulers failed fully to grasp? You candidates all recite and take as your models the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, and have long studied the age of Yao and Shun. Why not express all that you have in mind in writing? Those administering this examination would welcome hearing it.
Question: Warfare is a great affair of state, and the general holds the lives of the armies in his hands; selecting him is therefore also essential to the conduct of warfare. Thus it is said: “There is no army certain of victory, but there are generals certain of victory.” Yet what person of antiquity did not wish to overlook no single skill and to bring every counsel into service [?]? Nevertheless, finding and employing such men is no easy matter. “The Grand Preceptor Shangfu rose like an eagle.” Should generals, then, be employed solely for their martial prowess? Yet employing some whose skill in battle was unrivaled was likened to raising a tiger; another, who withdrew from the frontier [?], was called a goshawk. Those who possess martial prowess but lack righteousness cannot be employed. “For the Odes, Documents, rites, and music, only Xi Gu [?] will do.” Should only men of literary cultivation, then, be employed? Yet among writers of prose and rhapsodies was one defeated at Heqiao, and among those who enjoyed contemporary renown was one routed at Chentao. Those who possess literary cultivation but lack substance cannot be employed. Failing these, should one seek men who are old and experienced? Yet one fears that they may not…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
皆矍鑠翁而或有攻狄不下如魯仲連
所料者在也無已則少而英銳者是求
歟又恐其不皆淮陰少年而或有徒讀
父書如應侯所間者在也地產可求得
如辛趙者斯善矣然不有按圖索驥之
誚歟門望可求得如王謝者斯善矣然
不有肉食者鄙之譏歟福將之說興則
無以家為者怠矣安得遏其端而使素
餐者無出位之想歟債帥之途啓則憂
===
國奉公者沮矣安得絕其進而使饕餮
者無非分之請歟將欲捐爵賞如漢高
則恐其他日功多之難處將欲吝使相
如宋祖則恐其一時武事之不競將欲
專其任以委之則又有懲于藩鎮之跋
扈將欲分其權以制之則又有監于荀
林父之輿尸然則如之何而可邪儒者
於天下事無一非其所當為矧文事武
備宣聖之所不廢者試借一籌用為本
punctuated: 皆矍鑠翁，而或有攻狄不下，如魯仲連所料者在也。無已，則少而英銳者是求歟？又恐其不皆淮陰少年，而或有徒讀父書，如應侯所間者在也。地產可求，得如辛趙者斯善矣，然不有按圖索驥之誚歟？門望可求，得如王謝者斯善矣，然不有肉食者鄙之譏歟？福將之說興，則無以家為者怠矣，安得遏其端，而使素餐者無出位之想歟？債帥之途啓，則憂國奉公者沮矣，安得絕其進，而使饕餮者無非分之請歟？將欲捐爵賞如漢高，則恐其他日功多之難處；將欲吝使相如宋祖，則恐其一時武事之不競；將欲專其任以委之，則又有懲于藩鎮之跋扈；將欲分其權以制之，則又有監于荀林父之輿尸。然則如之何而可邪？儒者於天下事，無一非其所當為，矧文事武備，宣聖之所不廢者！試借一籌，用為本
translation_en:
…all be vigorous old men; among them there may be some who attack Di but cannot take it, just as Lu Zhonglian anticipated. If that will not do, should we seek men who are young, outstanding, and spirited? Yet we fear that they will not all be like the young man of Huaiyin: some may merely have read their fathers’ military books, like the man whose appointment the Marquis of Ying brought about through intrigue. We might seek men by their native region: finding men like Xin and Zhao would indeed be good. Yet would this not invite the reproach of seeking a fine horse by following a picture? We might seek men by their family standing: finding men like Wang and Xie would indeed be good. Yet would this not invite the criticism that “meat-eaters are shallow”? When the notion of the “fortunate general” gains currency, those who put aside establishing a household grow dispirited. How can we check this tendency at its source, so that those who draw stipends without service have no thought of reaching beyond their station? When the path opens for commanders who incur debts to purchase office, those who care for the state and serve the public are discouraged. How can we block their advancement, so that the rapacious make no requests beyond their due?

If we wish to bestow ranks and rewards freely, as Gaozu of Han did, we fear the difficulty of dealing with men whose achievements later become too great. If we wish to withhold appointments as military commissioners with concurrent grand councillor titles, as Taizu of Song did, we fear that military affairs may falter in the immediate term. If we wish to entrust a commander with sole responsibility, we are deterred by the overbearing conduct of the regional military governors. If we wish to divide his authority in order to control him, we have the warning of Xun Linfu’s defeat, with corpses borne home in carts. What, then, should be done?

Of all affairs under Heaven, none lies outside a Confucian scholar’s proper responsibilities. How much more is this true of civil affairs and military preparedness, neither of which the Illustrious Sage neglected! Offer a plan, then, for the use of those in charge…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text: 兵者毋徒曰軍旅之事未之學也
punctuated: 兵者，毋徒曰：「軍旅之事，未之學也。」
translation_en: …those in charge of military affairs. Do not merely say: “I have not studied matters of military campaigning.”

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百三十五名
第一名張璿直隸晉州學生書
第二名楊灝直隸易州學生易
