title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者樂水仁者樂山知者動仁者靜知者
樂仁者壽
楊灝
同考試官教諭王批題本揭書出最平易作之
多浮冗可厭此篇說理有序而語亦精潔夫子論知
者之事殆無餘蘊故錄之
同考試官教諭鄒批善會朱傳成文而措詞
===
精核論語義似此者絕少
考試官左諭德靳批詞不繁而意足非𠅘作可到
考試官學士江批體認親切可嘉
聖人指知仁者之情有不同必原其體而著其
效也夫樂水樂山知仁者之情則異矣非聖人
原其體而著其效焉抑孰知其然哉吾想其意
若曰人之成德不無知與仁之殊則情之所樂
自有水與山之異是故水之為物流行而不息
者也孰不見之而惟知者之喜好則在於水焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「知者樂水，仁者樂山；知者動，仁者靜；知者樂，仁者壽。」

楊灝

同考試官教諭王批：「題本揭書出，最平易，作之多浮冗可厭。此篇說理有序，而語亦精潔，夫子論知者之事，殆無餘蘊，故錄之。」

同考試官教諭鄒批：「善會朱傳成文，而措詞精核，論語義似此者絕少。」

考試官左諭德靳批：「詞不繁而意足，非𠅘作可到。」

考試官學士江批：「體認親切，可嘉。」

聖人指知仁者之情有不同，必原其體而著其效也。夫樂水樂山，知仁者之情則異矣。非聖人原其體而著其效焉，抑孰知其然哉？吾想其意若曰：人之成德，不無知與仁之殊，則情之所樂，自有水與山之異。是故水之為物，流行而不息者也。孰不見之？而惟知者之喜好，則在於水焉。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The wise delight in water; the benevolent delight in mountains. The wise are active; the benevolent are still. The wise are joyful; the benevolent are long-lived.”

Yang Hao

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The topic is taken directly from the book [?] and is thoroughly straightforward, yet treatments of it are often tiresomely superficial and prolix. This essay expounds the principles in an orderly way, and its language is precise and clean. It leaves virtually nothing unexplored in the Master’s discussion of the wise. Hence its inclusion.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: “It skillfully assimilates Zhu Xi’s commentary into an essay, with precise and carefully considered wording. Essays on the meaning of the Analects like this are exceedingly rare.”

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Mentor: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning is complete. This is beyond the reach of an ordinary composition [?].”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: “Its intimate grasp of the subject deserves praise.”

When the Sage points out that the dispositions of the wise and the benevolent differ, he must trace their underlying constitutions and make their effects manifest. In delighting in water and delighting in mountains, the dispositions of the wise and the benevolent indeed differ. Unless the Sage traced their underlying constitutions and made their effects manifest, who could understand why this is so? I imagine his meaning to be as follows: In the perfected virtue of human beings, there are distinctions between wisdom and benevolence; thus, in what their dispositions delight in, there is naturally a distinction between water and mountains. Now water is a thing that flows without ceasing. Who does not see it? Yet it is specifically the wise whose delight is in water. …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
山之為物鎮定而不移者也孰不瞻之而惟仁
者之喜好則在於山焉是何也知者是非之心
具而私欲不足以蔽之達於事理而周流無滯
其體則本動也動故有似於水其樂水也非以
是耶仁者本心之德全而外物不足以擾之安
於義理而厚重不遷其體則本靜也靜故有似
於山其樂山也不以此耶然知者惟其動也吾
見事至而能處物來而能應從容自得所謂心
廣體胖者在是矣有弗樂乎仁者惟其靜也吾
===
見志氣自爾其凝定精神自爾其純一常永貞
固所謂黄髮台背者在是矣有弗壽乎噫知者
非不知靜也而動其體也仁者非不能動也而
靜其體也人品既殊則其所樂之情異而效亦
因之一自然之理耳宜吾夫子形容之以為萬
世學者告歟雖然此特為知仁各得其一偏者
論耳若夫聖人則異於是天性渾全陰陽合德
兼動靜而一以貫之又何有於二者之别乎觀
其川上之嘆泰山之登亦可以驗之矣然則夫
punctuated: 山之為物，鎮定而不移者也，孰不瞻之？而惟仁者之喜好則在於山焉。是何也？知者是非之心具，而私欲不足以蔽之，達於事理而周流無滯，其體則本動也。動故有似於水，其樂水也，非以是耶？仁者本心之德全，而外物不足以擾之，安於義理而厚重不遷，其體則本靜也。靜故有似於山，其樂山也，不以此耶？然知者惟其動也，吾見事至而能處，物來而能應，從容自得，所謂心廣體胖者在是矣，有弗樂乎？仁者惟其靜也，吾見志氣自爾其凝定，精神自爾其純一，常永貞固，所謂黄髮台背者在是矣，有弗壽乎？噫！知者非不知靜也，而動其體也；仁者非不能動也，而靜其體也。人品既殊，則其所樂之情異，而效亦因之，一自然之理耳。宜吾夫子形容之，以為萬世學者告歟！雖然，此特為知仁各得其一偏者論耳。若夫聖人，則異於是，天性渾全，陰陽合德，兼動靜而一以貫之，又何有於二者之别乎？觀其川上之嘆、泰山之登，亦可以驗之矣。然則夫
translation_en:
… Mountains, by their nature, stand firm and unmoving. Who does not behold them? Yet it is the benevolent who take particular delight in mountains. Why is this? The wise possess fully the mind that distinguishes right from wrong, and selfish desires cannot obscure it. They comprehend the principles of affairs and move freely through them without obstruction; their fundamental constitution is thus active. Being active, they resemble water. Is this not why they delight in water? The benevolent possess the virtue of their original mind in its completeness, and external things cannot disturb it. They rest content in moral principles, remaining steadfast and substantial; their fundamental constitution is thus still. Being still, they resemble mountains. Is this not why they delight in mountains?

Now, precisely because the wise are active, I see that they can deal with affairs as they arise and respond to things as they come, remaining at ease and self-possessed. Here is what is meant by “the mind is expansive and the body at ease.” Could they fail to be joyful? Precisely because the benevolent are still, I see that their resolve and vital energies naturally become settled and their spirit naturally becomes pure and undivided, enduring in constancy and firmness. Here is what is meant by “yellow hair and a mottled back,” the signs of advanced age. Could they fail to be long-lived?

Ah! It is not that the wise do not understand stillness, but activity is their fundamental constitution. It is not that the benevolent cannot act, but stillness is their fundamental constitution. Since their personal qualities differ, their feelings concerning what delights them differ, and the effects follow accordingly: this is simply a principle of nature [?]. How fitting that our Master described this to instruct learners for all generations!

Nevertheless, this discussion concerns only those who have attained either wisdom or benevolence as a partial accomplishment. The sage is different. His Heaven-endowed nature is complete and undivided; in him, yin and yang unite their virtues. He embraces both activity and stillness, with a single principle running through them. What distinction between the two could remain? This can also be verified by considering his sigh beside the river and his ascent of Mount Tai. Then …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
于斯言其亦所謂自道者歟
故君子尊德性而道問學
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批中庸一題講存心致知處士
子類能為之然細玩其詞冗雜可厭獨此作認理真
切而語亦工緻必甞用心於性理之學者敬羨
同考試官教授王批此題不難於遣詞而難於
認理豈溺于記誦之習故耶獨此作理致深長而文亦明暢
允宜錄出
===
考試官左諭德靳批似非尋常事記誦者
考試官學士江批一結尤見學識
凝道者有存心之功有致知之功蓋尊德性所
以存心而道問學所以致知也君子於此而兼
盡其功則聖道烏有不凝者哉中庸二十七章
發明誠之者之事示人以脩德凝道之大端如
此誠以聖人之道其大無外其小無內而非至
德莫之凝也則君子存心致知之功可偏廢耶
是故德性者吾所受於天之正理也不有以尊
punctuated:
于斯言，其亦所謂自道者歟？

故君子尊德性而道問學。
張璿

同考試官教諭姜批：中庸一題，講存心致知處，士子類能為之。然細玩其詞，冗雜可厭。獨此作認理真切，而語亦工緻，必甞用心於性理之學者，敬羨。

同考試官教授王批：此題不難於遣詞，而難於認理，豈溺于記誦之習故耶？獨此作理致深長，而文亦明暢，允宜錄出。

考試官左諭德靳批：似非尋常事記誦者。

考試官學士江批：一結尤見學識。

凝道者，有存心之功，有致知之功。蓋尊德性所以存心，而道問學所以致知也。君子於此而兼盡其功，則聖道烏有不凝者哉？中庸二十七章，發明誠之者之事，示人以脩德凝道之大端如此。誠以聖人之道，其大無外，其小無內，而非至德莫之凝也，則君子存心致知之功可偏廢耶？是故德性者，吾所受於天之正理也。不有以尊
translation_en:
…in these words, was he not also, as the saying goes, describing himself?

“Therefore the gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning.”
Zhang Xuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: On this topic from the Doctrine of the Mean, candidates generally can discuss preserving the mind and extending knowledge. Yet close examination of their wording reveals tiresome verbosity and clutter. This composition alone grasps principle truly and precisely, and its language is also polished and meticulous. Its author must have devoted himself to the study of human nature and principle. I admire him respectfully.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: The difficulty of this topic lies not in choosing words but in grasping principle. Could this be because candidates are mired in habits of memorization and recitation? This composition alone conveys profound and far-reaching understanding of principle, while its prose is clear and fluent. It certainly deserves to be transcribed for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Mentor: The author seems no ordinary practitioner of memorization and recitation.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: The conclusion especially reveals his learning and understanding.

To bring the Way to full realization requires the effort of preserving the mind and the effort of extending knowledge. Honoring one’s moral nature is the means of preserving the mind, while pursuing inquiry and learning is the means of extending knowledge. If the gentleman fully applies himself to both, how could the Way of the sages fail to be realized? Chapter Twenty-Seven of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the work of those who strive to become sincere, thus showing people the essential means of cultivating virtue and realizing the Way. Indeed, the Way of the sages is so great that nothing lies outside it and so minute that nothing lies within it; yet without the highest virtue, no one can bring it to realization. Can the gentleman, then, neglect either the effort of preserving the mind or that of extending knowledge?

Thus moral nature is the correct principle that we receive from Heaven. Unless we find the means to honor…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之則何以存此心之本然而極道體之大乎必
也戒慎不覩恒如天監之在茲恐懼不聞常若
上帝之臨汝服膺之心拳拳焉使吾之得於天
者操于端莊靜一之中而私意不得以穢之也
欽崇之意翼翼焉使天之命于我者保于整齊
嚴肅之內而人欲不得以污之也夫然則此心
無不存而所以極道體之大者于是矣至若問
學者吾所適於道之正路也不有以由之則何
以窮衆理之當然而盡道體之細乎必也朝益
===
暮習或求之文字之中或索之講論之際不敢
挾已見以自是日就月將或考之事為之著或
察之念慮之微不敢矜一得以自足弗問則已
問之弗知弗措焉弗學則已學之弗能弗措焉
夫然則其知無不致而所以盡道體之細者在
是矣是則不知存心則昏昧雜擾固無以為致
知之本不知致知則偏狹固滯亦無以盡此心
之全二者交修入德之方莫切于此然則君子
由人而天此其權輿也歟雖然自精一之論發
punctuated: 之，則何以存此心之本然而極道體之大乎？必也戒慎不覩，恒如天監之在茲；恐懼不聞，常若上帝之臨汝。服膺之心拳拳焉，使吾之得於天者操于端莊靜一之中，而私意不得以穢之也；欽崇之意翼翼焉，使天之命于我者保于整齊嚴肅之內，而人欲不得以污之也。夫然，則此心無不存，而所以極道體之大者于是矣。至若問學者，吾所適於道之正路也。不有以由之，則何以窮衆理之當然而盡道體之細乎？必也朝益暮習，或求之文字之中，或索之講論之際，不敢挾已見以自是；日就月將，或考之事為之著，或察之念慮之微，不敢矜一得以自足。弗問則已，問之弗知弗措焉；弗學則已，學之弗能弗措焉。夫然，則其知無不致，而所以盡道體之細者在是矣。是則不知存心，則昏昧雜擾，固無以為致知之本；不知致知，則偏狹固滯，亦無以盡此心之全。二者交修，入德之方莫切于此。然則君子由人而天，此其權輿也歟？雖然，自精一之論發
translation_en:
…it, how could one preserve this mind in its original condition and fully realize the vastness of the substance of the Way? One must be watchful and cautious over what is unseen, always as though Heaven were watching here, and apprehensive over what is unheard, always as though the Lord on High were overlooking you. With a heart earnestly devoted to holding fast to it, one must maintain what one has received from Heaven amid dignity, stillness, and singleness of purpose, so that selfish intentions cannot defile it. With an attitude of vigilant reverence, one must preserve what Heaven has ordained within oneself amid orderliness and solemnity, so that human desires cannot sully it. Thus this mind will be preserved in every respect, and herein lies the means of fully realizing the vastness of the substance of the Way.
As for inquiry and learning, these are the proper path by which we approach the Way. Unless one follows it, how can one exhaustively investigate what is right in all principles and comprehend the finest details of the substance of the Way? One must increase one's learning in the morning and practice it in the evening, seeking sometimes in written texts and sometimes through discussion, never presuming that one's own views [?] are correct. One must advance daily and progress monthly, sometimes examining what is manifest in actions and affairs, sometimes scrutinizing the subtleties of thoughts and deliberations, never boasting of a single insight and resting content with it. If one does not inquire, so be it; but once one inquires, one must not stop until one understands. If one does not learn, so be it; but once one learns, one must not stop until one is capable. Thus one's knowledge will be extended in every respect, and herein lies the means of comprehending the finest details of the substance of the Way.
Hence, if one does not know how to preserve the mind, one remains benighted, confused, and distracted, and certainly has no foundation for extending knowledge. If one does not know how to extend knowledge, one remains narrow, rigid, and obstructed, and likewise cannot fully realize the wholeness of this mind. These two must be cultivated together: no method of entering into virtue is more essential than this. Is this, then, not the starting point from which the gentleman advances from the human to the heavenly? Nevertheless, ever since the teaching of refinement and singleness of purpose was first set forth…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
于虞廷聖賢世守以為心法未有易者子思乃
復以此言何耶蓋人之所以為學心與理而已
故必心之存知之至而后可以力行此二者所
以當先盡也不然世之以頓悟為高者何以入
於禪以記誦為業者何以流於俗而聖道終於
不續耶程子曰涵養須用敬進學則在致知噫
程子斯言出而子思之學復明矣
其君用之則安富尊榮其子弟從之則孝
弟忠信
===
王用賢
同考試官訓導周 批 此題多以窮達立說殊失
孟子本意且不拘則泛令人厭觀晚得此卷理到詞豐
讀之竦然蓋亦能學素食之詩者歟
同考試官訓導李 批 作者儘多但講涉支離
蔓語細加檢閱與孟子答公孫丑意不甚相對惟此篇
平實典重宜在所取
同考試官教諭林 批 題本冠冕場中士子類
能遺詞但安富尊榮泛講不切似非孟子意此作專
punctuated:
于虞廷，聖賢世守以為心法，未有易者。子思乃復以此言，何耶？蓋人之所以為學，心與理而已。故必心之存、知之至，而后可以力行，此二者所以當先盡也。不然，世之以頓悟為高者，何以入於禪？以記誦為業者，何以流於俗，而聖道終於不續耶？程子曰：「涵養須用敬，進學則在致知。」噫！程子斯言出，而子思之學復明矣。

其君用之則安富尊榮，其子弟從之則孝弟忠信。

王用賢

同考試官訓導周批：此題多以窮達立說，殊失孟子本意。且不拘則泛，令人厭觀。晚得此卷，理到詞豐，讀之竦然。蓋亦能學素食之詩者歟？

同考試官訓導李批：作者儘多，但講涉支離蔓語，細加檢閱，與孟子答公孫丑意不甚相對。惟此篇平實典重，宜在所取。

同考試官教諭林批：題本冠冕，場中士子類能遺詞，但安富尊榮泛講不切，似非孟子意。此作專
translation_en:
…at the court of Yu, sages and worthies have preserved it generation after generation as the teaching of the mind, never altering it. Why, then, did Zisi express it again in these words? What learning concerns is simply the mind and principle. Thus, only after preserving the mind and bringing knowledge to its fullest extent can one vigorously put learning into practice. This is why these two tasks must first be fully accomplished. Otherwise, why do those who esteem sudden enlightenment fall into Chan Buddhism, while those who make memorization and recitation their occupation drift into vulgar learning, leaving the Way of the sages without successors? Master Cheng said: “Cultivation requires reverence; advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.” Ah! With these words of Master Cheng, Zisi’s teaching became clear once more.

“When their ruler employs them, there is peace, wealth, dignity, and glory; when his sons and younger brothers follow them, there is filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness.”

Wang Yongxian 王用賢

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor: Most treatments of this topic frame their arguments around adversity and success, departing markedly from Mencius’s original intention. Moreover, they are either constricted or vague, making them tiresome to read. Late in the process I obtained this script: its reasoning is penetrating and its language abundant. Reading it stirred me deeply. Might its author also be one who has learned the lesson of the ode about not eating unearned food?

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: There are very many essays on this topic, but their explanations tend toward disjointed and rambling language. On close examination, they do not correspond very well to the intention of Mencius’s reply to Gongsun Chou. This essay alone is straightforward and substantial, dignified and weighty; it deserves selection.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The topic itself is grand and dignified, and candidates in the examination generally manage to compose their wording [?]. Yet their discussions of peace, wealth, dignity, and glory are vague and fail to address the point; they seem not to capture Mencius’s intention. This essay concentrates specifically on…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
就一國上發揮而婉轉委曲絶無滲漏獨步一場者也
考試官左諭德靳批說君子有功人國語極警策
考試官學士江批詞無長語似是老筆
道行于國君而治效隆道明于國人而風俗美
甚矣國不可以無君子也治隆于上而俗美于
下君子之功何如哉宜孟子以是闢公孫丑素
餐之問也請申言之君子負知言養氣之學蘊
輔世長民之具其居于人國也豈徒然哉上焉
而有君也誠使為君者好善忘勢而禮貌之必
===
恭諫行言聽而信任之不貳與之共天位也與
之治天民也則庶政明於間暇之時多福集於
朝堂之上保國家如岡陵而運祚靈長使菽粟
如水火而用度充足其安富何如也天與人歸
享祿位于崇高大畏小懷保聲名之洋溢其尊
榮何如也若是者非君子孰致之乎所謂道行
于國君而治效隆者以此下焉而有子弟也誠
使為子弟者矜而式之資吾所以明善者以淑
其身則而象之資吾所以誠身者以進其心中
punctuated:
就一國上發揮，而婉轉委曲，絶無滲漏，獨步一場者也。
考試官左諭德靳批：說君子有功人國，語極警策。
考試官學士江批：詞無長語，似是老筆。
道行于國君而治效隆，道明于國人而風俗美。甚矣，國不可以無君子也！治隆于上而俗美于下，君子之功何如哉！宜孟子以是闢公孫丑素餐之問也。請申言之。君子負知言養氣之學，蘊輔世長民之具，其居于人國也，豈徒然哉？上焉而有君也，誠使為君者好善忘勢，而禮貌之必恭，諫行言聽，而信任之不貳，與之共天位也，與之治天民也，則庶政明於間暇之時，多福集於朝堂之上，保國家如岡陵而運祚靈長，使菽粟如水火而用度充足，其安富何如也！天與人歸，享祿位于崇高；大畏小懷，保聲名之洋溢，其尊榮何如也！若是者，非君子孰致之乎？所謂道行于國君而治效隆者，以此。下焉而有子弟也，誠使為子弟者矜而式之，資吾所以明善者以淑其身，則而象之，資吾所以誠身者以進其心；中
translation_en:
…develops the argument specifically in relation to a single state, treating it with subtlety and thoroughness, leaving absolutely no gaps. It stands unrivaled in this examination.
Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher, comments: The account of how the gentleman benefits a state is expressed in exceptionally incisive language.
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: There is no wordiness in the composition; it seems the work of a seasoned writer.
When the Way is practiced by a state's ruler, the achievements of government flourish; when the Way is made clear to its people, their customs become fine. How profoundly a state depends on having gentlemen! Government flourishes above and customs become fine below: how great is the gentleman's contribution! It was fitting that Mengzi used this to rebut Gongsun Chou's question about eating without earning one's keep. Allow me to elaborate. The gentleman possesses the learning of understanding words and nurturing vital energy, and holds within himself the capacity to assist the age and lead the people. Can his presence in a state be without purpose?
Above, there is the ruler. If the ruler truly loves goodness and forgets his own power, invariably treats the gentleman with reverent courtesy, acts on his remonstrances and listens to his words, trusts him without wavering, shares with him the position bestowed by Heaven, and joins with him in governing Heaven's people, then the many affairs of government will be well ordered even in times of leisure, and manifold blessings will gather at court. The state will be secured like the hills, its allotted reign enduring; beans and grain will be as plentiful as water and fire, and resources will suffice for expenditure. How great its security and wealth will be! Heaven will grant its favor and the people will turn to it; the ruler will enjoy emoluments and exalted rank. Great states will fear him and small states cherish him, and his reputation will remain far-reaching. How great his dignity and glory will be! Who but the gentleman could bring this about? This is what is meant by saying that when the Way is practiced by a state's ruler, the achievements of government flourish.
Below, there are the sons and younger brothers. If they truly honor the gentleman and take him as their model, drawing upon that by which he understands goodness to improve themselves, and follow and emulate him, drawing upon that by which he makes himself sincere to advance their own hearts, then those who are upright…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
以養其不中也才以養其不才也則舊染化于
薫陶之餘善行得于觀感之下共為子職而道
路無負戴之勞克念天顯而門墻無鬩閱之事
孝弟之行成矣發己自盡而事上之不欺循物
無違而乆要之不忘忠信之化興矣若是者非
君子孰導之乎所謂道明于國人而風俗美者
以此噫上焉而隆治效于君下焉而美風俗于
民君子之功大矣公孫丑乃以素餐疑之不亦
異乎雖然君子之所為衆人固不識也如孟子
===
在戰國時雖名實未加于上下然闢楊墨以閑
先聖之道陳仁義以勸齊梁之君所謂其功不
在禹下者固非阿其所好而云也柰何一時君
臣既不能知而公孫丑彭更之徒親受其業者
亦不能無疑焉世道至此其亦可慨也夫
易
謙亨君子有終
錢宏
同考試官教諭鄒 批 謙卦一題經生治之素熟
punctuated:
以養其不中也，才以養其不才也，則舊染化于薫陶之餘，善行得于觀感之下。共為子職，而道路無負戴之勞；克念天顯，而門墻無鬩閱之事。孝弟之行成矣。發己自盡，而事上之不欺；循物無違，而乆要之不忘。忠信之化興矣。若是者，非君子孰導之乎？所謂道明于國人而風俗美者，以此。噫！上焉而隆治效于君，下焉而美風俗于民，君子之功大矣。公孫丑乃以素餐疑之，不亦異乎？雖然，君子之所為，衆人固不識也。如孟子在戰國時，雖名實未加于上下，然闢楊墨以閑先聖之道，陳仁義以勸齊梁之君，所謂其功不在禹下者，固非阿其所好而云也。柰何一時君臣既不能知，而公孫丑、彭更之徒，親受其業者，亦不能無疑焉。世道至此，其亦可慨也夫！
《易》
謙，亨，君子有終。
錢宏
同考試官教諭鄒批：謙卦一題，經生治之素熟。
translation_en:
…to nurture those who lack moral balance, and use their ability to nurture those who lack ability. Then old, ingrained faults are transformed through their formative influence, and good conduct is acquired through observation and inspiration. All fulfill their duties as sons, so that their elders need not toil along the roads carrying burdens on their backs or heads; they conscientiously heed Heaven’s manifest principles, so that there are no household quarrels [?]. Thus filial and fraternal conduct is established. They give fully of themselves, serving their superiors without deceit; they act in accordance with things without deviation, never forgetting longstanding commitments. Thus the transforming influence of loyalty and trustworthiness flourishes. Who but the gentleman could guide them to this? This is what is meant by the Way becoming clear to the people of the state and customs becoming good. Ah! Above, he enhances the ruler’s achievements in government; below, he improves the people’s customs. Great indeed is the gentleman’s contribution! Yet Gongsun Chou suspected him of eating without earning his keep. Is this not strange? Even so, ordinary people certainly do not understand what the gentleman does. Take Mengzi in the Warring States period: although his reputation and accomplishments had not yet made themselves felt among those above and below, he refuted the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di to defend the Way of the former sages, and expounded benevolence and righteousness to exhort the rulers of Qi and Liang. The statement that his contribution was no less than Yu’s was certainly not made merely to flatter someone one admired. How was it that not only the rulers and ministers of his time failed to understand him, but even Gongsun Chou, Peng Geng, and others who personally received his teaching could not remain free of doubts? That the ways of the world had come to this is indeed lamentable!

Book of Changes
“Modesty brings success. The gentleman carries it through to the end.”
Qian Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: Students of the Classics have long been thoroughly familiar with treating this topic on the hexagram Modesty…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然下筆多欠發揮甚或輕重不知惟此作善形容謙
意而尤說出君子之行深得聖人之旨可佳
同考試官教諭王批謙易中最吉之卦本義
明甚作者不泛則略且於卦德象處全無發揮簡切可誦
僅見此篇
考試官左諭德靳批作易義者不當如是邪
考試官學士江批講謙亨處甚快人意
前聖以不居其有之義名夫卦後聖以不居其
有之善著其占盖謙者不居其有之義非君子
===
不能也其致亨而有終也宜哉前聖後聖以是
名卦繫辭厥旨精矣且伏羲以下艮上坤之卦
名之曰謙其意以為人之善不一而惟謙為至
人之行不一而惟謙為難此卦之德內焉艮也
其德則止外焉坤也其德則順止乎內而順乎
外則是內有易簡過人之實而外有巽順下人
之恭有德不德非謙之意歟此卦之象下焉艮
也其象為山上焉坤也其象為地山在下而地
在上則是屈艮山至高之體而處於坤地至卑
punctuated:
然下筆多欠發揮，甚或輕重不知。惟此作善形容謙意，而尤說出君子之行，深得聖人之旨，可佳。
同考試官教諭王批：謙，易中最吉之卦，本義明甚。作者不泛則略，且於卦德象處全無發揮。簡切可誦，僅見此篇。
考試官左諭德靳批：作易義者，不當如是邪？
考試官學士江批：講謙亨處，甚快人意。
前聖以不居其有之義名夫卦，後聖以不居其有之善著其占。盖謙者，不居其有之義，非君子不能也。其致亨而有終也，宜哉！前聖後聖以是名卦繫辭，厥旨精矣。且伏羲以下艮上坤之卦，名之曰謙，其意以為人之善不一，而惟謙為至；人之行不一，而惟謙為難。此卦之德，內焉艮也，其德則止；外焉坤也，其德則順。止乎內而順乎外，則是內有易簡過人之實，而外有巽順下人之恭。有德不德，非謙之意歟？此卦之象，下焉艮也，其象為山；上焉坤也，其象為地。山在下而地在上，則是屈艮山至高之體，而處於坤地至卑
translation_en:
… Yet when candidates put brush to paper, they often fail to develop its meaning; some do not even distinguish what is important from what is secondary. This essay alone aptly portrays the meaning of modesty and, especially, brings out the conduct of the gentleman. It deeply grasps the sage’s intent and deserves praise.
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: Qian (Modesty) is the most auspicious hexagram in the Book of Changes, and its fundamental meaning is very clear. Writers are either vague or cursory, and offer no elaboration at all on the hexagram’s virtues and images. For concision and aptness, worthy of recitation, I have seen only this essay.
Examiner Jin, Left Mentor, comments: Should not those composing essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes write like this?
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: The explanation of how modesty brings success is thoroughly satisfying.
The earlier sage named this hexagram according to the principle of not claiming credit for what one possesses; the later sage set forth its prognostication according to the goodness of not claiming credit for what one possesses. Modesty means not claiming credit for what one possesses, and only a gentleman can accomplish this. How fitting that it should bring success and a worthy conclusion! The earlier and later sages used this principle to name the hexagram and append its statement: profound indeed was their intent.
Now Fuxi named the hexagram with Gen below and Kun above Qian, or Modesty. His meaning was that human excellences are many, but modesty is supreme; human practices are many, but modesty is difficult. As for this hexagram’s virtues, its inner trigram is Gen, whose virtue is stillness; its outer trigram is Kun, whose virtue is compliance. Stillness within and compliance without mean that inwardly one possesses a substance of ease and simplicity surpassing others, while outwardly one displays the deference and compliance of humbly placing oneself below others. To possess virtue without making a virtue of it—is this not the meaning of modesty?
As for this hexagram’s images, its lower trigram is Gen, whose image is the mountain; its upper trigram is Kun, whose image is the earth. The mountain below and the earth above signify bending down the supremely lofty form of Gen’s mountain and placing it beneath the utmost lowliness of Kun’s earth …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之下以卑蘊高非謙之象歟伏羲以謙名卦者
如此文王繫其辭以為人有能謙之德必有能
謙之效占者慎斯術也以往出乎身而加乎民
何適不通發乎邇而見乎遠何行不達以之居
卑自无壯趾之困也履道其坦矣以之居尊自
无夬履之厲也天衢其亨矣敦若無若虛之心
以自持始雖晦矣然實愈大而聲愈宏謙謙君
子終必致譽命而有慶不期其顯而自顯也操
不矜不伐之意以自考始雖屈矣然位愈尊而
===
德愈光謙謙君子終必縻好爵于无疆不期其
伸而自伸也文王以亨以有終著其效而必以
君子賛之者開物成務之意切矣占者可不知
所務哉抑論易諸卦之占未有善于謙者聖人
何取於是哉太極中本無一物謙固人所當為
而非君子則亦莫之為也觀夫克讓者堯温恭
者舜以天下至聖而賛其德者不能外焉則謙
之為道可易視哉雖然行之以誠而自得者君
子之謙也行之以偽而有所造作者老氏之術
punctuated: 之下，以卑蘊高，非謙之象歟？伏羲以謙名卦者如此。文王繫其辭，以為人有能謙之德，必有能謙之效。占者慎斯術也以往，出乎身而加乎民，何適不通？發乎邇而見乎遠，何行不達？以之居卑，自无壯趾之困也，履道其坦矣；以之居尊，自无夬履之厲也，天衢其亨矣。敦若無若虛之心以自持，始雖晦矣，然實愈大而聲愈宏，謙謙君子終必致譽命而有慶，不期其顯而自顯也。操不矜不伐之意以自考，始雖屈矣，然位愈尊而德愈光，謙謙君子終必縻好爵于无疆，不期其伸而自伸也。文王以亨、以有終著其效，而必以君子賛之者，開物成務之意切矣。占者可不知所務哉？抑論易諸卦之占，未有善于謙者，聖人何取於是哉？太極中本無一物，謙固人所當為，而非君子則亦莫之為也。觀夫克讓者堯，温恭者舜，以天下至聖而賛其德者不能外焉，則謙之為道可易視哉？雖然，行之以誠而自得者，君子之謙也；行之以偽而有所造作者，老氏之術
translation_en:
…beneath it: to contain the lofty within the lowly—is this not the image of Modesty? Such was Fuxi’s meaning in naming the hexagram Modesty. King Wen appended its statement, holding that anyone possessing the virtue of practicing modesty must obtain the results of practicing modesty. If the diviner proceeds with careful adherence to this way, extending it from himself to the people, where could he go without finding passage? If it issues from what is near and becomes manifest afar, what undertaking could fail to reach its goal? Through it, one occupying a lowly position will naturally escape the predicament of being “powerful in the toes”; the path he treads will be level. Through it, one occupying an exalted position will naturally escape the peril of “resolute treading”; the highway of Heaven will lie open to him.

By cultivating a heart that regards itself as having nothing and being empty, and thereby maintaining his conduct, he may at first remain obscure. Yet his substance grows ever greater and his reputation ever more resounding. The modest, modest gentleman must in the end receive praise and appointment, and enjoy blessings: without expecting prominence, he naturally becomes prominent. By holding fast to the resolve neither to presume upon himself nor to boast, and thereby examining himself, he may at first remain constrained. Yet his position becomes ever more exalted and his virtue ever more radiant. The modest, modest gentleman must in the end be granted fine emoluments without limit: without expecting advancement, he naturally advances. King Wen made its results clear through the words “success” and “having an end,” yet insisted on commending it in terms of the gentleman. His concern to disclose the nature of things and bring affairs to completion was indeed earnest. Can the diviner fail to understand what he should strive for?

Now, among the prognostications of all the hexagrams in the Changes, none is better than that of Modesty. What did the sages value in it? Within the Supreme Ultimate there is originally not a single thing. Modesty is certainly what people ought to practice, yet none but a gentleman can practice it. Consider Yao, who was capable of yielding, and Shun, who was gentle and reverent. They were the greatest sages in the world, yet those praising their virtue could not go beyond these qualities. Can the way of modesty, then, be regarded lightly? Nevertheless, practicing it sincerely and attaining it within oneself is the modesty of the gentleman; practicing it falsely, with deliberate contrivance, is the technique of Laozi…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
似德而非德也謙云乎哉一誠偽之間而理欲
判焉學易者不可不辨
乾天也故稱乎父坤地也故稱乎母
金𤇍
同考試官教諭鄒批此作本後天圖學發明
聖人所以稱二老之故明白簡要宜錄之以示經生之不讀
啓蒙者
同考試官教諭王批此題於乾坤父母處類能
言之而不知其義者多惟此本圖學發明其言有據蓋
===
熟於本領者
考試官左諭德靳批此非苟異衆作者
考試官學士江批本啓蒙立說良是
聖人發明後天乾坤之卦必推二老之所由名
也夫乾象天而名以父坤象地而名以母是固
各有義矣非說卦聖人發明以示人孰從而知
之哉甞即文王後天之圖而觀之蓋有曰乾父
者矣乾以父稱則其尊非六子之可擬也而乾
何以稱乎父耶蓋乾之為卦三畫皆竒陽之純
punctuated:
似德而非德也，謙云乎哉？一誠偽之間，而理欲判焉。學易者不可不辨。

乾，天也，故稱乎父；坤，地也，故稱乎母。
金𤇍

同考試官教諭鄒批：此作本後天圖學，發明聖人所以稱二老之故，明白簡要，宜錄之以示經生之不讀《啓蒙》者。

同考試官教諭王批：此題於乾坤父母處，類能言之而不知其義者多。惟此本圖學發明，其言有據，蓋熟於本領者。

考試官左諭德靳批：此非苟異衆作者。

考試官學士江批：本《啓蒙》立說，良是。

聖人發明後天乾坤之卦，必推二老之所由名也。夫乾象天而名以父，坤象地而名以母，是固各有義矣。非《說卦》聖人發明以示人，孰從而知之哉？甞即文王後天之圖而觀之，蓋有曰乾父者矣。乾以父稱，則其尊非六子之可擬也。而乾何以稱乎父耶？蓋乾之為卦，三畫皆竒，陽之純
translation_en:
…resembles virtue but is not virtue. Can it be called humility? The distinction between sincerity and falsity separates principle from desire. Students of the Changes must discern this.

“Qian is Heaven, and therefore is called father; Kun is Earth, and therefore is called mother.”
By Jin [given name 𤇍, reading uncertain].

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: This composition draws on the study of the Later Heaven diagram to elucidate why the sage called them the two parents. Clear, concise, and essential, it should be recorded for students of the Classics who have not read the Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Qimeng).

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: On this topic, many can speak of Qian and Kun as father and mother without understanding what this means. This composition alone elucidates the matter through the study of the diagrams. Its statements have a sound basis: its author clearly knows the fundamentals thoroughly.

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Mentor: This is not a composition that merely seeks to differ from the crowd.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: It bases its argument on the Introduction to the Study of the Changes; this is entirely sound.

In elucidating the Later Heaven trigrams Qian and Kun, the sage necessarily traced the reason for their designation as the two parents. Qian represents Heaven and is named father; Kun represents Earth and is named mother. Each designation certainly has its own meaning. Had the sage not elucidated this in the Explanation of the Trigrams (Shuogua) to instruct people, how could anyone have come to understand it? I once examined King Wen’s Later Heaven diagram, and there indeed was the designation “Qian, father.” Since Qian is called father, its honored position cannot be matched by that of the six children. Yet why is Qian called father? It is because, in the trigram Qian, all three lines are undivided: it is the purest yang…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也健之至也有天之象焉今夫天之位乎上也
確然至健生理一動而品物皆資之以為其朕
兆元氣一行而萬物皆賴之以肇其端倪所謂
知始者在是所謂成象者在是是乾乃萬物所
以生有父之道也有父之道則稱之為父非以
是故歟又有曰坤母者矣坤以母稱則其尊非
六子之可同也而坤何以稱乎母耶盖坤之為
卦三畫皆偶陰之純也順之至也有地之象焉
今夫地之位乎下也隤然至順凡資生理以為
===
其朕兆者莫不于焉而流形凡藉元氣以肇其
端倪者莫不于焉而效法所謂代天有終者在
是所謂承天時行者在是是坤乃萬物之所由
成有母之道也有母之道則稱之為母非以是
故歟此皆文王觀伏羲已成之卦推其未明之
象而說卦發明之者也聖人之蘊因卦以發詎
不然夫抑論之乾坤易之縕也羲皇仰觀俯察
之初畫一奇以象陽畫一偶以象陰乾坤立而
天下之理具矣先天對待之體後天流行之用
punctuated: 也，健之至也，有天之象焉。今夫天之位乎上也，確然至健，生理一動，而品物皆資之以為其朕兆；元氣一行，而萬物皆賴之以肇其端倪。所謂知始者在是，所謂成象者在是。是乾乃萬物所以生，有父之道也。有父之道，則稱之為父，非以是故歟？又有曰坤母者矣。坤以母稱，則其尊非六子之可同也，而坤何以稱乎母耶？盖坤之為卦，三畫皆偶，陰之純也，順之至也，有地之象焉。今夫地之位乎下也，隤然至順，凡資生理以為其朕兆者，莫不于焉而流形；凡藉元氣以肇其端倪者，莫不于焉而效法。所謂代天有終者在是，所謂承天時行者在是。是坤乃萬物之所由成，有母之道也。有母之道，則稱之為母，非以是故歟？此皆文王觀伏羲已成之卦，推其未明之象，而《說卦》發明之者也。聖人之蘊，因卦以發，詎不然夫？抑論之，乾坤，《易》之縕也。羲皇仰觀俯察之初，畫一奇以象陽，畫一偶以象陰，乾坤立而天下之理具矣。先天對待之體，後天流行之用，
translation_en:
…and is the utmost in strength, embodying the image of Heaven. Now Heaven occupies the position above, firm and supremely strong. Once its life-generating principle stirs, all things draw upon it for their first stirrings; once its primordial qi circulates, the myriad things depend upon it to initiate their beginnings. Herein lies what is called “presiding over beginnings”; herein lies what is called “forming images.” Thus Qian is that through which the myriad things are born and possesses the Way of a father. Since it possesses the Way of a father, is this not why it is called the father?
There is also the designation “Kun, the mother.” Since Kun is called the mother, its honored status cannot be equaled by the six children. But why is Kun called the mother? In the trigram Kun, all three lines are divided: it is pure yin and the utmost in yielding, embodying the image of Earth. Now Earth occupies the position below, compliant and supremely yielding. Everything that draws upon the life-generating principle for its first stirrings takes on flowing form here; everything that relies upon primordial qi to initiate its beginnings manifests its pattern here. Herein lies what is called “bringing things to completion on Heaven’s behalf”; herein lies what is called “receiving Heaven’s influence and acting in accordance with the seasons.” Thus Kun is that through which the myriad things attain completion and possesses the Way of a mother. Since it possesses the Way of a mother, is this not why it is called the mother?
These are all images that King Wen inferred, by contemplating the trigrams already established by Fuxi, but that had not yet been made clear; the Explanation of the Trigrams elucidates them. The sage’s profound understanding is revealed through the trigrams—is this not so? To discuss the matter further, Qian and Kun are the inner substance of the Book of Changes. When the august Fuxi first looked upward and examined what lay below, he drew a single undivided line to symbolize yang and a single divided line to symbolize yin. Once Qian and Kun were established, the principles of all under Heaven were fully present. The structure of paired opposites in the Earlier Heaven arrangement and the operation of circulating processes in the Later Heaven arrangement…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
何莫非乾坤為之哉雖然其在吾心亦有然者
人能法易簡之德以成位乎天地之中則乾坤
之理不在於卦圖而在於我矣孰謂文王圖學
之妙非為吾人計哉
書
先王顧諟天之明命以承上下神祇社稷
宗廟罔不祇肅
邊寧
同考試官教諭姜批題本正大作者多認理不真
此作文氣莊重深得經旨宜錄以冠本房
同考試官教授王批此題以敬為主作者多泛而
不切是篇文理通暢得伊尹言意之意見美美
考試官左諭德靳批老臣忠懇之意此作盡之
考試官學士江批通篇以敬字立說得旨
聖君明大德也無間其功而於承大祭也無間
其敬蓋明德事神必本於敬者人君之先務也
有商聖君能然伊尹得不舉以為太甲告哉想
其意蓋謂吾王承今日之丕緒可不知其所自
punctuated:
何莫非乾坤為之哉？雖然，其在吾心亦有然者。人能法易簡之德，以成位乎天地之中，則乾坤之理不在於卦圖，而在於我矣。孰謂文王圖學之妙，非為吾人計哉？

書
先王顧諟天之明命，以承上下神祇、社稷、宗廟，罔不祇肅。
邊寧

同考試官教諭姜批：題本正大，作者多認理不真。此作文氣莊重，深得經旨，宜錄以冠本房。
同考試官教授王批：此題以敬為主，作者多泛而不切。是篇文理通暢，得伊尹言意之意見，美美。
考試官左諭德靳批：老臣忠懇之意，此作盡之。
考試官學士江批：通篇以敬字立說，得旨。

聖君明大德也，無間其功；而於承大祭也，無間其敬。蓋明德事神，必本於敬者，人君之先務也。有商聖君能然，伊尹得不舉以為太甲告哉？想其意，蓋謂吾王承今日之丕緒，可不知其所自
translation_en:
…What among these is not brought about by Qian and Kun? Yet the same is also true within our own minds. If people can emulate the virtues of ease and simplicity and thereby establish their place between Heaven and Earth, then the principles of Qian and Kun reside not in the hexagram diagrams but in ourselves. Who could say that the subtlety of King Wen’s learning concerning the diagrams was not intended for our benefit?

Book of Documents
“The former king kept Heaven’s luminous mandate constantly before him. In serving the spirits above and below, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temples, he was invariably reverent and solemn.”
By Bian Ning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The topic itself is upright and weighty, but many writers fail to grasp its principles truly. This composition is dignified in its expression and deeply apprehends the classic’s meaning. It should be selected to head the essays from this examining room.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Professor: “Reverence is central to this topic, but many writers are diffuse and fail to address it closely. This essay’s reasoning and expression flow clearly, capturing the intention of Yi Yin’s words [?]. Excellent, excellent!”
Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: “This composition fully conveys the loyal earnestness of the veteran minister.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: “The entire essay develops its argument around the word ‘reverence’ and grasps the purport.”

In making his great virtue manifest, the sage ruler never relaxed his efforts; in conducting the great sacrifices, he never relaxed his reverence. For making virtue manifest and serving the spirits must be rooted in reverence: this is the ruler’s foremost duty. The sage ruler of Shang could act thus. How could Yi Yin fail to cite his example in admonishing Tai Jia? We may imagine that his intention was to say: Our king has inherited this great undertaking today; can he fail to know whence it came…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乎彼明命者天之所以命乎人而人之所以得
乎天者也惟我成湯知天之所以命於我者不
可以少昧也則靜而存動而察常目在之使全
體為之呈露罔敢怠焉知我之所以得於天者
不可以少昏也則義制事禮制心常目在之俾
大用為之顯行罔敢忽焉日新之功雖盤盂而
有銘所謂昧爽丕顯是已寧使其有一時之不
明乎懋昭之功雖羹墻而有見所謂無時豫怠
是已寧使其有一息之不明乎成湯顧諟明命
===
如此則其達之於事神也焉往而不敬哉何者
君身百神之主而敬德事神之要也故上而天
神下而地祇分雖殊矣成湯則一皆以此心承
之而不違外而社稷內而宗廟分雖異矣成湯
則一皆以此心奉之而不爽對越之忱隨所在
而隆蓋未嘗敬於上而遺於下也昭格之念因
所事而篤蓋未嘗敬於內而失於外也吁以顧
諟之心而為祗肅之心以明德之敬而為事神
之敬則其所以建丕緒以貽後人者有自矣為
punctuated: 乎？彼明命者，天之所以命乎人，而人之所以得乎天者也。惟我成湯，知天之所以命於我者不可以少昧也，則靜而存，動而察，常目在之，使全體為之呈露，罔敢怠焉；知我之所以得於天者不可以少昏也，則義制事，禮制心，常目在之，俾大用為之顯行，罔敢忽焉。日新之功，雖盤盂而有銘，所謂昧爽丕顯是已，寧使其有一時之不明乎？懋昭之功，雖羹墻而有見，所謂無時豫怠是已，寧使其有一息之不明乎？成湯顧諟明命如此，則其達之於事神也，焉往而不敬哉？何者？君身百神之主，而敬德事神之要也。故上而天神，下而地祇，分雖殊矣，成湯則一皆以此心承之而不違；外而社稷，內而宗廟，分雖異矣，成湯則一皆以此心奉之而不爽。對越之忱，隨所在而隆，蓋未嘗敬於上而遺於下也；昭格之念，因所事而篤，蓋未嘗敬於內而失於外也。吁！以顧諟之心而為祗肅之心，以明德之敬而為事神之敬，則其所以建丕緒以貽後人者有自矣。為
translation_en:
…? That luminous mandate is what Heaven confers upon human beings and what human beings receive from Heaven. Our Cheng Tang alone understood that what Heaven had conferred upon him must not be obscured in the slightest. Thus, in stillness he preserved it, and in activity he examined it, keeping his attention constantly upon it so that its entire substance stood revealed, never daring to grow remiss. He understood that what he had received from Heaven must not be dimmed in the slightest. Thus he regulated affairs through righteousness and governed his heart through ritual propriety, keeping his attention constantly upon it so that its great operation became manifest in practice, never daring to neglect it.

In his work of daily renewal, even his basins and bowls bore inscriptions. This is what is meant by “making it greatly manifest at dawn”: how could he allow it to remain unilluminated for even a moment? In his work of diligently making it shine, even in soup and against a wall he beheld it. This is what is meant by “never indulging in ease or indolence”: how could he allow it to remain unilluminated for even a single breath? Such was Cheng Tang’s constant regard for the luminous mandate. When he extended this to serving the spirits, where could he fail to be reverent?

Why was this so? The ruler himself presides over the hundred spirits, and reverence for virtue is essential to serving them. Thus, although the celestial spirits above and the terrestrial spirits below had different stations, Cheng Tang attended to them all with this same heart, without deviation. Although the altars of soil and grain outside and the ancestral temple within had different stations, Cheng Tang served them all with this same heart, without error. His sincerity in standing before the spirits grew profound wherever they were: he never revered those above while neglecting those below. His intent to reach the spirits grew earnest according to those he served: he never revered those within while failing those outside.

Ah! By making the heart that constantly regarded the mandate the heart of solemn reverence, and by making the reverence with which he illuminated virtue the reverence with which he served the spirits, he established the foundation from which he built the great enterprise and bequeathed it to later generations. For one who is …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
太甲者可不知所以敬承之哉抑考太甲嗣位
之初不惠于阿衡伊尹先見其微也故作書為
訓首啓之以此次述有夏之忠信感之一篇之
中拳拳致意老臣忠愛至矣厥後太甲克終允
德為商令主謂非伊尹告戒之功而誰歟然顧
諟天命之一言實萬世君人者明德之要存之
則治否則亂也嗚呼是豈特一時嗣王所當知
哉
德威惟畏德明惟明
===
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批本帝舜實事作講最是
而文字亦豐贍醇雅可愛故錄之
同考試官教授王批場中作者多以德威德明四
字牽綴成文繁復可厭此篇詞贍理明壁經中翹楚者
考試官左諭德靳批說理透徹
考試官學士江批發揮德威德明處可觀
聖君之德有所以肅天下者有所以正天下者
蓋肅天下莫大於德威而正天下莫大於德明
punctuated:
太甲者，可不知所以敬承之哉？抑考太甲嗣位之初，不惠于阿衡，伊尹先見其微也，故作書為訓，首啓之以此，次述有夏之忠信感之。一篇之中，拳拳致意，老臣忠愛至矣。厥後太甲克終允德，為商令主，謂非伊尹告戒之功而誰歟？然顧諟天命之一言，實萬世君人者明德之要，存之則治，否則亂也。嗚呼！是豈特一時嗣王所當知哉？

德威惟畏，德明惟明。

張璿

同考試官教諭姜批：本帝舜實事作講，最是，而文字亦豐贍醇雅可愛，故錄之。

同考試官教授王批：場中作者多以德威德明四字牽綴成文，繁復可厭。此篇詞贍理明，壁經中翹楚者。

考試官左諭德靳批：說理透徹。

考試官學士江批：發揮德威德明處可觀。

聖君之德，有所以肅天下者，有所以正天下者。蓋肅天下莫大於德威，而正天下莫大於德明
translation_en:
…could Tai Jia fail to understand how to receive and carry this forward reverently? Now, examining the beginning of Tai Jia’s succession to the throne, we find that he did not heed the A-heng, the chief minister. Yi Yin perceived the first subtle signs of this beforehand and therefore composed a document to instruct him. He began by enlightening him on this point, then recounted the loyalty and trustworthiness of the Xia to move him. Throughout the document he earnestly conveyed his intentions: the old minister’s loyalty and loving concern were utmost. Subsequently, Tai Jia succeeded in remaining true to virtue to the end and became an excellent ruler of Shang. To whose achievement could this be attributed, if not to Yi Yin’s admonitions? Yet the single injunction to keep Heaven’s mandate constantly in view is truly the essential means by which rulers of all ages make their virtue bright. When they preserve it, there is order; otherwise, disorder. Alas! Could this be something that only the succeeding king of that particular time needed to understand?

“His virtuous majesty alone was feared; his virtuous discernment alone was held to be clear-sighted.”

Zhang Xuan 張璿

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Grounding the exposition in the actual deeds of Emperor Shun is entirely right. The writing is also rich, ample, pure, and elegant—worthy of appreciation. For this reason it has been selected.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Professor: Many writers in the examination hall string together compositions around the four characters ‘virtuous majesty’ and ‘virtuous discernment,’ producing tiresome elaboration and repetition. This essay is ample in expression and clear in reasoning, an outstanding work among those on the ‘Wall Classic’ [?].

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: The exposition of principle is penetrating and thorough.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: The passages elaborating virtuous majesty and virtuous discernment are worthy of attention.

The virtue of a sage ruler has that whereby he instills reverence throughout the realm, and that whereby he sets the realm right. For nothing is greater than virtuous majesty in instilling reverence throughout the realm, and nothing is greater than virtuous discernment in setting the realm right…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也自非帝舜之聖其孰能兩全之哉穆王訓刑
而舉是以為呂侯告其意盖謂人君為治非威
無以肅天下之衆然苗民以虐為威則威非其
威矣舜則易其道而以德為威焉想其仁而有
勇凛乎聖武之布昭剛而能斷肅乎王靈之丕
振雖不能無刑法之制也然一皆本於欽恤之
攸寓而非依勢以作威雖不能無賞罰之行也
然一皆出於好生之攸存而非倚法以為削舜
之以德為威如此初豈有意于致民之畏哉但
===
見震懾於德威之下者仰之若雷霆妖誕屏息
自爾不犯于有司也畏之如神明邪妄潛消自
爾罔干于政治也茲非以德為威而天下之皆
畏乎人君致治非明無以正天下之心然苗民
以察為明則明非其明矣舜則變其道而以德
為明焉想其重華之旁達昭然日月之照臨玄
德之敷宣燦然日星之炳燿濬哲文明有以畢
照遠近之幽微明物察倫有以周知中外之隱
慝舜之以德為明如此初豈有心於使民之明
punctuated: 也。自非帝舜之聖，其孰能兩全之哉？穆王訓刑，而舉是以為呂侯告，其意盖謂人君為治，非威無以肅天下之衆。然苗民以虐為威，則威非其威矣。舜則易其道，而以德為威焉。想其仁而有勇，凛乎聖武之布昭；剛而能斷，肅乎王靈之丕振。雖不能無刑法之制也，然一皆本於欽恤之攸寓，而非依勢以作威；雖不能無賞罰之行也，然一皆出於好生之攸存，而非倚法以為削。舜之以德為威如此，初豈有意于致民之畏哉？但見震懾於德威之下者，仰之若雷霆，妖誕屏息，自爾不犯于有司也；畏之如神明，邪妄潛消，自爾罔干于政治也。茲非以德為威，而天下之皆畏乎？人君致治，非明無以正天下之心。然苗民以察為明，則明非其明矣。舜則變其道，而以德為明焉。想其重華之旁達，昭然日月之照臨；玄德之敷宣，燦然日星之炳燿。濬哲文明，有以畢照遠近之幽微；明物察倫，有以周知中外之隱慝。舜之以德為明如此，初豈有心於使民之明
translation_en:
…Indeed, who but one as sage as Emperor Shun could fully possess both? When King Mu gave instruction concerning punishments, he invoked this in his address to the Marquis of Lü. His meaning was presumably that a ruler cannot govern and bring the multitudes of the realm to order without awe-inspiring authority. Yet the Miao people made cruelty their authority, so theirs was not true authority. Shun changed their way and made virtue his authority. Imagine his benevolence joined with courage: how imposing the manifest brilliance of his sagely martial power! His firmness joined with decisiveness: how solemn the mighty assertion of his royal might! Although he could not dispense with penal institutions, all were rooted in reverent care and compassion, rather than reliance on power to inspire terror. Although he could not dispense with rewards and punishments, all arose from his concern to preserve life, rather than reliance on law to oppress. Such was Shun’s use of virtue as authority. Had he ever intended to make the people afraid? Yet those awed by his virtuous authority looked up to him as to thunder: uncanny and deceitful conduct fell silent, and naturally they committed no offenses against the authorities. They revered him as a divine intelligence: wickedness and perversity quietly vanished, and naturally they did nothing to disrupt government. Was this not making virtue his authority, so that all under Heaven stood in awe?

For a ruler to achieve good government, he must have discernment to rectify the hearts of all under Heaven. Yet the Miao people made intrusive scrutiny their discernment, so theirs was not true discernment. Shun changed their way and made virtue his discernment. Imagine his redoubled brilliance reaching everywhere, radiant as the illumination of sun and moon; his profound virtue spreading abroad, resplendent as the shining sun and stars. His penetrating wisdom and cultivated brilliance enabled him to illuminate every obscurity and subtlety, near and far; his understanding of things and discernment of human relationships enabled him to know fully the concealed wickedness within and without. Such was Shun’s use of virtue as discernment. Had he ever intended to make the people discerning…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
哉但見覆育於德明之中者是非明白舉知務
乎人道之宜鰥寡無復其盖蔽也善惡昭彰舉
知循夫天理之正民神無復以雜糅也茲非以
德為明而天下之皆明乎吁威可能也以德而
為威者不可能也明可能也以德而為明者不
可能也然則舜之所以遏絕苗民而致治化之
隆者豈偶然哉大抵君非威則懦而徒威者多
至於虐非明則昏而徒明者或至於察二者必
有德以為之本斯善矣穆王訓刑首舉舜事以
===
為言其亦庶乎知所本者惜乎五刑有贖而有
戾於先王之良法也然其篇中不止曰德而又
曰中曰敬曰勤不一而足惓惓仁厚忠愛猶有
唐虞三代之遺意在焉夫子所以錄其書者端
有取於斯云
詩
雞既鳴矣朝既盈矣匪雞則鳴蒼蠅之聲
東方明矣朝既昌矣匪東方則明月出
之光
punctuated:
哉？但見覆育於德明之中者，是非明白，舉知務乎人道之宜，鰥寡無復其盖蔽也；善惡昭彰，舉知循夫天理之正，民神無復以雜糅也。茲非以德為明，而天下之皆明乎？吁！威可能也，以德而為威者不可能也；明可能也，以德而為明者不可能也。然則舜之所以遏絕苗民而致治化之隆者，豈偶然哉？大抵君非威則懦，而徒威者多至於虐；非明則昏，而徒明者或至於察。二者必有德以為之本，斯善矣。穆王訓刑，首舉舜事以為言，其亦庶乎知所本者。惜乎五刑有贖，而有戾於先王之良法也。然其篇中不止曰德，而又曰中、曰敬、曰勤，不一而足。惓惓仁厚忠愛，猶有唐虞三代之遺意在焉。夫子所以錄其書者，端有取於斯云。

詩

雞既鳴矣，朝既盈矣。匪雞則鳴，蒼蠅之聲。東方明矣，朝既昌矣。匪東方則明，月出之光。
translation_en:
…was it? We see only that those sheltered and nurtured within the illumination of his virtue clearly distinguished right from wrong: all knew to attend to what was fitting in human conduct, and widowers and widows were no longer left in obscurity. Good and evil were plainly revealed: all knew to follow the rectitude of Heaven’s principle, and humans and spirits were no longer intermixed. Was this not illumination through virtue, by which all under Heaven became enlightened? Ah! Authority can be achieved, but authority through virtue is beyond ordinary attainment. Discernment can be achieved, but discernment through virtue is beyond ordinary attainment. Was it, then, mere chance that Shun put an end to the ways of the Miao people and brought orderly government and moral transformation to their height?

Generally, a ruler without authority is weak, but one who relies on authority alone often becomes cruel; without discernment he is benighted, but one who relies on discernment alone may become excessively inquisitorial. Both must be rooted in virtue; only then are they good. When King Mu delivered his instructions on punishments, he began by invoking Shun’s deeds. He thus came close to understanding what should serve as the foundation. Regrettably, he allowed redemption payments for the Five Punishments, thereby departing from the good laws of the former kings. Yet this chapter speaks not only of virtue, but also of balance, reverence, and diligence, among much else. Its earnest humanity, generosity, loyalty, and care still preserve something of the spirit of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. It was precisely these qualities that the Master valued in recording this document.

The Book of Odes

“The cock has already crowed;
the court is already full.”
“It is not the cock crowing,
but the sound of flies.”
“The east is bright;
the court is already thronged.”
“It is not the east that is bright,
but the light of the rising moon.”

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
許魯
同考試官訓導周批此作詞理俱到深得賢妃
警君之意可與言詩矣
同考試官訓導李批詩人叙賢妃告君視朝意
多含蓄欲發於筆端不易也子就塲屋中數語挑剔分
明可嘉
同考試官教諭林批風義不難作塲中士子
類務騁辭而意或不白惟此簡切條達賢妃警畏之心
溢於言表讀之不俟終篇而可以興矣
===
考試官左諭德靳批風義似此者絕少
考試官學士江批措詞明暢
賢妃欲君視朝有警於所聞之似者有警於所
見之似者夫告君以視朝無非警畏之心之所
存也詩人兩述其事而美之則齊妃之賢可見
矣吾想為齊妃者身處宫闈之間心運朝廷之
上至於將旦之時必告其君曰雞鳴視朝此常
禮也今者雞鳴喈喈夜已央矣斯時也吾想百
爾君子趨公門而俟號令者鷺序于班行藹藹
punctuated:
許魯

同考試官訓導周批：此作詞理俱到，深得賢妃警君之意，可與言詩矣。

同考試官訓導李批：詩人叙賢妃告君視朝，意多含蓄，欲發於筆端不易也。子就塲屋中數語挑剔分明，可嘉。

同考試官教諭林批：風義不難作，塲中士子類務騁辭，而意或不白。惟此簡切條達，賢妃警畏之心溢於言表，讀之不俟終篇而可以興矣。

考試官左諭德靳批：風義似此者絕少。

考試官學士江批：措詞明暢。

賢妃欲君視朝，有警於所聞之似者，有警於所見之似者。夫告君以視朝，無非警畏之心之所存也。詩人兩述其事而美之，則齊妃之賢可見矣。吾想為齊妃者，身處宫闈之間，心運朝廷之上。至於將旦之時，必告其君曰：「雞鳴視朝，此常禮也。今者雞鳴喈喈，夜已央矣。斯時也，吾想百爾君子，趨公門而俟號令者，鷺序于班行，藹藹
translation_en:
Xu Lu 許魯

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, an Assistant Instructor: This composition is accomplished in both expression and reasoning. It fully grasps the worthy consort’s intention in admonishing her lord. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Odes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, an Assistant Instructor: In describing the worthy consort urging her lord to hold court, the poet leaves much implicit; bringing this out in writing is no easy matter. With just a few phrases written in the examination hall, you have brought these meanings clearly to light. This is commendable.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, an Instructor: An exposition on the Airs is not difficult to write. Candidates in the examination hall generally strive to display their eloquence, yet their meaning sometimes remains unclear. This composition alone is concise, pertinent, lucid, and well ordered. The worthy consort’s vigilant and apprehensive heart reveals itself beyond the words. Even before finishing it, the reader may be stirred.

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: Expositions on the Airs like this are exceedingly rare.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, an Academician: The wording is clear and fluent.

The worthy consort wished her lord to hold court. She admonished him on the basis of what seemed to be so in what she heard, and on the basis of what seemed to be so in what she saw. In urging her lord to hold court, she expressed throughout her vigilant and apprehensive heart. The poet twice recounts these events in praise of her; thus the worthiness of the consort of Qi becomes apparent. I imagine that, as consort of Qi, though she dwelt within the palace chambers, her thoughts were occupied with the court. As dawn approached, she would surely tell her lord: “To hold court at cockcrow is the established ritual. Now the cocks are crowing in chorus, and the night has reached its midpoint. At this moment, I imagine all you gentlemen who hasten to the palace gate to await commands, standing in court ranks like ordered herons, gathered in great numbers …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
如也凡我卿士集禁垣而待敷陳者鵠立於兩
階彬彬如也吾君尚爾遲遲而不興其能安乎
然其實非雞之鳴也乃蒼蠅之聲也是豈賢妃
之自誑哉心常恐晚故聞其似者以為真耳啓
告之詞方已而警畏之心尤切故又再告之曰
日出視朝此常制也今者東方已明日將旦矣
斯時也吾想待漏公門之下者已蹌蹌然其盛
莫不翹首以待王言之頒也披星禁垣之外者
已濟濟然其多莫不傾心以俟衷懷之吐也吾
===
君尚爾徐徐而不出其能寧乎然其實非東方
之明也乃月出之光也是豈賢妃之自誣哉心
常恐晚故見其似者以為真耳吁雞未鳴而猶
告則已鳴而告可知矣日未出而猶告則已出
而告可知矣賢妃心存警畏如此宜乎詩人叙
其事而美之也歟嗟夫朝廷之上四方則焉閨
門之内萬化關焉古昔帝王成光明之業而享
國祚之久者賢妃之功不可無也若齊妃啓告
之勤如此其至誠所感必有移轉君心而人不
punctuated: 如也。凡我卿士集禁垣而待敷陳者，鵠立於兩階，彬彬如也。吾君尚爾遲遲而不興，其能安乎？然其實非雞之鳴也，乃蒼蠅之聲也。是豈賢妃之自誑哉？心常恐晚，故聞其似者以為真耳。啓告之詞方已，而警畏之心尤切，故又再告之曰：「日出視朝，此常制也。今者東方已明，日將旦矣。斯時也，吾想待漏公門之下者，已蹌蹌然其盛，莫不翹首以待王言之頒也；披星禁垣之外者，已濟濟然其多，莫不傾心以俟衷懷之吐也。吾君尚爾徐徐而不出，其能寧乎？」然其實非東方之明也，乃月出之光也。是豈賢妃之自誣哉？心常恐晚，故見其似者以為真耳。吁！雞未鳴而猶告，則已鳴而告可知矣；日未出而猶告，則已出而告可知矣。賢妃心存警畏如此，宜乎詩人叙其事而美之也歟！嗟夫！朝廷之上，四方則焉；閨門之内，萬化關焉。古昔帝王成光明之業而享國祚之久者，賢妃之功不可無也。若齊妃啓告之勤如此，其至誠所感，必有移轉君心而人不
translation_en:
…in orderly abundance. “All our high ministers and officers who assemble within the palace precincts, awaiting their opportunity to present their counsel, stand erect like swans beside the two stairways, dignified and refined. If my lord still delays and does not rise, can he be at ease?” Yet it was not actually the crowing of a cock, but the sound of flies. Could this worthy consort have been deceiving herself? Her heart constantly feared being late, so she took a similar sound for the real thing. Her words of admonition had scarcely ended when her vigilance and apprehension grew still more urgent. Thus she addressed him again: “To hold court at sunrise is the established rule. Now the east is already bright, and day is about to break. At this moment, I imagine those waiting below the palace gate for the appointed hour already form an imposing assembly, moving with measured dignity, all craning their necks in expectation of the royal pronouncements. Those who have come beneath the stars to wait outside the palace precincts already gather in great numbers, all eagerly awaiting the expression of your innermost thoughts. If my lord still lingers and does not come forth, can he be at peace?” Yet it was not actually the brightness of the eastern sky, but the light of the rising moon. Could this worthy consort have been deluding herself? Her heart constantly feared being late, so she took a similar sight for the real thing.

Ah! If she admonished him even before the cock had crowed, we may be sure she would do so once it had crowed. If she admonished him even before the sun had risen, we may be sure she would do so once it had risen. Such was the vigilance and apprehension in this worthy consort’s heart: surely it was fitting that the poet should recount her deeds and praise her! Alas! The court provides the model for all regions, while within the inner chambers lie the springs of all moral transformation. The glorious achievements and enduring dynastic fortunes of the emperors and kings of antiquity could not have been attained without the contributions of worthy consorts. With the consort of Qi so diligent in her admonitions, the influence of her utmost sincerity must have moved and changed her lord’s heart in ways that others did not…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
及知者矣然則齊國在當時獨以富强稱其亦
有賴乎此耶噫君國者且然君天下者可以監
矣
君子萬年介爾昭明
顏正
同考試官訓導周批介福昭明實含下章祚
胤意作者漫無歸着獨是篇理到而辭足以發之
必佳士也
同考試官訓導李批凡作雅義有矩度不可
牽强補綴雖引用字語亦須精密的實乃佳况臣荅
君之詞尤不可不謹嚴故刊此以範學者
===
同考試官教諭林批君福易言而昭明二字
難於摹寫獨此作發揮明白意亦有詩人忠愛之心者
惡乎弗錄
考試官左諭德靳批大雅義甚麗然亦甚典
考試官學士江批得臣子祝君之意
歷無疆之年享至顯之福人臣祝君然也蓋福
以昭明而享之萬年人君之所願莫過於此也
punctuated:
及知者矣。然則齊國在當時獨以富强稱，其亦有賴乎此耶？噫！君國者且然，君天下者可以監矣。

君子萬年，介爾昭明。
顏正

同考試官訓導周批：介福昭明，實含下章祚胤意。作者漫無歸着，獨是篇理到，而辭足以發之，必佳士也。

同考試官訓導李批：凡作雅義，有矩度，不可牽强補綴。雖引用字語，亦須精密的實乃佳。况臣荅君之詞，尤不可不謹嚴，故刊此以範學者。

同考試官教諭林批：君福易言，而昭明二字難於摹寫。獨此作發揮明白，意亦有詩人忠愛之心者，惡乎弗錄？

考試官左諭德靳批：大雅義甚麗，然亦甚典。

考試官學士江批：得臣子祝君之意。

歷無疆之年，享至顯之福，人臣祝君然也。蓋福以昭明，而享之萬年，人君之所願莫過於此也。
translation_en:
…beyond others’ awareness. If so, did Qi’s distinction in wealth and power at that time also owe something to this? Ah! If this holds for one who rules a state, one who rules all under Heaven may take it as a lesson.

“May our lord live ten thousand years; may you be granted resplendent blessings.”
Yan Zheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor: The great and resplendent blessings implicitly encompass the blessing upon descendants mentioned in the following stanza. Other writers ramble without reaching a conclusion. This essay alone fully grasps the principle, and its language adequately expresses it. Its author must be an excellent scholar.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Any exposition of the Odes of the Court must observe proper standards; it must not be forcibly cobbled together. Even quoted words and phrases must be precise and sound if the composition is to be good. How much more scrupulous and dignified must language be when a subject answers his ruler! We therefore print this essay as a model for students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: It is easy to speak of blessings for a ruler, but difficult to portray the meaning of the two characters for “resplendent.” This composition alone develops that meaning clearly. I believe its author, too, possesses the poet’s heart of loyalty and love. How could we fail to include it?

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: This exposition of the Major Odes of the Court is exceedingly elegant, yet also thoroughly grounded in classical precedent.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: It captures the spirit in which a subject wishes blessings upon his ruler.

To live for boundless years and enjoy the most glorious blessings: such are the wishes a subject offers his ruler. For blessings to be resplendent, and to enjoy them for ten thousand years—nothing a ruler desires could surpass this.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
臣子以是而為其君祝忠愛之心何深哉周之
父兄因王舉行葦之燕歌此以答之若謂吾君
肆筵設席而禮意之殷勤祝壽頌德而恩寵之
優渥我將何以報之耶惟願吾君宅中圖大歷
年齡之永久由百歲以至於千居重馭輕更歲
月之延綿由千歲以至於萬時序雖屢更也而
皇矣上帝大爾以昭明之福者如一日即其始
不異於其終焉日月雖推遷也而彼蒼者天介
爾以昭明之福者如一時要其終不殊於其始
===
焉如介之以福祿耶則天命常凝海宇有不震
不騰之慶人心永戴億兆有會極歸極之休其
福祿如是何昭明似之如介之以子孫耶則維
千維億螽斯有蟄蟄之祥宜君宜王麟趾有振
振之瑞其子孫如是何昭明如之瑞應駢臻耿
耿乎日月之照臨凡吾民之景仰於萬年者無厭
斁也休徵疊見昭昭乎雲漢之為章凡吾人之
快覩於萬年者無終窮也福而至是則我臣子
之心庶幾少罄而吾王之恩庶幾乎可答矣意
punctuated: 臣子以是而為其君祝，忠愛之心何深哉！周之父兄因王舉行葦之燕，歌此以答之，若謂：「吾君肆筵設席，而禮意之殷勤；祝壽頌德，而恩寵之優渥。我將何以報之耶？惟願吾君宅中圖大，歷年齡之永久，由百歲以至於千；居重馭輕，更歲月之延綿，由千歲以至於萬。時序雖屢更也，而皇矣上帝大爾以昭明之福者如一日，即其始不異於其終焉；日月雖推遷也，而彼蒼者天介爾以昭明之福者如一時，要其終不殊於其始焉。如介之以福祿耶，則天命常凝，海宇有不震不騰之慶；人心永戴，億兆有會極歸極之休。其福祿如是，何昭明似之！如介之以子孫耶，則維千維億，螽斯有蟄蟄之祥；宜君宜王，麟趾有振振之瑞。其子孫如是，何昭明如之！瑞應駢臻，耿耿乎日月之照臨，凡吾民之景仰於萬年者，無厭斁也；休徵疊見，昭昭乎雲漢之為章，凡吾人之快覩於萬年者，無終窮也。福而至是，則我臣子之心庶幾少罄，而吾王之恩庶幾乎可答矣。」意
translation_en:
…When subjects offer this blessing for their ruler, how profound is their loyal affection! When the king of Zhou held the banquet celebrated in “Reeds Along the Banks” (Xing wei), his elder kinsmen sang this song in response, as though saying: “Our ruler spreads the mats and sets out the seats with such attentive courtesy; he wishes us long life and praises our virtue with such abundant favor. How shall we repay him? We wish only that our ruler, dwelling at the center and planning great undertakings, may enjoy enduring years, from a hundred to a thousand; and that, holding the seat of greatest authority and directing those below, he may pass through ever-lengthening months and years, from a thousand to ten thousand. Though the seasons repeatedly change, august God on High shall magnify you with radiant blessings as constantly as on a single day: their beginning shall be no different from their end. Though days and months pass, that azure Heaven shall aid you with radiant blessings as constantly as at a single moment: their end shall prove no different from their beginning.

“If Heaven aids you with blessings and emoluments, then Heaven’s Mandate shall remain firmly secured, and all within the seas shall rejoice in freedom from disturbance and upheaval. The people’s hearts shall uphold you forever, and the countless multitudes shall enjoy the felicity of gathering about and turning toward the sovereign standard. With blessings and emoluments such as these, what radiance could compare? If Heaven aids you with descendants, then they shall number in thousands and myriads, displaying the auspicious abundance of swarming locusts; fit to be lords and kings, they shall manifest the auspicious nobility celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hoof” (Lin zhi). With descendants such as these, what radiance could equal them? Auspicious responses shall arrive together, shining brightly as the sun and moon illuminate the world; throughout ten thousand years, our people shall never tire of looking up to them in admiration. Favorable signs shall appear one after another, brilliant as the patterned splendor of the River of Heaven; throughout ten thousand years, our delight in beholding them shall know no end. When blessings reach this extent, perhaps we subjects shall have given some expression to the fullness of our hearts, and perhaps our king’s kindness may be repaid.” I think …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
非有周太平之盛其君臣上下之交安能有□
氣象哉抑觀行葦君燕其臣欲其享壽祺介景
福而極恩禮之隆此則其臣歌既醉以答之亦
欲君被天祿以獲祚胤而罄頌禱之誠上施下
報藹然一堂無非忠厚懇切之誠意蓋與事矯
揉而面為佞者不可同日語也此其上下交而
其志同所以為有道之世歟先正謂太和元氣
在成周宇宙間吾於此觀之益信
春秋
===
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子
盟于踐土 公朝于王所 公會晋侯
齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯陳子莒子邾子秦
人于温 天王狩于河陽 壬申公朝
于王所 諸侯遂圍許 俱僖公二十八年
周讓
同考試官教諭洪 批 題本胡傳場中作者皆
就圍許上說叙事有遺而文法不整殊為可厭此篇
以晋文尊王討罪立說善於叙事辭亦明暢蓋經生之□
punctuated:
非有周太平之盛，其君臣上下之交，安能有□氣象哉？抑觀《行葦》，君燕其臣，欲其享壽祺、介景福，而極恩禮之隆；此則其臣歌《既醉》以答之，亦欲君被天祿以獲祚胤，而罄頌禱之誠。上施下報，藹然一堂，無非忠厚懇切之誠意，蓋與事矯揉而面為佞者不可同日語也。此其上下交而其志同，所以為有道之世歟？先正謂太和元氣在成周宇宙間，吾於此觀之益信。
春秋
公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土。公朝于王所。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于温。天王狩于河陽。壬申，公朝于王所。諸侯遂圍許。俱僖公二十八年。
周讓
同考試官教諭洪批：題本《胡傳》，場中作者皆就圍許上說，叙事有遺，而文法不整，殊為可厭。此篇以晋文尊王討罪立說，善於叙事，辭亦明暢，蓋經生之□
translation_en:
…were it not for the flourishing peace of Zhou, how could relations between ruler and ministers, superiors and inferiors, have displayed such [?] an atmosphere? Consider also “Reeds Along the Path” (Xing wei): the ruler feasted his ministers, wishing them longevity and good fortune and seeking great blessings for them, thus extending his favor and ceremonial courtesy to the utmost. His ministers responded by singing “Already Drunk” (Ji zui), likewise wishing that their ruler might receive Heaven’s bounty and obtain blessings and descendants, and pouring forth their sincere praise and prayers. The superior bestowed favors and those below reciprocated; all gathered in one hall in harmony, expressing nothing but generous, earnest sincerity. This surely cannot be spoken of in the same breath as contrived conduct and flattery to someone’s face. Was it this communion between superiors and inferiors, and their shared purpose, that made theirs an age possessing the Way? A former worthy said that the primal vital force of supreme harmony pervaded the world of Chengzhou. What I see here makes me believe this all the more.
Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and they concluded a covenant at Jiantu. The duke paid court at the king’s residence. The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and a representative of Qin at Wen. The Heavenly King hunted at Heyang. On the renshen day, the duke paid court at the king’s residence. The assembled lords then besieged Xu. All these entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.
Zhou Rang
Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor: The topic is based on Hu’s Commentary. The candidates in the examination hall all confined their discussion to the siege of Xu, leaving omissions in their narration and their compositions poorly structured—particularly tiresome. This essay bases its argument on Duke Wen of Jin’s honoring the king and punishing wrongdoing. It narrates events skillfully, and its language is clear and fluent. Indeed, among students of the Classics, [illegible]…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
生之傑然者
考試官左諭德靳批胡傳意正如此
考試官學士江批體貼傳意為文迥異衆作
伯主始率諸侯以盡尊王之禮伯主繼
率諸侯以討慢王之罪為可嘉此見王所之朝
許國之圍皆伯事之善也春秋均美之也宜哉
且我僖末年晋文主伯始盟踐土天王有下勞
之行再會于温天王有河陽之狩其寵之也至
矣文也於此可少慢乎是以領袖諸侯拜天顔
===
於咫尺偕同列辟展臣敬於斯須兩朝盛典迭
舉於王綱不振之秋一念忠誠每發於人心不
臣之日水木本原之心攸著上下冠履之分復
明雖曰朝非其地然天子在是諸侯就朝禮之
變也不亦彷彿朝于方嶽之意邪故春秋兩書
王所之朝於踐土于温之下其所以予晋文者
以此若乃踐土河陽許國近地諸侯再會既無
一跡之臨王所兩朝亦無一介之遣其不恭也
甚矣文也於此可少縱乎是以朝禮甫畢遂圍
punctuated:
生之傑然者。
考試官左諭德靳批：胡傳意正如此。
考試官學士江批：體貼傳意，為文迥異衆作。
伯主始率諸侯以盡尊王之禮，伯主繼率諸侯以討慢王之罪，為可嘉。此見王所之朝、許國之圍，皆伯事之善也，《春秋》均美之也宜哉！
且我僖末年，晋文主伯，始盟踐土，天王有下勞之行；再會于温，天王有河陽之狩。其寵之也至矣，文也於此可少慢乎？是以領袖諸侯，拜天顔於咫尺；偕同列辟，展臣敬於斯須。兩朝盛典，迭舉於王綱不振之秋；一念忠誠，每發於人心不臣之日。水木本原之心攸著，上下冠履之分復明。雖曰朝非其地，然天子在是，諸侯就朝，禮之變也，不亦彷彿朝于方嶽之意邪？故《春秋》兩書王所之朝於踐土、于温之下，其所以予晋文者以此。
若乃踐土、河陽，許國近地，諸侯再會，既無一跡之臨；王所兩朝，亦無一介之遣。其不恭也甚矣，文也於此可少縱乎？是以朝禮甫畢，遂圍
translation_en:
…an outstanding figure among the scholars.
Examiner Jin, Left Mentor, comments: “This is precisely the meaning of Hu’s Commentary.”
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: “Closely attuned to the commentary’s meaning, this composition stands far apart from the other submissions.”
The hegemon first led the feudal lords in fully performing the rites of honoring the king; he subsequently led them in punishing the offense of treating the king with disrespect. This merits praise. Thus, both the audiences at the king’s lodging and the siege of the state of Xu were worthy acts of a hegemon. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should commend them equally!
Now, in the closing years of our Duke Xi’s reign, Duke Wen of Jin exercised the hegemony. When he first convened the covenant at Jiantu, the Heavenly King made a journey to bestow his solicitude upon those below him; when the lords assembled again at Wen, the Heavenly King held his hunt at Heyang. The favor he showed Duke Wen was indeed unsurpassed. Could Wen, under these circumstances, show the slightest disrespect? Accordingly, he led the feudal lords in bowing before the royal countenance at close quarters; together with his fellow rulers, he promptly displayed the reverence due from a subject. The grand ceremonies of the two audiences were performed in succession at a time when royal authority languished; his steadfast loyalty repeatedly manifested itself in days when men’s hearts no longer acknowledged the duties of subjects. His regard for the source of the stream and the root of the tree was thereby made manifest, and the distinction between superior and inferior—as between cap and shoes—was again clarified. Although it may be said that the audiences were held in an improper place, the Son of Heaven was there, and the feudal lords went there to attend him: this was an adaptation of ritual to circumstance. Did it not resemble the intent of holding audiences at the sacred mountains of the several regions? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals twice records an audience at the king’s lodging, following the entries for Jiantu and Wen. This is why it gives its approval to Duke Wen of Jin.
As for Jiantu and Heyang, these were places near the state of Xu. Yet, when the feudal lords assembled twice, Xu made no appearance at all; and when two audiences were held at the king’s lodging, it did not dispatch even a single envoy. Its disrespect was extreme. Could Wen, under these circumstances, allow it the slightest indulgence? Accordingly, as soon as the audience ceremonies were concluded, he proceeded to lay siege…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其國都諸侯聿同大環其城邑罪有可聲非凌
弱暴寡之舉詞有可執非復讎報怨之師伯討
之義既伸尊王之功益大雖曰圍非美事而圍
許之役為王室計非為私也不亦庶幾貶爵削
地之意邪故春秋特書諸侯遂圍許於兩朝王
所之下其所以嘉晉文者以此噫尊王人臣之
大節也討罪天下之大法也晉文皆能舉之所
以繼桓之伯而世道賴以小康者其在此夫雖
然猶有未盡善者城濮勝楚俘不獻于王庭于
===
溫請狩則又以臣召君其可訓乎况圍許之役
亦假公義以濟私忿其名正而實譎迹雖是而
心則非矣春秋與之者盖亦為世道計有不得
已焉爾若夫三王之世則惡取此
晉韓厥帥師伐鄭仲孫蔑會齊崔杼曹人
邾人杞人次于郲襄公元年
周讓
同考試官教諭洪 批 此題聖人筆削大旨夫人
能言之而至於削楚救重在郲處知者甚少獨此深悉
punctuated:
其國都，諸侯聿同，大環其城邑。罪有可聲，非凌弱暴寡之舉；詞有可執，非復讎報怨之師。伯討之義既伸，尊王之功益大。雖曰圍非美事，而圍許之役，為王室計，非為私也，不亦庶幾貶爵削地之意邪？故春秋特書諸侯遂圍許於兩朝王所之下，其所以嘉晉文者以此。噫！尊王，人臣之大節也；討罪，天下之大法也。晉文皆能舉之，所以繼桓之伯，而世道賴以小康者，其在此夫！雖然，猶有未盡善者：城濮勝楚，俘不獻于王庭；于溫請狩，則又以臣召君，其可訓乎？况圍許之役，亦假公義以濟私忿，其名正而實譎，迹雖是而心則非矣。春秋與之者，盖亦為世道計，有不得已焉爾。若夫三王之世，則惡取此？
「晉韓厥帥師伐鄭，仲孫蔑會齊崔杼、曹人、邾人、杞人次于郲。」襄公元年。
周讓。
同考試官教諭洪批：此題聖人筆削大旨，夫人能言之，而至於削楚救、重在郲處，知者甚少。獨此深悉
translation_en:
…their capital. The assembled lords acted together, completely encircling its walls. There were crimes that could be publicly denounced: this was no act of bullying the weak or oppressing the few. There were defensible grounds for the action: this was no army bent on revenge or the settling of grievances. Once the righteousness of the hegemon’s punitive action had been vindicated, his achievement in honoring the king became still greater. Although a siege is no admirable undertaking, the siege of Xu was undertaken for the royal house, not for private interests. Did it not approximate the intent of reducing ranks and stripping away territory? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records, after the two audiences at the king’s lodging, that “the assembled lords thereupon besieged Xu.” This is why it commends Duke Wen of Jin. Ah! Honoring the king is a minister’s great duty; punishing wrongdoing is the great law of the realm. Duke Wen of Jin was able to uphold both. Surely herein lay the reason he succeeded Duke Huan as hegemon and brought a measure of peace to the world!
Nevertheless, there were still things that fell short of perfection. After defeating Chu at Chengpu, he did not present the captives at the royal court. At Wen, in requesting a royal hunt, he again acted as a subject summoning his sovereign. Could this serve as an example to follow? Moreover, in the siege of Xu, he also borrowed the authority of public righteousness to gratify private resentment. His action was correct in name but deceitful in substance; although his conduct appeared right, his motives were wrong. That the Spring and Autumn Annals approves him was also out of concern for the condition of the world: there was, in this, something unavoidable. In the age of the Three Kings, what use would there have been for such conduct?
“Han Jue of Jin led an army to attack Zheng. Zhongsun Mie joined Cui Zhu of Qi and men of Cao, Zhu, and Qi 杞, and they encamped at Lai.” First year of Duke Xiang.
Zhou Rang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, Instructor: Everyone can explain the general purport of the Sage’s inclusion and deletion of words in this topic. But very few understand the omission of Chu’s rescue and the weight placed on the words ‘at Lai.’ This essay alone understands in depth…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
傳意而辭尤雅健故録之
考試官左諭德靳批寫得書法意出
考試官學士江批得謹嚴之法
春秋紀内兵討罪見伯主所行放乎義削外兵
恤患見貳國所從背乎義考諸晉伐鄭而楚救
之春秋書伐書次不書救者意有在矣何則晉
自彭城討叛之餘命韓厥為伐鄭之舉揚其威
武撻其國都殆與楚子眞伐鄭等矣春秋紀之
見晉所行放乎義者何邪蓋鄭人棄中國而從
===
蠻夷助叛臣以迫君父此罪所當討而不可釋
者晉於斯時使其狃於速克亦奚足取今而韓
厥之師雖直抵于鄭諸侯之眾猶徐次于鄫整
兵慎戰不以斬馘執俘為功愛眾惜民不以好
攻樂殺為事晉之所行若此兵雖加鄭何足怪
哉春秋特書伐鄭次鄫者若曰鄭有可討之罪
晉得討罪之宜也所謂紀内兵討罪見伯主所
行放乎義者非以此歟然當韓厥伐鄭之日楚
子辛有救鄭之師解其倒懸拯其危急殆與晉
punctuated:
傳意，而辭尤雅健，故録之。

考試官左諭德靳批：寫得書法意出。

考試官學士江批：得謹嚴之法。

春秋紀内兵討罪，見伯主所行放乎義；削外兵恤患，見貳國所從背乎義。考諸晉伐鄭而楚救之，春秋書伐、書次、不書救者，意有在矣。何則？晉自彭城討叛之餘，命韓厥為伐鄭之舉，揚其威武，撻其國都，殆與楚子眞伐鄭等矣。春秋紀之，見晉所行放乎義者，何邪？蓋鄭人棄中國而從蠻夷，助叛臣以迫君父，此罪所當討而不可釋者。晉於斯時，使其狃於速克，亦奚足取？今而韓厥之師雖直抵于鄭，諸侯之眾猶徐次于鄫，整兵慎戰，不以斬馘執俘為功；愛眾惜民，不以好攻樂殺為事。晉之所行若此，兵雖加鄭，何足怪哉？春秋特書伐鄭、次鄫者，若曰鄭有可討之罪，晉得討罪之宜也。所謂紀内兵討罪，見伯主所行放乎義者，非以此歟？然當韓厥伐鄭之日，楚子辛有救鄭之師，解其倒懸，拯其危急，殆與晉
translation_en:
…the meaning of the commentary, and its language is especially elegant and vigorous; hence its inclusion.

Examiner Jin, Left Mentor, comments: “It brings out the intent behind the manner of recording.”

Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: “It achieves the method of careful precision and rigor.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals records the armies of the central states punishing wrongdoing, showing that the hegemon’s actions accorded with righteousness; it omits the relief of distress by an army from outside those states, showing that the allegiance chosen by the wavering state ran counter to righteousness. Consider Jin’s attack on Zheng and Chu’s rescue of it: the Annals records the attack and the encampment but does not record the rescue. There is a purpose in this. Why? After suppressing the rebellion at Pengcheng, Jin ordered Han Jue to undertake an attack on Zheng, displaying its military might and striking at Zheng’s capital. This was virtually the same as the ruler of Chu’s full-scale attack on Zheng. Why, then, does the Annals record it to show that Jin’s conduct accorded with righteousness? Because the people of Zheng had abandoned the central states to follow the barbarians, assisting rebellious ministers in bringing pressure upon their ruler and father. This was a crime that deserved punishment and could not be pardoned. Had Jin at this time become intent on easy, rapid conquest, what would there have been to commend? Yet although Han Jue’s army advanced directly to Zheng, the forces of the other lords still proceeded slowly and encamped at Zeng. They kept their troops in order and were cautious about battle, counting neither severed heads and ears nor captured prisoners as achievements. They cherished their troops and cared for the people, rather than devoting themselves to aggression and delighting in killing. Given such conduct by Jin, what was objectionable about its use of arms against Zheng? In expressly recording “attacked Zheng” and “encamped at Zeng,” the Annals was in effect saying that Zheng had committed a punishable offense and that Jin had punished it appropriately. Is this not what is meant by recording the armies of the central states punishing wrongdoing to show that the hegemon’s actions accorded with righteousness? Yet when Han Jue attacked Zheng, Zixin of Chu led an army to rescue Zheng, releasing it from its torment and saving it from imminent peril. This was virtually the same as Jin’s…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
卻缺救鄭同矣春秋削之見鄭所從背乎義者
何邪盖晉乃中國之伯楚實南蠻之強𢎞楚當
棄而晉所當從者鄭於斯時使能裁以大義夫
豈不可何乃懷中目之恩而忍心以背晉棄儀
衛之重而堅意以從夷私欲是徇下喬木而入
幽谷從違不審舎親暱而比豺狼鄭之所從若
此楚雖救鄭何足録哉春秋不書楚子辛救鄭
者若曰鄭無可救之善楚不得有能救之名也
所謂削外兵恤患見貳國所從背乎義者不以
===
是歟由是觀之聖人書法或顯或微一皆以義
為之權衡爾何嘗容心於其間哉抑鄭之從楚
固為有罪使晉自是以往修其德政以懷鄭使
之不叛助之守禦以保鄭使之不至於叛則盡
善矣奈何今日興師為虎牢之城明日出師為
虎牢之戍服鄭之道如是君子所以不能無憾
于悼公也雖然蕭魚之會推誠感鄭而鄭終為
晉有若悼公者又惡可盡非哉
禮記
punctuated:
卻缺救鄭同矣。春秋削之，見鄭所從背乎義者，何邪？盖晉乃中國之伯，楚實南蠻之強𢎞，楚當棄而晉所當從者。鄭於斯時，使能裁以大義，夫豈不可？何乃懷中目之恩，而忍心以背晉；棄儀衛之重，而堅意以從夷？私欲是徇，下喬木而入幽谷；從違不審，舎親暱而比豺狼。鄭之所從若此，楚雖救鄭，何足録哉？春秋不書楚子辛救鄭者，若曰：鄭無可救之善，楚不得有能救之名也。所謂削外兵恤患，見貳國所從背乎義者，不以是歟？由是觀之，聖人書法，或顯或微，一皆以義為之權衡爾，何嘗容心於其間哉？抑鄭之從楚，固為有罪；使晉自是以往，修其德政以懷鄭，使之不叛，助之守禦以保鄭，使之不至於叛，則盡善矣。奈何今日興師為虎牢之城，明日出師為虎牢之戍？服鄭之道如是，君子所以不能無憾于悼公也。雖然，蕭魚之會，推誠感鄭，而鄭終為晉有，若悼公者，又惡可盡非哉？

禮記
translation_en:
…was almost the same as Que Que’s rescue of Zheng. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals omit it, showing that Zheng’s choice of allegiance ran counter to righteousness? Jin was the hegemon of the central states, whereas Chu was a mighty power among the southern barbarians [?]. Chu was to be rejected, and Jin was the one to follow. Had Zheng at this time judged matters according to the great principles of righteousness, what could have prevented it from doing so? Why, then, did it cherish the kindness of Zhongmu [?] and harden its heart to turn its back on Jin, cast aside the importance of ceremonial safeguards, and firmly resolve to follow the barbarians? Pursuing only selfish desires, it descended from lofty trees into a dark ravine; failing to judge whom to follow and whom to reject, it abandoned its close kin and allied itself with jackals and wolves. Such being Zheng’s choice of allegiance, even though Chu rescued Zheng, what made that rescue worth recording? In not recording Zi Xin of Chu’s rescue of Zheng, the Spring and Autumn Annals seems to say: Zheng possessed no goodness that warranted rescue, and Chu could not be credited with having rescued it. Is this not what is meant by omitting an external army’s relief of distress to show that a state wavering between two allegiances had chosen contrary to righteousness?

Viewed in this light, the sage’s manner of recording events, whether explicit or subtle, takes righteousness alone as its measure. When did he ever allow personal bias to enter into it? Yet although Zheng was certainly culpable for following Chu, all would have been good had Jin thereafter cultivated its virtuous government to win Zheng’s allegiance and keep it from rebelling, and assisted its defenses to protect it and prevent it from being driven to rebellion. Why instead mobilize an army today to fortify Hulao, and dispatch troops tomorrow to garrison Hulao? That this was its method of bringing Zheng into submission explains why the gentleman cannot be without regret concerning Duke Dao. Nevertheless, at the meeting at Xiaoyu, he moved Zheng through his sincerity, and Zheng ultimately came under Jin’s sway. How, then, could someone such as Duke Dao be condemned in every respect?

Book of Rites

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
是天子□□□□□也故天子祭天地諸侯祭
社稷
趙聰
同考試官訓導袁批〔□□不過發明魯國郊祀之僭此作一本石梁王氏誌講深得本旨宜表而出之〕
考試官左諭德靳批〔明潔可誦〕
考試官學士江批〔得旨〕
聖人原二國遵先世之遺制必明以先王之定
制蓋杞宋二國皆王者之後宜世守其禮也然
===
不舉先王之定制以明之又何以見魯國之失
哉昔孔子適魯國而興嘆傷周道之寢微至此
謂夫杞之為國諸侯之國也杞而有郊若非禮
矣殊不知杞乃夏禹之後其先世勳勞不可廢
也故後世子孫得以世守天子之事以事其祖
禮所當然豈魯可得而比邪宋之為國亦諸侯
之國也宋而有郊似非禮矣殊不知宋乃殷契
之後其先世功德不可泯也故後世子孫得以
□遵先世之禮以祀其先禮所宜然豈魯可得
punctuated:
是天子□□□□□也，故天子祭天地，諸侯祭社稷。
趙聰。
同考試官訓導袁批〔□□不過發明魯國郊祀之僭，此作一本石梁王氏誌講，深得本旨，宜表而出之。〕
考試官左諭德靳批〔明潔可誦。〕
考試官學士江批〔得旨。〕
聖人原二國遵先世之遺制，必明以先王之定制。蓋杞宋二國皆王者之後，宜世守其禮也。然不舉先王之定制以明之，又何以見魯國之失哉？昔孔子適魯國而興嘆，傷周道之寢微至此。謂夫杞之為國，諸侯之國也。杞而有郊，若非禮矣。殊不知杞乃夏禹之後，其先世勳勞不可廢也，故後世子孫得以世守天子之事，以事其祖。禮所當然，豈魯可得而比邪？宋之為國，亦諸侯之國也。宋而有郊，似非禮矣。殊不知宋乃殷契之後，其先世功德不可泯也，故後世子孫得以□遵先世之禮，以祀其先。禮所宜然，豈魯可得
translation_en:
“This is the Son of Heaven’s [five illegible characters][?]. Therefore, the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; the feudal lords sacrifice to the gods of soil and grain.”

Zhao Cong.

Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔[Two illegible characters][?] merely elucidates Lu’s usurpation in performing the suburban sacrifice. This composition follows throughout the recorded lectures [?] of Master Wang of Shiliang, thoroughly grasps the underlying meaning, and deserves to be singled out and published.〕

Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher, comments: 〔Clear and polished, worthy of recitation.〕

Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: 〔Grasps the meaning.〕

The Sage, in explaining why the two states followed the institutions handed down by their ancestors, necessarily clarified the matter through the established institutions of the former kings. Both Qi and Song were descended from royal houses, and it was fitting that they should preserve their rites from generation to generation. Yet without adducing the established institutions of the former kings to clarify this, how could the fault of Lu be shown?

Formerly, Confucius went to Lu and sighed, lamenting that the Way of Zhou had declined to such a degree. As for Qi, it was a state ruled by a feudal lord. That Qi should perform the suburban sacrifice might seem contrary to ritual propriety. Yet this overlooks the fact that Qi descended from Yu of the Xia: the meritorious achievements of its ancestors could not be set aside. Thus their descendants in later generations were permitted to preserve the sacrificial observances of the Son of Heaven and use them to serve their ancestors. This was entirely appropriate according to ritual. How could Lu claim to be comparable?

Song was likewise a state ruled by a feudal lord. That Song should perform the suburban sacrifice might seem contrary to ritual propriety. Yet this overlooks the fact that Song descended from Xie of the Yin: the achievements and virtue of its ancestors could not be effaced. Thus their descendants in later generations were permitted to [one illegible character][?] follow their ancestors’ rites in sacrificing to their forebears. This was fitting according to ritual.
