title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而並邪且以周公所制定禮言之天子之有天
下其尊無對也故祭天于圓丘祭地于方澤惟
天子得以行之若乃諸侯一國之君但可祭其
國中所有社稷之神而已豈可上僭而行郊祭
之禮哉天子之臨四海其尊無上也故燔柴以
祭天瘞埋以祭地惟天子得以舉之若乃諸侯
一方之長但當祭其域中所有土穀之神而已
又豈可踰分而舉天地之祭哉吁聖人言此則
魯之不可以有郊也明矣雖然周公制禮作樂
爲萬世不易之典夫何傳之未久即有僭亂之
事而流弊遂至家臣僭大夫三桓僭魯魯僭天
子原其所以皆在成王賜伯禽天子禮樂中来
也孔子曰嗚呼哀哉我觀周道幽厲傷之他日
又曰禘自既灌而往者吾不欲觀之矣夫子之
言豈得已哉
是故君子貌足畏也色足憚也言足信也
趙煦
同考試官訓導袁批作者於足畏足憚足信
punctuated:
而並邪？且以周公所制定禮言之，天子之有天下，其尊無對也。故祭天于圓丘，祭地于方澤，惟天子得以行之。若乃諸侯，一國之君，但可祭其國中所有社稷之神而已，豈可上僭而行郊祭之禮哉？天子之臨四海，其尊無上也。故燔柴以祭天，瘞埋以祭地，惟天子得以舉之。若乃諸侯，一方之長，但當祭其域中所有土穀之神而已，又豈可踰分而舉天地之祭哉？吁！聖人言此，則魯之不可以有郊也明矣。雖然，周公制禮作樂，爲萬世不易之典，夫何傳之未久，即有僭亂之事，而流弊遂至家臣僭大夫，三桓僭魯，魯僭天子？原其所以，皆在成王賜伯禽天子禮樂中来也。孔子曰：「嗚呼哀哉！我觀周道，幽厲傷之。」他日又曰：「禘自既灌而往者，吾不欲觀之矣。」夫子之言，豈得已哉？

是故君子貌足畏也，色足憚也，言足信也。
趙煦

同考試官訓導袁批：作者於足畏、足憚、足信
translation_en:
…be ranked alongside it? Moreover, consider the rites established by the Duke of Zhou. As possessor of all under Heaven, the Son of Heaven has a dignity without equal. Thus, only the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound and to Earth at the Square Pool. A feudal lord, however, is ruler of a single state and may sacrifice only to the gods of soil and grain within that state. How could he usurp the prerogatives of his superior and perform the suburban sacrifice? As ruler of the Four Seas, the Son of Heaven has a dignity above all others. Thus, only the Son of Heaven may burn wood in sacrifice to Heaven and bury offerings in sacrifice to Earth. A feudal lord, however, is chief of a single region and should sacrifice only to the gods of soil and grain within his territory. How could he overstep his station and offer sacrifices to Heaven and Earth? Ah! From these words of the Sage, it is clear that Lu was not entitled to perform the suburban sacrifice. Yet the Duke of Zhou established rites and made music as immutable standards for all generations. How was it that, so soon after their transmission, acts of usurpation and disorder arose, their pernicious effects eventually extending to household retainers usurping the prerogatives of great officers, the three Huan lineages usurping those of the ruler of Lu, and Lu usurping those of the Son of Heaven? If we trace the cause, it all originated in King Cheng’s granting Bo Qin the rites and music of the Son of Heaven. Confucius said: “Alas, how grievous! When I contemplate the way of Zhou, I see that Kings You and Li damaged it.” On another occasion he said: “At the di sacrifice, from the point after the libation has been poured, I have no wish to watch.” Could the Master have refrained from saying these things?

“Therefore, the gentleman’s bearing is sufficient to inspire awe, his expression sufficient to inspire reverence, and his words sufficient to inspire trust.”
By Zhao Xu.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
處多不能發明獨此篇補叙整潔錄之以式學者
考試官左諭德靳批講畏憚信處不類眾作
考試官學士江批明暢可嘉
觀君子之自重起人情之同重蓋君子者為人
之表率也苟著于身者不自重焉何以起人之
同重哉表記記君子謹獨之功其驗如此謂夫
著于身者貌也貌焉不敬則失足於人而不足
畏矣君子不矜而莊則其貌之著也皆中規而
卒度故凡得於接見者必肅然興仰止之心懔
===
然動矜式之念不啻如神明之在上也曾有慢
易而不畏乎見于面者色也色焉不敬則失色
於人而不足憚矣君子不厲而威則其色之見
也皆輯柔而載令故凡得於觀瞻者惕然致恭
之不易悚然修敬之不遑不啻雷霆之在前也
曾有褻玩而不憚乎以至出諸口者非言乎言
焉不敬則失口於人而不足信矣君子不言而
信則其所發者皆有稽當理之言故凡得於聽
受者必服膺弗失尊之如筮龜書紳不忘守之
punctuated:
處，多不能發明，獨此篇補叙整潔，錄之以式學者。
考試官左諭德靳批：講畏、憚、信處，不類眾作。
考試官學士江批：明暢可嘉。
觀君子之自重，起人情之同重。蓋君子者，為人之表率也。苟著于身者不自重焉，何以起人之同重哉？《表記》記君子謹獨之功，其驗如此。謂夫著于身者，貌也。貌焉不敬，則失足於人而不足畏矣。君子不矜而莊，則其貌之著也，皆中規而卒度。故凡得於接見者，必肅然興仰止之心，懔然動矜式之念，不啻如神明之在上也。曾有慢易而不畏乎？見于面者，色也。色焉不敬，則失色於人而不足憚矣。君子不厲而威，則其色之見也，皆輯柔而載令。故凡得於觀瞻者，惕然致恭之不易，悚然修敬之不遑，不啻雷霆之在前也。曾有褻玩而不憚乎？以至出諸口者，非言乎？言焉不敬，則失口於人而不足信矣。君子不言而信，則其所發者，皆有稽當理之言。故凡得於聽受者，必服膺弗失，尊之如筮龜，書紳不忘，守之
translation_en:
…in these passages, most writers fail to elucidate the meaning. This essay alone supplies an orderly and polished exposition; it is included as a model for students.
Examiner Jin, Left Mentor, comments: Its discussion of awe, apprehension, and trust differs from the other compositions.
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: Clear and fluent; worthy of praise.
Observe how the gentleman’s respect for himself inspires others to respect him in turn. The gentleman serves as an example for others. If he shows no self-respect in what is manifested in his person, how can he inspire others to respect him? The chapter “Record of Exemplary Conduct” records the gentleman’s achievement in watchfulness over himself when alone; its effects are evident in this way. What is manifested in his person is his bearing. If his bearing lacks reverence, he will make a false step before others and fail to inspire awe. The gentleman is dignified without being self-important; thus his outward bearing conforms to the compass and accords fully with the measure [?]. All who meet him therefore solemnly feel the desire to look up to him, and with awe conceive the wish to take him as their model, as though a divine presence were above them. Could anyone treat him casually and slightingly, without awe?
What appears upon his face is his expression. If his expression lacks reverence, he will lose his composure before others and fail to inspire apprehension. The gentleman possesses authority without being severe; thus his expression is invariably gentle and good. All who behold him remain alert and constant in their deference, and attend to their reverence with a trembling urgency, as though thunder were immediately before them. Could anyone treat him with disrespectful familiarity, without apprehension?
And what issues from his mouth—is it not speech? If his speech lacks reverence, he will misspeak before others and fail to inspire trust. The gentleman commands trust without speaking; thus whatever he utters consists of words grounded in evidence and consonant with principle. All who hear and receive them necessarily cherish them in their hearts without losing them, revere them like divination by milfoil and tortoise shell, write them upon their sashes so as not to forget them, and observe them…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
如四時又何有疑貳而不信者我是則君子之
貌之色之言自然見重於人也如此非慎獨而
自重也疇克爾耶雖然貌難於足畏色難於足
憚而言難於足信君子尋常敬忌故於動處無
不中節有不期然而然者矣曾子告孟敬子曰
君子所貴乎道者三與此正相合然則君子脩
身之要舍是無他術矣
第貳場
論
===
天地之帥吾其性
張璿
同考試官教諭姜 批 西銘一篇横渠文之極純
粹者而此一語又篇中之要旨也子能發揮奧妙曲盡無遺
殆未可以場屋時文目之也健羡
同考試官教授王 批 此題士子多知之至能根
據程朱論議不為險恠浮艷語而文自工僅見此篇
考試官左諭德靳 批 能表出子厚不愧屋漏為無忝
存心養性為匪懈二語為事天工夫此其尤過人者
punctuated:
如四時，又何有疑貳而不信者我？是則君子之貌、之色、之言，自然見重於人也如此，非慎獨而自重也，疇克爾耶？雖然，貌難於足畏，色難於足憚，而言難於足信。君子尋常敬忌，故於動處無不中節，有不期然而然者矣。曾子告孟敬子曰：「君子所貴乎道者三。」與此正相合。然則君子脩身之要，舍是無他術矣。
第貳場
論
天地之帥吾其性
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批：「西銘一篇，横渠文之極純粹者，而此一語又篇中之要旨也。子能發揮奧妙，曲盡無遺，殆未可以場屋時文目之也。健羡。」
同考試官教授王批：「此題士子多知之，至能根據程朱論議，不為險恠浮艷語，而文自工，僅見此篇。」
考試官左諭德靳批：「能表出子厚『不愧屋漏為無忝，存心養性為匪懈』二語，為事天工夫，此其尤過人者。」
translation_en:
…as they do the four seasons. How, then, could anyone harbor doubts and withhold trust [?]? Thus the gentleman’s bearing, expression, and words naturally command such respect from others. Without being watchful over himself when alone and maintaining self-respect, who could achieve this? Yet it is difficult to make one’s bearing worthy of awe, one’s expression worthy of reverence, and one’s words worthy of trust. Because the gentleman is habitually reverent and wary, every action accords with the proper measure; this happens naturally, without his deliberately seeking it. Zengzi told Meng Jingzi: “There are three things that the gentleman values in the Way.” This accords precisely with what has been said here. Thus, as to the essentials of the gentleman’s self-cultivation, there is no other method besides this.
Second Session
Discourse
“That which commands Heaven and Earth is my nature.”
Zhang Xuan
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The Western Inscription is among the purest of Hengqu’s writings, and this particular phrase expresses an essential point of the piece. You have expounded its profound subtleties, exploring every aspect without omission. This can hardly be regarded merely as a conventional examination essay. Most admirable [?].”
Associate Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “Many candidates know this topic, but this is the only essay I have seen that grounds its discussion in Cheng and Zhu, avoids strained, bizarre, superficial, or ornate language, and nevertheless achieves literary excellence naturally.”
Examiner Jin, Left Mentor, comments: “He is able to bring out Zihou’s two statements—that ‘to feel no shame even in the secluded recesses of one’s room is to bring no dishonor,’ and that ‘to preserve one’s mind and nurture one’s nature is to be unremitting’—as the work of serving Heaven. This is where he particularly surpasses others.”

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官學士江批西銘發前賢所未發此論蓋
亦能發張子所未發者歟
論曰人至微也而與天地並大者蓋必得天地
之理以為性焉人之所以為人者非以其有是
性乎天地之所以為天地而父母乎萬物者非
以其有是理乎天地無是理則無以主乎萬化
吾人無是性則無以參乎三才故理之與氣雖
不能相無而理其主也噫天地之帥天地之理
之所在也而吾人之性原其所自實得於是則
===
在天地者非有餘在吾人者非不足一而已矣
此吾人所以混然中處於兩間而並大也與張
子作西銘有曰天地之帥吾其性吾于此一言
蓋有以窺見夫古人事天之心矣其所以參天
地賛化育以極夫功用之大者豈有所強於外
哉固曰自盡其性以求無忝于天地而已矣雖
然鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂天地無心者也而
何以帥言哉孔子曰天地之大德曰生又曰復
其見天地之心則是天地雖無心而亦有無心
punctuated:
考試官學士江批：西銘發前賢所未發，此論蓋亦能發張子所未發者歟！

論曰：人至微也，而與天地並大者，蓋必得天地之理以為性焉。人之所以為人者，非以其有是性乎？天地之所以為天地而父母乎萬物者，非以其有是理乎？天地無是理，則無以主乎萬化；吾人無是性，則無以參乎三才。故理之與氣，雖不能相無，而理其主也。噫！天地之帥，天地之理之所在也，而吾人之性，原其所自，實得於是，則在天地者非有餘，在吾人者非不足，一而已矣。此吾人所以混然中處於兩間而並大也與！張子作《西銘》，有曰：「天地之帥，吾其性。」吾于此一言，蓋有以窺見夫古人事天之心矣。其所以參天地、賛化育，以極夫功用之大者，豈有所強於外哉？固曰自盡其性，以求無忝于天地而已矣。雖然，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂，天地無心者也，而何以帥言哉？孔子曰：「天地之大德曰生。」又曰：「復，其見天地之心。」則是天地雖無心，而亦有無心
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: “The Western Inscription brings to light what earlier worthies had not brought to light. Might this discourse likewise bring to light what Master Zhang himself had not?”

The discourse reads: Human beings are exceedingly small, yet they equal Heaven and Earth in greatness, surely because they receive the principle of Heaven and Earth as their nature. Is it not possession of this nature that makes human beings human? Is it not possession of this principle that makes Heaven and Earth what they are, and enables them to act as father and mother to the myriad things? Without this principle, Heaven and Earth would have nothing with which to govern the myriad transformations; without this nature, we human beings would have nothing with which to stand alongside them among the Three Powers. Thus, although principle and material force cannot exist without one another, principle is their ruler. Ah! What commands Heaven and Earth is where their principle resides. Tracing our human nature to its source, we find that it is indeed received from this. Thus, what is in Heaven and Earth is not more abundant, nor is what is in us deficient: it is one and the same. This is why we dwell in integral unity between Heaven and Earth and equal them in greatness!

When Master Zhang composed the Western Inscription, he said: “What commands Heaven and Earth is my nature.” In this one saying I can glimpse the mind with which the ancients served Heaven. In standing alongside Heaven and Earth and assisting their transforming and nourishing activity, thereby realizing the utmost greatness of their efficacy, did they force anything upon themselves from outside? It was simply a matter of fully realizing their own nature, seeking thereby not to disgrace Heaven and Earth.

Nevertheless, Heaven and Earth stir the myriad things into activity without sharing the sage’s concerns: they have no conscious intention. Why, then, speak of a commander? Confucius said: “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life.” He also said: “In Return, we may see the mind of Heaven and Earth.” Thus, although Heaven and Earth have no conscious intention, they nevertheless also possess a mind without conscious intention…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之心者矣維天之命於穆不已謂其一無主宰
者於其間可乎使無主宰者於其間則四時之
行有時而紊矣五行之布有時而忒矣庶類萬
物之生有時而息矣天地其何以為天地而父
母乎萬物邪然所謂天地之帥者何也天地之
心是也夫天地之心一而其性情則不同焉乾
健坤順者是也天地之性情一而其為德則不
同焉元亨利貞者是也德之所具曰心心之所
之曰志志也者非天地之帥而主宰乎天地之
===
塞者乎是故溫而春萬物生焉炎而夏萬物長
焉其生其長氣也而必有所以生之長之者孰
主張是元亨為之也肅而秋萬物收焉寒而冬
萬物藏焉其收其藏氣也而必有所以收之藏
之者孰綱維是利貞為之也蓋其理則謂之道
其用則謂之神其體則謂之易其主宰則謂之
帝其生生不已則謂之仁其實一也其實一天
地之心也不離於陰陽而亦不雜於陰陽不外
於陰陽而亦不倚於陰陽噫此固天地之所以
punctuated: 之心者矣。「維天之命，於穆不已」，謂其一無主宰者於其間，可乎？使無主宰者於其間，則四時之行有時而紊矣，五行之布有時而忒矣，庶類萬物之生有時而息矣。天地其何以為天地而父母乎萬物邪？然所謂天地之帥者何也？天地之心是也。夫天地之心一，而其性情則不同焉，乾健坤順者是也。天地之性情一，而其為德則不同焉，元亨利貞者是也。德之所具曰心，心之所之曰志。志也者，非天地之帥而主宰乎天地之塞者乎？是故溫而春，萬物生焉；炎而夏，萬物長焉。其生其長，氣也，而必有所以生之長之者。孰主張是？元亨為之也。肅而秋，萬物收焉；寒而冬，萬物藏焉。其收其藏，氣也，而必有所以收之藏之者。孰綱維是？利貞為之也。蓋其理則謂之道，其用則謂之神，其體則謂之易，其主宰則謂之帝，其生生不已則謂之仁，其實一也。其實一，天地之心也。不離於陰陽而亦不雜於陰陽，不外於陰陽而亦不倚於陰陽。噫！此固天地之所以
translation_en:
…a heart nonetheless. “The mandate of Heaven—how profound, and unceasing!” Can one say that there is no governing agency whatsoever within it? Were there no governing agency within it, the succession of the four seasons would sometimes fall into disorder, the deployment of the Five Phases would sometimes go awry, and the generation of the myriad things in all their kinds would sometimes cease. How, then, could Heaven and Earth constitute Heaven and Earth and act as father and mother to the myriad things? What, then, is meant by the commander of Heaven and Earth? It is the heart of Heaven and Earth. The heart of Heaven and Earth is one, yet their natures and dispositions differ: Qian is vigorous, and Kun is yielding. The nature and disposition of Heaven and Earth are one, yet their virtues differ: these are origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy. That in which virtue resides is called the heart; that toward which the heart moves is called the will. Is this will not the commander of Heaven and Earth, governing what fills Heaven and Earth?

Thus, with warmth comes spring, and the myriad things are born; with heat comes summer, and the myriad things grow. Their birth and growth are the workings of vital force, yet there must be that which causes them to be born and to grow. What directs this? Origination and flourishing do so. With severity comes autumn, and the myriad things are gathered in; with cold comes winter, and the myriad things are stored away. Their gathering and storing are the workings of vital force, yet there must be that which causes them to be gathered and stored. What orders this? Benefit and constancy do so. In respect of its principle, it is called the Way; in respect of its operation, it is called the numinous; in respect of its constitutive substance, it is called Change; in respect of its governance, it is called the Lord on High; in respect of its ceaseless generation of life, it is called benevolence. In reality, these are one. This single reality is the heart of Heaven and Earth. It is inseparable from yin and yang, yet is not mingled with yin and yang; it is not outside yin and yang, yet neither does it depend upon yin and yang. Ah! This is indeed that by which Heaven and Earth…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
為天地而父母乎萬物者與夫天地之所以為
天地者既在於是則吾人之所以為人者又能
外於是邪何也天地固吾人之父母也吾人固
天地之子也父子不可以為二氣則吾人之於
天地獨可以為二理乎哉天地之帥其為吾人
之性也亦明矣何者性也者與生俱生者也具
于吾心而宰乎吾身者也四端由是而出五典
由是而行萬事萬物之理由是而統蓋亦吾人
一身之帥也而謂非天地之帥而可乎是故天
===
地有是志吾亦有是志其心一也天地有是健
順吾亦有是健順其性情一也天地有是元亨
利貞吾亦有是仁義禮智其四德一也吾之以
仁而愛也非即天地之以元而生邪吾之以禮
而讓也非即天地之以亨而長邪吾之以義而
惡也非即天地之以利而收邪吾之以知而知
也非即天地之以貞而藏邪吾之貫古今塞宇
宙而無所不有也非即天地之所以為大者邪
是故粹然其至善也在天地者與在我者同不
punctuated: 為天地而父母乎萬物者與！夫天地之所以為天地者既在於是，則吾人之所以為人者又能外於是邪？何也？天地固吾人之父母也，吾人固天地之子也。父子不可以為二氣，則吾人之於天地獨可以為二理乎哉？天地之帥，其為吾人之性也亦明矣。何者？性也者，與生俱生者也，具于吾心而宰乎吾身者也。四端由是而出，五典由是而行，萬事萬物之理由是而統，蓋亦吾人一身之帥也，而謂非天地之帥而可乎？是故天地有是志，吾亦有是志，其心一也；天地有是健順，吾亦有是健順，其性情一也；天地有是元亨利貞，吾亦有是仁義禮智，其四德一也。吾之以仁而愛也，非即天地之以元而生邪？吾之以禮而讓也，非即天地之以亨而長邪？吾之以義而惡也，非即天地之以利而收邪？吾之以知而知也，非即天地之以貞而藏邪？吾之貫古今、塞宇宙而無所不有也，非即天地之所以為大者邪？是故粹然其至善也，在天地者與在我者同不
translation_en:
…be Heaven and Earth and act as parents to the myriad things! Since what makes Heaven and Earth Heaven and Earth lies in this, can what makes us human lie outside it? Why is this so? Heaven and Earth are indeed our parents, and we are indeed their children. Father and son cannot be regarded as having two separate vital energies; could we alone, in relation to Heaven and Earth, be regarded as having two separate principles? It is also clear that the governing principle of Heaven and Earth constitutes our human nature. Why? Our nature is what is born together with us, inherent in our hearts and governing our persons. From it emerge the four moral sprouts; through it the five cardinal relationships are put into practice; under it the principles of all affairs and things are brought together. It is thus also the governing principle of each person's entire being. How could one say that it is not the governing principle of Heaven and Earth?
Thus, Heaven and Earth possess this purpose, and I too possess this purpose: their heart and mine are one. Heaven and Earth possess this vigor and compliance, and I too possess this vigor and compliance: their nature and dispositions and mine are one. Heaven and Earth possess origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy (yuan, heng, li, zhen), and I too possess benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom: their four virtues and mine are one. When I love through benevolence, is this not precisely Heaven and Earth's bringing forth life through origination? When I yield through ritual propriety, is this not precisely Heaven and Earth's nurturing growth through flourishing? When I abhor through righteousness, is this not precisely Heaven and Earth's gathering in through benefit? When I understand through wisdom, is this not precisely Heaven and Earth's storing away through constancy? When I extend throughout past and present and fill the universe, encompassing everything, is this not precisely what makes Heaven and Earth great? Thus, in the purity of its utmost goodness, what is in Heaven and Earth and what is in me alike cannot…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
可得而雜也渾然其至誠也在天地者與在我
者同不可得而貳也廓然其至公也在天地者
與在我者同不可得而私也何也性同故也夫
性同而卒有不同者氣質殽之而自小耳豈性
之本然哉信矣夫天地非有餘吾人非不足也
大哉性乎其萬物之一原者乎故自已而推之
於人人之性與我同也使有不同焉途人不可
以為禹眾人不可以為堯舜矣自人而推之物
物之性其初與我同也使有不同焉虎狼無父
===
子蜂蟻無君臣豺獺無報本之義矣是豈有我
者之得私哉由是論之則吾人為天地之子而
並大於兩間昭昭也故曰乾稱父坤稱母予兹
藐焉乃混然中處又曰民吾同胞物吾與也嗚
呼盡之矣雖然吾人為天地之子固也而所以
事天者可無道乎亦曰自盡其性而已不然天
固與之吾固棄之天固全之吾固虧之是所謂
悖德之子之類也是不克肖乎天地者也善事
其天者肯如是乎必也推親親之厚以大無我
punctuated:
可得而雜也。渾然其至誠也，在天地者與在我者同，不可得而貳也。廓然其至公也，在天地者與在我者同，不可得而私也。何也？性同故也。夫性同而卒有不同者，氣質殽之而自小耳，豈性之本然哉？信矣夫，天地非有餘，吾人非不足也。大哉性乎！其萬物之一原者乎！故自已而推之於人，人之性與我同也。使有不同焉，途人不可以為禹，眾人不可以為堯舜矣。自人而推之物，物之性其初與我同也。使有不同焉，虎狼無父子，蜂蟻無君臣，豺獺無報本之義矣。是豈有我者之得私哉？由是論之，則吾人為天地之子，而並大於兩間，昭昭也。故曰：「乾稱父，坤稱母，予兹藐焉，乃混然中處。」又曰：「民吾同胞，物吾與也。」嗚呼！盡之矣！

雖然，吾人為天地之子固也，而所以事天者，可無道乎？亦曰自盡其性而已。不然，天固與之，吾固棄之；天固全之，吾固虧之。是所謂悖德之子之類也，是不克肖乎天地者也。善事其天者肯如是乎？必也推親親之厚，以大無我
translation_en:
…cannot be adulterated. In its undivided, utmost sincerity, what is in Heaven and Earth is the same as what is in me: it cannot be divided. In its all-embracing, utmost impartiality, what is in Heaven and Earth is the same as what is in me: it cannot be made selfish. Why? Because the nature is the same. Though the nature is the same, differences ultimately arise because the material endowment confounds it and people diminish themselves. How could this be the nature in its original condition? Truly, Heaven and Earth have no surplus, and we human beings have no deficiency. How great is the nature! Is it not the single source of all things? Thus, extending from oneself to other people, their nature is the same as mine. Were there a difference, a passerby could not become Yu, and ordinary people could not become Yao or Shun. Extending from people to other creatures, their nature at its origin is the same as mine. Were there a difference, tigers and wolves would have no bond between father and offspring, bees and ants no bond between ruler and minister, and jackals and otters no sense of the duty to repay their source. How could this be something that those possessed of a self may claim exclusively? Viewed in this way, it is perfectly clear that we human beings are the children of Heaven and Earth and stand alongside them in greatness between the two. Thus it is said: “Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother; I, small as I am, dwell in their midst, one with them.” It is also said: “The people are my siblings, and other creatures are my companions.” Ah! This says it all!

Nevertheless, though we are indeed the children of Heaven and Earth, can there be no proper way to serve Heaven? It is simply to fulfill one's own nature. Otherwise, what Heaven has bestowed, we discard; what Heaven has made whole, we impair. This is to belong to the class of those called children who violate virtue; it is to fail to resemble Heaven and Earth. Would someone who serves Heaven well be willing to act thus? Surely one must extend the depth of affection for one's own kin to enlarge selflessness…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之公因事親之誠以盡事天之道神明之德□
其窮之以吾父母之志所當繼也變化之道我
其知之以吾父母之事所當述也以天下為一
家以中國為一人而匹夫匹婦惟恐有一之不
得其所者以民吾同胞皆吾父母之所愛也取
之有時用之有節而一草木一鳥獸惟恐不若
其性者以物吾黨與皆吾父母之心之所恤也
極樂天踐形之妙以至於沒身而無一行之不
慊者吾父母全而生之吾不可不全而歸之也
===
是不曰天地克肖之子而何哉噫事天至此語
其道則王語其德則聖矣然亦豈有加於吾性
之外哉西銘之作大率覺天下不知性者之梏
于自小也夫天下之言性者亦眾矣而未有及
於此者張子殆發前聖之所未發者歟雖然中
庸不云乎惟天下至誠為能盡其性能盡其性
則能盡人物之性而可與天地參矣此固西銘
之所自出也此固張子之所以能紹子思之傳
也或乃疑其言之大高遠而難入者則張子蓋
punctuated: 之公，因事親之誠，以盡事天之道。神明之德，□其窮之，以吾父母之志所當繼也；變化之道，我其知之，以吾父母之事所當述也。以天下為一家，以中國為一人，而匹夫匹婦，惟恐有一之不得其所者，以民吾同胞，皆吾父母之所愛也。取之有時，用之有節，而一草木、一鳥獸，惟恐不若其性者，以物吾黨與，皆吾父母之心之所恤也。極樂天踐形之妙，以至於沒身而無一行之不慊者，吾父母全而生之，吾不可不全而歸之也。是不曰天地克肖之子而何哉！噫！事天至此，語其道則王，語其德則聖矣。然亦豈有加於吾性之外哉？《西銘》之作，大率覺天下不知性者之梏于自小也。夫天下之言性者亦眾矣，而未有及於此者，張子殆發前聖之所未發者歟？雖然，《中庸》不云乎：「惟天下至誠，為能盡其性；能盡其性，則能盡人物之性，而可與天地參矣。」此固《西銘》之所自出也，此固張子之所以能紹子思之傳也。或乃疑其言之大、高遠而難入者，則張子蓋
translation_en:
…the impartiality that embraces all without selfishness, and, through sincerity in serving one’s parents, fully realize the Way of serving Heaven. As for the virtue of spiritual illumination, [□: illegible, ?] fathom it, for the aspirations of our father and mother must be carried on; as for the Way of transformation, I must understand it, for the undertakings of our father and mother must be continued. Regard all under Heaven as one family and the Central Kingdom as one person, fearing only that even a single ordinary man or woman may fail to find their proper place: the people are our siblings, all beloved by our father and mother. Take things at the proper times and use them with restraint, fearing only that even a single plant or tree, bird or beast may not flourish according to its nature: other beings are our companions, all objects of our father and mother’s concern. Fully realize the subtle perfection of delighting in Heaven and fulfilling one’s bodily form, so that until death not a single action leaves one dissatisfied: our father and mother brought us into being whole, and we must return whole.

If such a person is not called a child who worthily resembles Heaven and Earth, what else could one call them? Ah! When serving Heaven reaches this point, in terms of the Way one is a king, and in terms of virtue one is a sage. Yet how could this add anything beyond our own nature? The Western Inscription (Ximing) was written chiefly to awaken those throughout the world who do not understand their nature and are fettered by belittling themselves. Many in the world have spoken about human nature, yet none have reached this point. Did Master Zhang perhaps reveal what the earlier sages had not revealed? Yet does the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) not say: “Only one of utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his nature; if he can fully realize his nature, he can fully realize the natures of people and other beings, and can form a triad with Heaven and Earth”? This is indeed the source of the Western Inscription; this is indeed how Master Zhang was able to carry on Zisi’s transmitted teaching. Should anyone doubt his words because they are vast, lofty, remote, and difficult to enter into, Master Zhang has indeed …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
言之矣所謂存心養性為匪懈者即子思戒慎
恐懼之意靜而存養之功也所謂不媿屋漏為
無忝者即子思慎獨之意動而省察之功也是
皆盡性之要而學者可為之事也何高遠之有
嗟夫其大至於與天地並而其實則不外乎一
心此吾聖賢之學所以異乎異端之徒也事天
者毋于吾性之外求之
表
擬宋儒臣葉采進近思錄集解表〔淳祐十二年〕
===
楊灝
同考試官教諭鄒批周程張四子微言盡在
此書其所以上接孟氏之傳者表能道之是用錄出
同考試官教諭王批温純典雅作表者當如此
考試官左諭德靳批得儒臣進書體
考試官學士江批其間議論甚有關涉不獨駢儷
之工也
伏以
真儒鳴道遠承洙泗之傳
punctuated:
言之矣。所謂存心養性為匪懈者，即子思戒慎恐懼之意，靜而存養之功也；所謂不媿屋漏為無忝者，即子思慎獨之意，動而省察之功也。是皆盡性之要，而學者可為之事也，何高遠之有？嗟夫！其大至於與天地並，而其實則不外乎一心。此吾聖賢之學所以異乎異端之徒也。事天者，毋于吾性之外求之。

表
擬宋儒臣葉采進近思錄集解表〔淳祐十二年〕
楊灝

同考試官教諭鄒批：「周程張四子微言，盡在此書。其所以上接孟氏之傳者，表能道之，是用錄出。」
同考試官教諭王批：「温純典雅，作表者當如此。」
考試官左諭德靳批：「得儒臣進書體。」
考試官學士江批：「其間議論甚有關涉，不獨駢儷之工也。」

伏以，真儒鳴道，遠承洙泗之傳，
translation_en:
…has spoken of this. What he calls “preserving the mind and nourishing the nature” as the way to be unremitting expresses Zisi’s meaning of vigilance and apprehension: it is the work of preservation and nourishment in stillness. What he calls “feeling no shame in the secluded chamber” as the way to remain without dishonor expresses Zisi’s meaning of watchfulness when alone: it is the work of reflection and scrutiny in activity. These are all essentials for fully realizing one’s nature, and things that learners can put into practice. What is lofty or remote about them? Ah! In its greatness, this learning reaches the point of standing alongside Heaven and Earth, yet in its substance it does not extend beyond the single mind. This is what distinguishes the learning of our sages and worthies from that of the followers of heterodox teachings. Those who serve Heaven must not seek it outside their own nature.

Memorial
A memorial composed in the voice of the Song scholarly official Ye Cai, submitting Collected Explanations of Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu jijie). 〔Twelfth year of Chunyou [1252]〕
By Yang Hao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: “The subtle teachings of the four masters—Zhou, the two Chengs, and Zhang—are all contained in this book. This memorial succeeds in explaining how they carried forward the transmission from Master Meng. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Gentle, pure, classically poised, and elegant: this is how a memorial should be written.”
Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: “It captures the proper form for a scholarly official’s presentation of a book.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: “The arguments within it have considerable bearing on the subject; its merit is not confined to skill in parallel prose.”

I humbly submit that true Confucian scholars give voice to the Way, carrying forward the distant transmission of the Zhu and Si rivers [the teaching of Confucius]…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
明主右文兼録芻蕘之善謹齋心而進
御敢稽首以颺言竊惟治道之隆汙寔本斯
文之興廢蓋由周公而上皇極建則俗美
治隆慨自孟氏以還正學湮則經殘教弛
異端並起大義漸乖逮更煨燼之餘益失
源流之正漢師章句訓詁徒勤唐重詞華
支離彌甚譬之羣飲寧知河海之深如彼
墻窺孰見室家之好心法不傳于正脉治
功僅見于小康理有固然無足異者天開
===
皇宋星集文奎
聖聖相承始復唐虞之治
明明繼照式張周孔之規于是濂溪倡絶學于
先伊洛闡微言于後道統復續人文載光
顧山木之巳頹幸簡編之未泯紫陽繼出
獨號儒宗東萊並興雅稱同志因寒泉精
舍之會啓圖書集傳之藏謂其廣大淵深
不免望洋之嘆掇其精純簡要用為行遠
之基乃就此書庸示来哲猶懼外馳而無
punctuated:
明主右文，兼録芻蕘之善。謹齋心而進御，敢稽首以颺言。竊惟治道之隆汙，寔本斯文之興廢。蓋由周公而上，皇極建則俗美治隆；慨自孟氏以還，正學湮則經殘教弛。異端並起，大義漸乖。逮更煨燼之餘，益失源流之正。漢師章句，訓詁徒勤；唐重詞華，支離彌甚。譬之羣飲，寧知河海之深？如彼墻窺，孰見室家之好？心法不傳于正脉，治功僅見于小康。理有固然，無足異者。
天開皇宋，星集文奎。聖聖相承，始復唐虞之治；明明繼照，式張周孔之規。于是濂溪倡絶學于先，伊洛闡微言于後，道統復續，人文載光。顧山木之巳頹，幸簡編之未泯。紫陽繼出，獨號儒宗；東萊並興，雅稱同志。因寒泉精舍之會，啓圖書集傳之藏。謂其廣大淵深，不免望洋之嘆；掇其精純簡要，用為行遠之基。乃就此書，庸示来哲。猶懼外馳而無
translation_en:
…An enlightened ruler honors learning and also accepts worthy counsel from humble woodcutters. Reverently purifying our hearts, we submit this work for imperial inspection; bowing our heads, we venture to proclaim our thoughts. We humbly consider that the flourishing or decline of government rests fundamentally upon the rise or fall of this cultural tradition. From the Duke of Zhou back to earlier times, the establishment of the sovereign standard brought admirable customs and flourishing government. Alas, since Mengzi, the obscuring of orthodox learning has left the classics damaged and moral instruction neglected. Heterodox teachings arose together, and the great principles were gradually distorted. After the ravages of the burning of the books, the correct course of the tradition was still further lost. Han teachers labored fruitlessly over textual divisions and glosses; Tang scholars prized literary ornament, and fragmentation grew still worse. Like people drinking together, how could they know the depths of rivers and seas? Like those peering over a wall, who among them could see the beauty of the buildings within? The teachings of the mind were not transmitted through the orthodox lineage, and achievements in government amounted only to modest order. This followed necessarily from the circumstances and gives no cause for surprise.
Heaven inaugurated the august Song, and stars gathered in Kui, the constellation of literary culture. Sage rulers succeeded one another, at last restoring the government of Tang Yao and Yu Shun; enlightened sovereigns shone in succession, extending the exemplary rules of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. Thus Lianxi first revived the learning whose transmission had been broken, and the masters of Yi and Luo subsequently elucidated its subtle teachings. The succession of the Way was renewed, and human culture shone once more. Though the great trees of the mountains had already fallen—the masters had died—fortunately their writings had not disappeared. Ziyang then emerged, uniquely acclaimed as the foremost Confucian master; Donglai arose alongside him, long esteemed as a kindred spirit. Meeting at the Hanquan Retreat, they opened their stores of books, collected writings, and commentaries. Considering these so vast and profound that readers could scarcely avoid sighing as before a boundless ocean, they selected what was most refined, lucid, concise, and essential to provide a foundation for the long journey ahead. They thereby compiled this book to instruct worthy scholars yet to come. Still they feared that readers would pursue external things and fail to…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
得因掲近思以為名凡求端用力之方與
處己治人之法佛老之所以害正賢聖之
所以殊途體用兼該巨細畢舉既非博而
寡要寧至勞而少功事理則本之目前一
開卷而可盡治道亦運之掌上不下帶而
自存故四子寔階梯乎六經而是編又權
輿乎四子信斯言也豈欺我哉然本其親
汗竹之心恐亦有獻食芹之意祗緣命蹇
遂與願違臣何人斯乃蒙採納幼雖受讀
===
欲逃買櫝之譏晚若粗通終負斲輪之媿
妄成集解自備遺忘旁通實得之諸家大
旨則仍乎舊註廿年勤苦一旦遭逢揣己
非榮于時是慶兹盖伏遇
惟睿作聖自誠而明恊于
帝以重華取諸人而為善登祀五賢于孔廟理
學益明表章四書于虞庠百家盡掃盖已
大行其蘊豈特虛奨其人而臣適萃成編
冒塵
punctuated:
得，因掲近思以為名。凡求端用力之方與處己治人之法，佛老之所以害正、賢聖之所以殊途，體用兼該，巨細畢舉。既非博而寡要，寧至勞而少功？事理則本之目前，一開卷而可盡；治道亦運之掌上，不下帶而自存。故四子寔階梯乎六經，而是編又權輿乎四子。信斯言也，豈欺我哉？然本其親汗竹之心，恐亦有獻食芹之意。祗緣命蹇，遂與願違。臣何人斯，乃蒙採納？幼雖受讀，欲逃買櫝之譏；晚若粗通，終負斲輪之媿。妄成集解，自備遺忘。旁通實得之諸家，大旨則仍乎舊註。廿年勤苦，一旦遭逢，揣己非榮，于時是慶。
兹盖伏遇惟睿作聖，自誠而明，恊于帝以重華，取諸人而為善。登祀五賢于孔廟，理學益明；表章四書于虞庠，百家盡掃。盖已大行其蘊，豈特虛奨其人？而臣適萃成編，冒塵
translation_en:
…attain anything, they therefore chose “Reflections on Things Near at Hand” (Jinsi) as its title. It encompasses methods for finding a starting point and applying oneself, rules for governing oneself and others, the ways in which Buddhism and Daoism harm the orthodox teaching, and the different paths of worthies and sages. It embraces both substance and function and covers matters great and small. Since it is neither sprawling nor lacking in essentials, how could studying it require much labor for little result? The principles of affairs are grounded in what lies immediately before us: opening the book is enough to comprehend them all. The Way of government, too, can be wielded in the palm of one’s hand; without leaving one’s place, it is already present. Thus the four masters truly provide steps leading to the Six Classics, while this compilation provides an introduction to the four masters. These words are surely true; how could they deceive me? Yet, considering the intention behind their personally committing it to writing, I suspect they also wished to offer their humble fare of celery to the ruler. Because their fortunes were adverse, events ran contrary to their wishes. Who am I, your servant, to have my work accepted?
Although I received instruction in reading it when young, I wished to escape the reproach of buying the casket and discarding the pearl. Though in later years I may have gained a rough understanding, I still bear the shame evoked by the wheelwright’s lesson on what words cannot convey. Presumptuously, I compiled collected explanations to guard against my own forgetfulness. The connections I drew indeed came from various scholars, while the principal purport followed the old annotations. After twenty years of painstaking labor, I suddenly met with this favorable opportunity. Judging my own worth, I see this less as an honor to myself than as a cause for rejoicing for the age.
This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose perspicacity makes you a sage and whose sincerity leads to illumination. In harmony with the imperial predecessor, you renew his brilliance, and you draw upon others to practice goodness. You have elevated five worthies to receive sacrifices in the Temple of Confucius, making the Learning of Principle still clearer; you have exalted the Four Books in the imperial academy, sweeping away the hundred schools. You have already put the full import of this teaching extensively into practice: how could you merely bestow empty praise upon its exponents? And I, your servant, happened to have assembled this compilation and have presumptuously intruded upon…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
清燕其為懽忭曷既揄揚昔弱翁條董子之
謨則宣帝之中興有補主父奏賈生之策
則武皇之制治無虞矧是緒言復當昌運
儻于
萬幾之暇時賜覽觀是即四子之賢面承咨
訪毋畫已至勿安小成必將見天地之純
全于以極聖神之功化行同倫車同軌
君道與師道而並行日之升月之恒文運随
國運而長泰所有近思錄集解一部十冊謹
===
随
表上進以
聞干冒
宸嚴臣無任戰慄屏營之至
第叁場
策五道
第一問
張璿
同考試官教諭姜 批 五策皆善荅蕘論足取
punctuated:
清燕，其為懽忭，曷既揄揚？昔弱翁條董子之謨，則宣帝之中興有補；主父奏賈生之策，則武皇之制治無虞。矧是緒言，復當昌運！儻于萬幾之暇，時賜覽觀，是即四子之賢，面承咨訪。毋畫已至，勿安小成，必將見天地之純全，于以極聖神之功化。行同倫，車同軌，君道與師道而並行；日之升，月之恒，文運随國運而長泰。所有近思錄集解一部十冊，謹随表上進以聞。干冒宸嚴，臣無任戰慄屏營之至。
第叁場
策五道
第一問
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批：五策皆善荅，蕘論足取。
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s quiet leisure. How could I ever fully express my joy and exultation? In former times, when Ruoweng set forth Master Dong’s counsels, they helped Emperor Xuan restore the dynasty’s fortunes; when Zhufu presented Master Jia’s proposals, Emperor Wu’s ordering of government was free from anxiety. How much more fitting that these inherited teachings should encounter an age of flourishing fortune! If, amid the myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty would occasionally deign to read them, it would be as though you were consulting the four worthy masters face to face. Do not set your limit at what you have already attained, or rest content with modest achievements. You will surely perceive the purity and completeness of Heaven and Earth, and thereby bring the achievements and transforming influence of sagely wisdom to their utmost reach. Conduct will follow common norms, and carriages will share a common track; the Way of the ruler and the Way of the teacher will advance together. Like the rising sun and the enduring moon, the fortunes of learning will long flourish alongside those of the state. I respectfully submit herewith, accompanying this memorial for Your Majesty’s consideration, one complete copy in ten fascicles of the Collected Explanations of Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu jijie). Having presumed to offend Your Majesty’s august dignity, your servant is overcome with trembling and profound apprehension.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Zhang Xuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “All five policy essays answer well; their humble counsel merits acceptance [?].”

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
文皇帝貽謀之意且敷析詳明錄之以獻可無少裨
聖學之萬一乎
同考試官教授王批五策善答此篇尤能揄揚
當代貽謀之善與古帝王媲美其學識過人遠矣
考試官左諭德靳批此策于
聖學之大能識其要而文詞雅健又足以鋪張之盖亦究心于大者歟
考試官學士江批此策非學得其要者不能
聖人馭世有治法有以成一代之化聖人
為學有心法有以垂百世之規心法者治
===
法之本也治法者心法之推也是故心法
得其傳則聖德脩聖化行上可以承無疆
之業下可以垂無窮之澤學求如是而已
又何必敝精神役志慮規規于章句詞華
如經生文士為哉此我
太宗文皇帝御製聖學心法一書極垂範貽謨
之善而真可以為萬世
聖子神孫保位脩德之龜鑑也且所謂心法者
果何始乎堯之授舜也曰天之曆數在爾
punctuated:
文皇帝貽謀之意，且敷析詳明，錄之以獻，可無少裨聖學之萬一乎？

同考試官教授王批：五策善答，此篇尤能揄揚當代貽謀之善，與古帝王媲美，其學識過人遠矣。

考試官左諭德靳批：此策于聖學之大，能識其要，而文詞雅健，又足以鋪張之，盖亦究心于大者歟？

考試官學士江批：此策非學得其要者不能。

聖人馭世，有治法，有以成一代之化；聖人為學，有心法，有以垂百世之規。心法者，治法之本也；治法者，心法之推也。是故心法得其傳，則聖德脩，聖化行，上可以承無疆之業，下可以垂無窮之澤。學求如是而已，又何必敝精神，役志慮，規規于章句詞華，如經生文士為哉？此我太宗文皇帝御製《聖學心法》一書，極垂範貽謨之善，而真可以為萬世聖子神孫保位脩德之龜鑑也。且所謂心法者，果何始乎？堯之授舜也，曰：「天之曆數在爾
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen’s intention in bequeathing guidance to his successors; moreover, the exposition is detailed and clear. If recorded and presented to the throne, might it not contribute even a little to imperial sagely learning?

Associate Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: All five policy essays answer well. This essay is especially able to extol the excellence of the reigning dynasty’s guidance bequeathed to its successors, which rivals that of the ancient emperors and kings. His learning and discernment far surpass those of others.

Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher, comments: This policy essay grasps the essentials of the great subject of sagely learning. Its elegant and vigorous language is also fully adequate to expound them. Surely he too has devoted his mind to great matters!

Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: No one whose learning had not grasped the essentials could have written this policy essay.

When sages govern the world, they have methods of government by which to accomplish the transforming influence of an age. When sages pursue learning, they have methods of cultivating the mind by which to bequeath standards for a hundred generations. The methods of the mind are the foundation of the methods of government; the methods of government are the extension of the methods of the mind. Thus, when the methods of the mind are duly transmitted, sagely virtue is cultivated and sagely transformation takes effect. Looking back, one can carry forward an enduring imperial enterprise; looking ahead, one can bequeath blessings without end. Learning seeks nothing more than this. Why, then, exhaust one’s mental energies and tax one’s thoughts, narrowly preoccupied with textual phrases and literary ornament, as do classical scholars and men of letters? Thus the imperially authored book Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), by our Emperor Taizong Wen, exemplifies the highest excellence in setting standards and bequeathing guidance. It can truly serve as a guide and mirror for sagely sons and divine grandsons through all ages, enabling them to preserve their throne and cultivate their virtue. But where, indeed, did these so-called methods of the mind begin? When Yao transmitted authority to Shun, he said: “Heaven’s appointed succession rests with you…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
躬允執厥中舜之授禹也曰惟精惟一允
執厥中此萬世帝王聖學之淵源也禹以
是傳之湯湯以是傳之文武文武以是傳
之周公孔子周公孔子以是傳之顏曾思
孟語其功則不越乎致知力行之事語其
要則不外乎身心性情之間為人君而不
知此則無以主治於上為人臣而不知此
則無以輔治於下盖古人之學無不然者
則所謂帝王之學與常人同者其不然乎
===
慨夫黍離之嘆興而聖學不見于朝廷泰
山之望絕而聖學不傳于韋布道術分裂
心法晦盲業文辭者功雖倍而無益親技
藝者心雖勞而無用是盖世儒逐末之所
為而實非緝熈典學之當務也則所謂帝
王之學與常人異者亦豈不然乎我
文皇帝深慨於是故于
聽政之暇躬采聖賢嘉言作為心法一書以
為萬世訓
punctuated:
躬，允執厥中。」舜之授禹也，曰：「惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此萬世帝王聖學之淵源也。禹以是傳之湯，湯以是傳之文武，文武以是傳之周公孔子，周公孔子以是傳之顏曾思孟。語其功，則不越乎致知力行之事；語其要，則不外乎身心性情之間。為人君而不知此，則無以主治於上；為人臣而不知此，則無以輔治於下。盖古人之學無不然者，則所謂帝王之學與常人同者，其不然乎？

慨夫黍離之嘆興，而聖學不見于朝廷；泰山之望絕，而聖學不傳于韋布。道術分裂，心法晦盲。業文辭者，功雖倍而無益；親技藝者，心雖勞而無用。是盖世儒逐末之所為，而實非緝熈典學之當務也。則所謂帝王之學與常人異者，亦豈不然乎？我文皇帝深慨於是，故于聽政之暇，躬采聖賢嘉言，作為《心法》一書，以為萬世訓。
translation_en:
…upon your person. Hold faithfully to the Mean.” When Shun transmitted rulership to Yu, he said: “Be discerning and single-minded; hold faithfully to the Mean.” This is the fountainhead of the learning of the sages for emperors and kings throughout all ages. Yu transmitted it to Tang; Tang transmitted it to Kings Wen and Wu; Kings Wen and Wu transmitted it to the Duke of Zhou and Kongzi; the Duke of Zhou and Kongzi transmitted it to Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mengzi. In terms of its practical effort, it consists entirely in extending knowledge and putting it earnestly into practice; in terms of its essentials, it concerns nothing beyond the person, the mind, human nature, and the emotions. A ruler who does not understand this has no means of directing government above; a minister who does not understand it has no means of assisting government below. Such was invariably the learning of the ancients. Is it not therefore true that the learning of emperors and kings is the same as that of ordinary people?

Alas, when the lament of “The Millet Hangs Low” arose, the learning of the sages ceased to appear at court; when the hope embodied in Mount Tai was extinguished with Kongzi’s death, that learning ceased to be transmitted among commoners clad in plain cloth. The Way and its teachings became fragmented, and the teachings of the mind were obscured. Those who devoted themselves to literary composition doubled their efforts without benefit; those who concerned themselves with technical skills exhausted their minds without useful result. These were the pursuits of worldly scholars chasing after peripheral matters, and certainly not the proper work of continuously illuminating and cultivating the enduring teachings. Is it not therefore also true that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of ordinary people? Our Emperor Wen deeply lamented this state of affairs. Thus, in the intervals between attending to government, he personally selected exemplary sayings of the sages and worthies and compiled them into a book, Teachings of the Mind, to serve as instruction for all ages.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
大哉王言豈特若唐之帝範匡□一時之足法
哉又豈特
聖子神孫所當知哉盖其綱有四則君道也父
道也子道也臣道也而君道一綱實為之
要其目三十有一有統言者有專言者而
問學一目實為之先誠使居君師之位者
上思列聖之傳下究諸儒之論研極其精
微而融會于一理則治平之政畢舉位育
之效可臻心法立而治法行又何帝王之
===
盛不可並哉若夫後世文學之君有弗錄
者竊又有以仰窺
聖心之所在矣盖漢武明皇之製作雖工然其
所學者固所謂文詞之末也非聖學也使
移其所以究心於文詞者而于聖學焉是
務則必能節多欲之心而不蹈嬴秦之轍
轍必能知無逸之戒而不動漁陽之干戈
寧至漫無所補如彼哉漢元魏文之藝文
雖美然其所學者固所謂技藝之小也非
punctuated:
大哉王言！豈特若唐之帝範，匡□一時之足法哉？又豈特聖子神孫所當知哉？盖其綱有四，則君道也、父道也、子道也、臣道也，而君道一綱實為之要。其目三十有一，有統言者，有專言者，而問學一目實為之先。誠使居君師之位者，上思列聖之傳，下究諸儒之論，研極其精微，而融會于一理，則治平之政畢舉，位育之效可臻。心法立而治法行，又何帝王之盛不可並哉？
若夫後世文學之君有弗錄者，竊又有以仰窺聖心之所在矣。盖漢武、明皇之製作雖工，然其所學者固所謂文詞之末也，非聖學也。使移其所以究心於文詞者，而于聖學焉是務，則必能節多欲之心，而不蹈嬴秦之轍轍，必能知無逸之戒，而不動漁陽之干戈，寧至漫無所補如彼哉？漢元、魏文之藝文雖美，然其所學者固所謂技藝之小也，非
translation_en:
Great indeed are these royal words! Could they merely be like the Tang work Model for Emperors (Difan), worthy of emulation for setting right [?] a single age? And could they be something only his sagely sons and divine grandsons ought to know? The work has four main divisions: the way of the ruler, the way of the father, the way of the son, and the way of the minister. Of these, the way of the ruler is the essential one. Its thirty-one topics include both general discussions and treatments of particular matters; among them, inquiry and learning takes first place. If those occupying the position of ruler and teacher would truly reflect upon the transmission received from the successive sage emperors, examine the arguments of the Confucian scholars, investigate their subtlest meanings to the utmost, and comprehend them together as a single principle, then all measures for orderly and peaceful government could be implemented, and the effect of placing all things in their proper positions and nurturing them could be attained. Once the methods of the mind are established and the methods of government put into practice, what flourishing reign of an emperor or king could not be equaled?
As for the omission of certain later rulers distinguished in literary learning, here too I venture to discern something of the imperial mind’s intent. Although the compositions of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Minghuang of Tang were accomplished, what they studied was precisely what is called the peripheral pursuit of literary composition, rather than sagely learning. Had they redirected the attention they devoted to literary composition toward sagely learning, the former would surely have restrained his many desires and avoided following in the tracks of the Ying house of Qin [the transcription repeats “tracks”]; the latter would surely have understood the admonition against idle ease and avoided stirring up warfare at Yuyang. How could their learning then have proved so utterly unhelpful as it did? Although the artistic and literary accomplishments of Emperor Yuan of Han and Emperor Wen of Wei were fine, what they studied was precisely what is called the minor pursuit of technical arts, rather than…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖學也使移其所以致力於技藝者而于
聖學焉是專則必能變化優柔而不首為
西京基亂之主必能克廣德心而不僅成
三分鼎立之勢又寧至一無所補如彼哉
故立其本者雖或可該乎末而學其大者
則正不必復事其小也矧萬幾之繁勢固
不能以多兼而一心之微功尤不可以兩
用學聖學者可不知所擇哉若夫范祖禹
告其君則曰人君欲正其心未有不由稽
===
古好學而能致者故能好學則君子皆欣
慕願立於朝而太平致矣不能好學則小
人皆動其心欲立其朝而專其權利矣用
君子則治用小人則亂皆在乎君心之所
召也范氏勸學之意切矣此學聖學者所
當知也朱晦翁告其君則曰人君講學雖
所以為正心之要而其所謂學則又有邪
正之别焉盖味聖賢之言以求義理之當
察古今之變以驗得失之幾必反之身以
punctuated:
聖學也。使移其所以致力於技藝者，而于聖學焉是專，則必能變化優柔，而不首為西京基亂之主；必能克廣德心，而不僅成三分鼎立之勢，又寧至一無所補如彼哉？故立其本者，雖或可該乎末，而學其大者，則正不必復事其小也。矧萬幾之繁，勢固不能以多兼，而一心之微，功尤不可以兩用。學聖學者，可不知所擇哉？
若夫范祖禹告其君，則曰：「人君欲正其心，未有不由稽古好學而能致者。故能好學，則君子皆欣慕，願立於朝，而太平致矣；不能好學，則小人皆動其心，欲立其朝而專其權利矣。用君子則治，用小人則亂，皆在乎君心之所召也。」范氏勸學之意切矣，此學聖學者所當知也。
朱晦翁告其君，則曰：「人君講學，雖所以為正心之要，而其所謂學，則又有邪正之别焉。盖味聖賢之言，以求義理之當；察古今之變，以驗得失之幾；必反之身以
translation_en:
…the learning of the sages. Had they redirected the effort they devoted to technical accomplishments and concentrated instead on the learning of the sages, Emperor Yuan of Han would surely have transformed his indecisiveness and would not have become the first ruler to lay the foundations of disorder in the Western Han; Emperor Wen of Wei would surely have broadened his virtuous disposition and would not merely have brought about a balance of power among three rival states. How, then, could their accomplishments have proved as utterly unhelpful as they did? Thus, those who establish the root may also encompass the branches, but those who study what is great need not further occupy themselves with what is petty. Moreover, amid the multitude of affairs of state, circumstances certainly do not permit one to attend to many pursuits at once; and in the subtle workings of the single mind, effort especially must not be divided between two purposes. Can those who pursue the learning of the sages fail to understand what they should choose?
Fan Zuyu, in addressing his sovereign, said: “No ruler wishing to rectify his mind has ever achieved this without examining antiquity and loving learning. If he loves learning, gentlemen will all admire him with delight and wish to serve at his court, and great peace will be attained. If he does not love learning, petty men will all be stirred to ambition, wishing to serve at his court and monopolize its power and benefits. Employing gentlemen brings order; employing petty men brings disorder. It all depends on what the ruler’s mind attracts.” Earnest indeed was Master Fan’s intention in urging learning! This is something those who pursue the learning of the sages ought to understand.
Zhu Huiweng, in addressing his sovereign, said: “Although a ruler’s study and discussion of learning are essential to rectifying his mind, what is called learning itself admits a distinction between the deviant and the correct. One must savor the words of the sages and worthies to seek what is right in moral principles, and examine changes in past and present to discern the incipient signs of success and failure; one must then turn these back upon oneself in order to …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
踐其實者學之正也涉獵記誦以雜博相
高割裂裝綴以華靡相勝反之身而無實
措之事而無當者學之邪也學之正心未
有不正者學之邪心未有不邪者朱子論
學之旨精矣此尤學聖學者所當知也仰
惟
聖明在上德同乾健學懋日新
經筵講心法之微言化理敷皇極之大道民
康物阜内安外寧
===
祖訓率由之功元老格心之效皆愚所親見而
快覩者狂瞽之言衹見其贅耳惟執事姑
取其芹曝之心可也
第二問
戴仲綸
同考試官訓導周 批 朱子辨雜學散見文集
中多為所窘此作有考據有發越蓋博學之士也
同考試官訓導李 批 此策極其所欲言而卒
歸于正猶有朱子文字家數
punctuated:
踐其實者，學之正也。涉獵記誦，以雜博相高；割裂裝綴，以華靡相勝；反之身而無實，措之事而無當者，學之邪也。學之正，心未有不正者；學之邪，心未有不邪者。朱子論學之旨精矣，此尤學聖學者所當知也。仰惟聖明在上，德同乾健，學懋日新。經筵講心法之微言，化理敷皇極之大道，民康物阜，内安外寧。祖訓率由之功，元老格心之效，皆愚所親見而快覩者。狂瞽之言，衹見其贅耳。惟執事姑取其芹曝之心可也。

第二問
戴仲綸

同考試官訓導周批：朱子辨雜學，散見文集中，多為所窘。此作有考據，有發越，蓋博學之士也。

同考試官訓導李批：此策極其所欲言，而卒歸于正，猶有朱子文字家數。
translation_en:
…put its substance into practice: this is correct learning. To browse widely and memorize texts, competing in miscellaneous erudition; to cut passages apart and stitch them together, competing in ornate extravagance; to find no substance when applying this learning to oneself and no fitness when applying it to affairs: this is deviant learning. When learning is correct, the mind is invariably correct; when learning is deviant, the mind is invariably deviant. Master Zhu’s account of the purpose of learning is penetrating indeed. This, above all, is what those who study the learning of the sages ought to understand.

I reverently reflect that our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, his virtue matching Heaven’s vigor, his diligent learning renewed daily. At the Classics Colloquium, the subtle teachings on the discipline of the mind are expounded; in transformative governance, the great Way of the August Ultimate is extended. The people prosper and goods abound; there is peace within and tranquility abroad. The achievements of following the ancestral injunctions, and the efficacy of senior statesmen in rectifying the sovereign’s mind, are things that I, in my ignorance, have personally witnessed with delight. My rash and blind words merely appear superfluous. May you, Sir, accept only the humble sincerity of these offerings of celery and sunshine.

Second Policy Question
Dai Zhonglun

Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor, comments: Master Zhu’s discussions distinguishing miscellaneous learning from the true are scattered throughout his collected writings, and many candidates are stymied by them. This composition offers substantiation from sources and illuminating elaboration. Its author is surely a man of broad learning.

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: This policy essay gives full expression to what its author wishes to say, yet ultimately returns to what is correct. It has something of the manner of Master Zhu’s writing.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭林批雜學為世道之害此策
寫之殆盡而文有奇氣必非尋行數墨者
考試官左諭德靳批此策能發揮朱子憂道之心可嘉
考試官學士江批先賢論辯子能辯之可謂辯博之士矣
甚矣君子憂道之切也異端之害正者闢
之固所當嚴雜學之亂真者辯之尤所當
力是豈君子之好為辯哉為天地立心為
生民立極為往聖繼絕學為萬世開太平
身世道之責則有不得不然而然者然異端闢
===
矣則人心由是而一正雜學辯矣則聖道
由是而益明天下之人如夢而覺如醉而
醒者皆君子之辯為之也嗚呼君子之有
功於世其大矣哉粵自先王之世一道德
同風俗人無異言家無異學未有所謂異
端之害也亦未有所謂雜學之名也周室
衰而禮樂缺異端興矣孔子憂之于是正
六經而先王之道明孔子沒而楊墨起異
端熾矣孟子憂之于是作七篇而孔子之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭林批：雜學為世道之害，此策寫之殆盡，而文有奇氣，必非尋行數墨者。
考試官左諭德靳批：此策能發揮朱子憂道之心，可嘉。
考試官學士江批：先賢論辯，子能辯之，可謂辯博之士矣。
甚矣，君子憂道之切也！異端之害正者，闢之固所當嚴；雜學之亂真者，辯之尤所當力。是豈君子之好為辯哉？為天地立心，為生民立極，為往聖繼絕學，為萬世開太平，身世道之責，則有不得不然而然者。然異端闢矣，則人心由是而一正；雜學辯矣，則聖道由是而益明。天下之人如夢而覺、如醉而醒者，皆君子之辯為之也。嗚呼！君子之有功於世，其大矣哉！粵自先王之世，一道德，同風俗，人無異言，家無異學，未有所謂異端之害也，亦未有所謂雜學之名也。周室衰而禮樂缺，異端興矣。孔子憂之，於是正六經，而先王之道明。孔子沒而楊墨起，異端熾矣。孟子憂之，於是作七篇，而孔子之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “This policy essay describes almost exhaustively the harm that eclectic learning does to the moral order of the world. Its writing has an extraordinary vitality: its author surely is no mere reader who follows lines and counts characters.”
Examiner Jin, Left Exhorter, comments: “This policy essay deserves praise for its ability to bring out Master Zhu’s concern for the Way.”
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: “You can elucidate the arguments of earlier worthies. You may indeed be called a scholar of broad learning and skill in disputation.”
How deeply the gentleman is concerned for the Way! Heterodox teachings that injure orthodoxy must certainly be sternly rejected; eclectic learning that confounds the truth must be disputed with still greater vigor. Could this be because the gentleman delights in disputation? To establish a heart for Heaven and Earth, to establish an ultimate standard for the people, to carry on the interrupted learning of past sages, and to inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations—bearing personal responsibility for the moral order of the world, he acts thus because he cannot do otherwise. Once heterodoxy has been refuted, people’s hearts are thereby brought into unity and rectitude; once eclectic learning has been critically distinguished, the Way of the sages becomes still clearer. That people throughout the world awaken as if from a dream and become sober as if from drunkenness is entirely the achievement of the gentleman’s disputation. Ah! How great is the gentleman’s contribution to the world!
In the age of the former kings, moral principles were unified and customs were shared. People voiced no divergent doctrines, and households pursued no divergent learning. There was as yet no such thing as the harm of heterodoxy, nor even the name “eclectic learning.” When the royal house of Zhou declined and rites and music fell into disrepair, heterodoxy arose. Kongzi was concerned about this; he therefore put the Six Classics in order, and the Way of the former kings became clear. After Kongzi died, the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di arose, and heterodoxy flourished. Mengzi was concerned about this; he therefore composed the Seven Books, and Kongzi’s …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
道著故有若頌孔子之功則謂其賢于堯
舜昌黎稱孟子之功而推其不在禹下皆
以是耳自是而後憂道之君子世亦未嘗
無人焉申韓諸家作於漢則董子能排之
而啓武帝罷黜之詔見于天人三策者可
考也董子不有功于漢室者哉佛老二氏
盛于唐則韓子能排之而致學者斗山之
仰見于原道諸篇者可稽也韓子不有功
于唐室者哉至于有宋之興則為本論以
===
專攻佛氏之失者歐陽子也為怪說以兼
攻時文之弊者石徂徠也其有功於宋又
不猶董子之于漢韓子之于唐乎盖是數
君子者雖未能盡學孟子之學而實皆能
心孟子之心者其不得已而辯人皆知之
也惟我朱子之辯雜學則尤有不得已焉
者而人或未之知也何者昔之所謂異端
楊墨之徒之異端也其說易攻也茲之所
謂雜學者吾儒學孔孟之徒之流于異端
punctuated: 道著。故有若頌孔子之功，則謂其賢于堯舜；昌黎稱孟子之功，而推其不在禹下，皆以是耳。自是而後，憂道之君子，世亦未嘗無人焉。申韓諸家作於漢，則董子能排之，而啓武帝罷黜之詔，見于《天人三策》者可考也。董子不有功于漢室者哉？佛老二氏盛于唐，則韓子能排之，而致學者斗山之仰，見于《原道》諸篇者可稽也。韓子不有功于唐室者哉？至于有宋之興，則為《本論》以專攻佛氏之失者，歐陽子也；為《怪說》以兼攻時文之弊者，石徂徠也。其有功於宋，又不猶董子之于漢、韓子之于唐乎？盖是數君子者，雖未能盡學孟子之學，而實皆能心孟子之心者，其不得已而辯，人皆知之也。惟我朱子之辯雜學，則尤有不得已焉者，而人或未之知也。何者？昔之所謂異端，楊墨之徒之異端也，其說易攻也；茲之所謂雜學者，吾儒學孔孟之徒之流于異端
translation_en:
…the Way became manifest. Thus, when You Ruo praised Confucius’s achievements, he declared him worthier than Yao and Shun; and when Han Yu of Changli praised Mencius’s achievements, he judged him no less than Yu. Both did so for this reason alone. Thereafter, no age lacked gentlemen who were concerned for the Way. When the schools of Shen Buhai, Han Fei, and others arose under the Han, Master Dong Zhongshu was able to refute them and prompt Emperor Wu’s edict dismissing them. The evidence can be examined in his Three Responses on Heaven and Humanity. Did Master Dong not render service to the Han dynasty? When Buddhism and Daoism flourished under the Tang, Master Han Yu was able to refute them, winning the reverence of scholars, who looked up to him as to the Northern Dipper and Mount Tai. The evidence can be examined in his Inquiry into the Way and other essays. Did Master Han not render service to the Tang dynasty?

With the rise of the Song, it was Master Ouyang Xiu who wrote On Fundamentals specifically to attack the errors of Buddhism; and it was Shi Culai who wrote Discourse on Anomalies, also attacking the faults of contemporary literary composition. Were their services to the Song not like those of Master Dong to the Han and Master Han to the Tang? Although these gentlemen could not fully master the learning of Mencius, they could indeed all take his mind as their own. Everyone knows that they engaged in disputation because they could not do otherwise. Yet our Master Zhu Xi had still more compelling reasons for disputing eclectic learning, reasons that some people may not understand. Why is this? What was formerly called heterodoxy was the heterodoxy of the followers of Yang Zhu and Mo Di, whose doctrines were easy to attack. What is now called eclectic learning is the drifting into heterodoxy of those within our Confucian tradition who study Confucius and Mencius…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者也其說雖明也試舉其槩言之易解作
于東坡若其間元亨利貞之訓陰陽鬼神
之說盖佛老之緒餘也自朱子之辯出而
後性命之理與詩書中庸孟子相表裏者
昭然矣老子解作于子由若其間孔老異
同之辯與其後序所引六祖之云是欲合
吾儒于老佛而彌縫之也自朱子之辯出
而後吾儒與二家之不同者廓如矣中庸
解之有辯非為張無垢而作乎盖張之學
===
本出于龜山而其後乃逃儒而歸釋不有
朱子之辯則子思戒謹恐懼之功其差彌
甚而聖人心法之傳泯矣大學解之有辯
非為吕舍人而作乎吕之先嘗學于程子
而其流亦惑于老子浮屠不有朱子之辯
則曾子格物致知之旨其失愈遠而古人
為學之道繆矣若乃陳陸之辯則尤其不
得已者盖同父世所謂豪傑之才也子靜
世所謂淵源之學也一言一論學者之視
punctuated: 者也，其說雖明也。試舉其槩言之：《易解》作于東坡，若其間元亨利貞之訓、陰陽鬼神之說，盖佛老之緒餘也。自朱子之辯出，而後性命之理與《詩》《書》《中庸》《孟子》相表裏者昭然矣。《老子解》作于子由，若其間孔老異同之辯，與其後序所引六祖之云，是欲合吾儒于老佛而彌縫之也。自朱子之辯出，而後吾儒與二家之不同者廓如矣。《中庸解》之有辯，非為張無垢而作乎？盖張之學本出于龜山，而其後乃逃儒而歸釋。不有朱子之辯，則子思戒謹恐懼之功，其差彌甚，而聖人心法之傳泯矣。《大學解》之有辯，非為吕舍人而作乎？吕之先嘗學于程子，而其流亦惑于老子浮屠。不有朱子之辯，則曾子格物致知之旨，其失愈遠，而古人為學之道繆矣。若乃陳陸之辯，則尤其不得已者。盖同父，世所謂豪傑之才也；子靜，世所謂淵源之學也。一言一論，學者之視
translation_en: …who have strayed into heterodoxy, although their doctrines are clear [?]. Let us briefly describe some examples. Dongpo wrote the Explanation of the Changes. Its interpretations of “the originating, the flourishing, the beneficial, and the steadfast,” and its accounts of yin and yang and of ghosts and spirits, are remnants of Buddhist and Daoist teachings. Only after Master Zhu’s refutations appeared did the principles of human nature and Heaven’s mandate become manifest in their mutual correspondence with the Book of Odes, the Book of Documents, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius. Ziyou wrote the Explanation of the Laozi. Its discussion of the similarities and differences between Confucius and Laozi, together with the sayings of the Sixth Patriarch quoted in its postface, seeks to unite our Confucian teachings with those of Laozi and the Buddha by patching over their differences. Only after Master Zhu’s refutations appeared did the differences between our Confucian teachings and those two schools become fully clear. Was not the refutation of the Explanation of the Doctrine of the Mean written to address Zhang Wugou? Zhang’s learning originally derived from Guishan, but he subsequently abandoned Confucianism and turned to Buddhism. Without Master Zhu’s refutation, the departure from Zisi’s practice of vigilance, caution, apprehension, and fear would have grown ever greater, and the transmission of the sages’ teaching of the mind would have disappeared. Was not the refutation of the Explanation of the Great Learning written to address Secretary Lü? Lü had earlier studied under Master Cheng, yet the subsequent course of his learning also became confused by Laozi and Buddhism. Without Master Zhu’s refutation, the deviation from Zengzi’s purpose in investigating things and extending knowledge would have grown ever greater, and the ancients’ way of learning would have been distorted. As for his debates with Chen and Lu, these were especially unavoidable. Tongfu possessed what the world called the talents of an outstanding hero; Zijing possessed what the world called learning with a profound intellectual lineage. Every utterance and every argument drew the eyes of students …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聽係焉可以自恣意為乎夫先王以道治
天下漢唐以智力把持天下其不可同論
審矣而同父乃以堯舜三代與漢祖唐宗
比而同之是金鐵之不辯也其膠固于功
利何如哉故朱子屢書辯之而不已盖非
為同父辯也不如是則王伯義利之說不
白也老氏言有無以有無為二周子言有
無以有無為一不相為謀亦審矣而子靜
疑濂溪之學出於老子特詆而攻之是理
===
氣之不分也故朱子屢書亦辯之而不已
盖非為子靜辯也不如是則吾儒異學之
判不明也異時朱子論海内學術之弊亦
曰江西頓悟永康事功若不極力爭辯道
終不明此可以觀君子之心矣嗚呼李斯
坑焚之禍荀卿之王道誤之也申韓刑名
之慘老子之道德倡之也學術不明流弊
至此任世道之責者安得不憂之深慮之
遠哉今之士得以識人心之正而不惑於
punctuated:
聽係焉，可以自恣意為乎？夫先王以道治天下，漢唐以智力把持天下，其不可同論審矣。而同父乃以堯舜三代與漢祖唐宗比而同之，是金鐵之不辯也。其膠固于功利何如哉！故朱子屢書辯之而不已，盖非為同父辯也，不如是則王伯義利之說不白也。老氏言有無，以有無為二；周子言有無，以有無為一。不相為謀亦審矣。而子靜疑濂溪之學出於老子，特詆而攻之，是理氣之不分也。故朱子屢書亦辯之而不已，盖非為子靜辯也，不如是則吾儒異學之判不明也。異時朱子論海内學術之弊，亦曰：「江西頓悟，永康事功，若不極力爭辯，道終不明。」此可以觀君子之心矣。

嗚呼！李斯坑焚之禍，荀卿之王道誤之也；申韓刑名之慘，老子之道德倡之也。學術不明，流弊至此，任世道之責者安得不憂之深、慮之遠哉！今之士得以識人心之正，而不惑於
translation_en:
…and hearing of students depended upon them. Could they therefore give free rein to their own opinions? The former kings governed the realm through the Way; the Han and Tang rulers maintained their grip on it through cunning and force. That these cannot be discussed on the same footing is certain. Yet Tongfu compared Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties with the founding emperor of Han and the great emperor of Tang, treating them as equivalent. This is to fail to distinguish gold from iron. How firmly he clung to achievement and advantage! Thus Master Zhu repeatedly wrote to dispute his views and would not desist. His purpose was not merely to argue with Tongfu: without doing so, the distinctions between true kingship and hegemony, and between righteousness and profit, would remain unclear.

Laozi spoke of being and nonbeing, treating them as two; Master Zhou spoke of being and nonbeing, treating them as one. That their teachings follow different paths is likewise certain. Yet Zijing suspected that Lianxi’s learning derived from Laozi and expressly disparaged and attacked it. This is to fail to distinguish principle from material force. Thus Master Zhu likewise repeatedly wrote to dispute his views and would not desist. His purpose was not merely to argue with Zijing: without doing so, the distinction between our Confucian learning and heterodox teachings would remain unclear. On another occasion, discussing the failings of scholarship throughout the realm, Master Zhu also said: “Jiangxi teaches sudden enlightenment; Yongkang advocates practical achievement. Unless we dispute these teachings with all our strength, the Way will never become clear.” Here we can see the heart of the noble man.

Alas! The calamity of burying scholars and burning books under Li Si arose because Xun Qing’s teaching of the kingly Way misled him; the cruelties of Shen Buhai and Han Fei’s doctrines of punishments and names were set in motion by Laozi’s teaching of the Way and virtue. When learning is unclear, its pernicious consequences reach such extremes. How could those who bear responsibility for the moral order of the age fail to feel profound concern and consider the distant consequences? That scholars today can recognize the rectitude of the human heart and avoid being misled by…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
性命之說知為學之方而不迷於趨向之
途謂非朱子之功而誰功先正曰周東遷
而孔子生宋南渡而朱子出愚則曰孔子
出而集群聖之大成朱子出而集諸儒之
大成其有功于萬世一也不識執事以為
然否
第三問
許魯
同考試官訓導周批此策以經權二字斷盡昔
===
賢用世之跡其與事剽竊餖飣以塞白者不侔矣
同考試官訓導李批古人事業此策一一能道
其心如身處其地者豈鹵莽議擬其間而有尚友之心
耶宜錄之
同考試官教諭林批此策論昔賢行事鑿鑿
皆有證據間亦有道人所未道者有是哉子之竒也
考試官左諭德靳批學識如此他日經濟其必有過人者矣
考試官學士江批有考據有斷制亦有筆力
嘗謂天下之事有常變之殊君子處之有
punctuated:
性命之說，知為學之方而不迷於趨向之途，謂非朱子之功而誰功？先正曰：「周東遷而孔子生，宋南渡而朱子出。」愚則曰：「孔子出而集群聖之大成，朱子出而集諸儒之大成，其有功于萬世一也。」不識執事以為然否？
第三問
許魯
同考試官訓導周批：此策以經權二字斷盡昔賢用世之跡，其與事剽竊餖飣以塞白者不侔矣。
同考試官訓導李批：古人事業，此策一一能道其心，如身處其地者，豈鹵莽議擬其間而有尚友之心耶？宜錄之。
同考試官教諭林批：此策論昔賢行事，鑿鑿皆有證據，間亦有道人所未道者，有是哉，子之竒也！
考試官左諭德靳批：學識如此，他日經濟，其必有過人者矣。
考試官學士江批：有考據，有斷制，亦有筆力。
嘗謂天下之事有常變之殊，君子處之有
translation_en:
…theories of human nature and destiny, and know the proper way to pursue learning without losing their direction—whose achievement could this be, if not Master Zhu’s? A former worthy said: “When the Zhou moved east, Confucius was born; when the Song crossed south, Master Zhu appeared.” I would humbly say: “Confucius appeared and brought the achievements of the many sages to their culmination; Master Zhu appeared and brought the achievements of the various Confucian scholars to their culmination. In their service to all subsequent ages, they are alike.” I do not know whether you, sir, consider this correct.
Third Policy Question
Xu Lu
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor: This policy essay comprehensively assesses how the worthies of former times served the world through the two concepts of constancy and discretion. It is quite unlike work that resorts to plagiarism and a patchwork of borrowed phrases merely to fill blank space [?].
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: In discussing the undertakings of the ancients, this policy essay explains their intentions one by one, as though its author had personally stood in their circumstances. Could one make crude judgments about them and yet possess the desire to befriend the ancients [?]? It should be selected.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: This policy essay discusses the deeds of former worthies with firm evidence for every assertion. At times it also says what others have not said. How remarkable your talent is!
Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher: With learning and discernment like this, he will surely surpass others when he undertakes the work of governing in the future.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Academician: It has substantiation, sound judgment, and forceful writing as well.
I have long held that the affairs of the world differ according to whether circumstances are ordinary or changing, and that the gentleman, in dealing with them, has…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
經權之異經所以處其常也權所以通其
變也處其常者無慊于一心通其變者有
功于斯世夫然後播休光于當時垂軌範
于来世迹之同異固不必一一計也愚請
以是復明問可乎夫丙吉孔明同為古之
賢相也而所遭之時則不同一則當火德
之方興一則當炎威之既燼也驅馳西蜀
經綸收拾之正難是豈可以為相之常體
例論邪親校簿書而卒成鼎足之勢孔明
===
之所處盖深有合乎詩之所謂夙興夜寐
者不然則開誠心布公道集衆思廣忠益
不知為相之大體者能之乎亞夫子儀同
為古之名將也而所處之地則不同一則
當兵威之全盛一則當國步之多艱也主
憂臣辱彷徨迫切之已甚是豈可以為將
之常規並論耶單騎結盟而卒致回紇之
羅拜子儀之所為盖深有合乎易之所謂
王臣蹇蹇者不然則功盖天下而主不疑
punctuated: 經權之異。經所以處其常也，權所以通其變也。處其常者無慊于一心，通其變者有功于斯世。夫然後播休光于當時，垂軌範于来世，迹之同異固不必一一計也。愚請以是復明問，可乎？夫丙吉、孔明同為古之賢相也，而所遭之時則不同：一則當火德之方興，一則當炎威之既燼也。驅馳西蜀，經綸收拾之正難，是豈可以為相之常體例論邪？親校簿書，而卒成鼎足之勢，孔明之所處盖深有合乎《詩》之所謂「夙興夜寐」者。不然，則開誠心，布公道，集衆思，廣忠益，不知為相之大體者能之乎？亞夫、子儀同為古之名將也，而所處之地則不同：一則當兵威之全盛，一則當國步之多艱也。主憂臣辱，彷徨迫切之已甚，是豈可以為將之常規並論耶？單騎結盟，而卒致回紇之羅拜，子儀之所為盖深有合乎《易》之所謂「王臣蹇蹇」者。不然，則功盖天下而主不疑，
translation_en:
…a distinction between constant principles and discretionary judgment. Constant principles serve to deal with ordinary circumstances; discretionary judgment serves to respond to changing circumstances. Those who deal with ordinary circumstances leave their conscience free of misgivings; those who respond to changing circumstances render service to the world. Only then do they spread their splendid renown in their own time and leave models for later generations. There is certainly no need to reckon up, one by one, the similarities and differences in their deeds. May I venture to answer your illuminating question on this basis?

Bing Ji and Kongming were both worthy chief ministers of antiquity, but the times they encountered differed: one lived when the dynasty endowed with the virtue of Fire was rising; the other, when its fiery might had already burned out. Toiling in western Shu, Kongming faced great difficulties in ordering affairs and gathering together what remained. How could he be judged by the ordinary conventions governing a chief minister? He personally checked registers and documents, yet ultimately established a realm standing as one of three powers, like the legs of a tripod. Kongming’s conduct surely accorded closely with what the Book of Odes calls “rising early and retiring late.” Otherwise, could someone who did not understand the essential responsibilities of a chief minister have opened his heart in sincerity, upheld impartiality, gathered the thinking of many, and drawn widely upon loyal counsel?

Yafu and Ziyi were both renowned generals of antiquity, but their circumstances differed: one acted when military power was at its height; the other, when the fortunes of the state were beset by difficulties. His lord’s distress was his servant’s disgrace; uncertainty and urgency had become extreme. How could his conduct be assessed alongside the other’s by the ordinary rules governing a general? Riding alone to conclude an alliance, Ziyi ultimately brought the Huige to bow before him in ranks. His actions surely accorded closely with what the Book of Changes calls “the king’s servant beset by difficulty upon difficulty.” Otherwise, though his achievements surpassed all others under Heaven, his ruler did not suspect him…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
位極人臣而眾不嫉非真將軍而能若是
乎子房世為韓相淵明世為晉臣其為世
臣之裔同而所遇之主不同也劉裕躬為
不道决無北面之義其必以徵士之節聞
無惑也若乃子房之於漢高固無不共戴
天之隙使不為之運籌帷幄則博浪之謀
其終能遂乎故先正謂其始終為韓庶幾
春秋復讎之義者深為得之而愚則又以
其辟穀之請而知其有以同於採菊之志
===
焉子陵善光武於西都之時李泌事肅宗
於明皇之世其為龍潜之舊同而所事之
君不同也肅宗言無不聽卒謀軍國之事
其得以中興之功顯固宜也若乃光武以
吏事責三公素無舍己任人之意而又不
能以賓師之禮處之則羊裘之志豈得而
遽變哉故先正稱其高尚之節出乎日月
之上者庶幾知之而愚則即其懷仁輔義
之言而知其本無絕人忘世之心焉陸贄
punctuated:
位極人臣而眾不嫉，非真將軍而能若是乎？

子房世為韓相，淵明世為晉臣，其為世臣之裔同，而所遇之主不同也。劉裕躬為不道，决無北面之義，其必以徵士之節聞，無惑也。若乃子房之於漢高，固無不共戴天之隙，使不為之運籌帷幄，則博浪之謀其終能遂乎？故先正謂其始終為韓，庶幾《春秋》復讎之義者，深為得之。而愚則又以其辟穀之請，而知其有以同於採菊之志焉。

子陵善光武於西都之時，李泌事肅宗於明皇之世，其為龍潜之舊同，而所事之君不同也。肅宗言無不聽，卒謀軍國之事，其得以中興之功顯，固宜也。若乃光武以吏事責三公，素無舍己任人之意，而又不能以賓師之禮處之，則羊裘之志豈得而遽變哉？故先正稱其高尚之節出乎日月之上者，庶幾知之。而愚則即其懷仁輔義之言，而知其本無絕人忘世之心焉。

陸贄
translation_en:
…to attain the highest rank a subject could hold without incurring the envy of others—could anyone who was not a true general have achieved this?

Zifang’s family had served for generations as chief ministers of the state of Han, and Yuanming’s family had served for generations as subjects of Jin. They were alike as descendants of hereditary servants of a ruling house, but the rulers they encountered differed. Liu Yu personally committed unrighteous acts, so there could assuredly be no justification for facing north and serving him as a subject. It is therefore unsurprising that Yuanming should have become known for the integrity of a scholar summoned to office who remained in retirement. As for Zifang’s relationship with Gaozu of Han, there was certainly no enmity that made it impossible for them to live beneath the same heaven. Had he not devised strategies for Gaozu within the command tent, could the purpose of his plot at Bolang ever have been accomplished? Thus the earlier worthy who said that he acted for the state of Han from beginning to end, approaching the principle of avenging wrongs taught in the Spring and Autumn Annals, understood him profoundly. Yet I, in my humble view, also discern from his request to abstain from grain that he shared something of the aspirations expressed in Yuanming’s picking chrysanthemums.

Ziling befriended Guangwu during his time in the western capital, and Li Mi served Suzong during the reign of Minghuang. They were alike in being old associates of rulers before their accession, but the sovereigns they served differed. Suzong heeded everything Li Mi said, and Li Mi ultimately planned affairs of the army and state. It was certainly fitting that he should gain renown for his contribution to restoring the dynasty. Guangwu, by contrast, held the Three Dukes responsible for administrative details; he had never been disposed to set aside his own judgment and entrust matters to others. Moreover, he could not treat Ziling with the courtesy due a guest and teacher. How, then, could the resolve of this man in a sheepskin coat suddenly change? Thus the earlier worthy who praised his lofty integrity as rising above the sun and moon came close to understanding him. Yet I, in my humble view, discern from his words about cherishing benevolence and supporting righteousness that he never intended to sever his ties with others or forget the world.

Lu Zhi…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
輿知貢舉得昌黎之賢名士之畢收也歐
陽永叔知貢舉退劉幾之怪名士之見黜
也是豈好惡之相反邪陸之考文精核乃
求賢之常法而歐之欲革鈎棘軋茁之體
固不得不變以通之也不然則通經學古
之習何由而成哉吕希哲為侍講荆公欲
之也而力辭其命楊中立為祕書蔡京薦
之也而遂就其官是豈趨向之不同邪吕
之不比匪人乃守身之常道而楊之援而
===
止之而止則是憫時之多故而欲以道易
之也不然則新經學術之謬何由而正哉
當熈寧之時張天祺請罷條例司不從而
去儒者事道之常也程明道用為條例司
官而不去大賢以上之作用也行若不同
矣然以吾不可學柳下惠之可者君子謂
之善學吾何敢疑其行不同哉當元祐之
日范蜀公以尚書僕射起之而不出廉貪
立懦之節也司馬温公以門下侍郎起之
punctuated: 輿知貢舉，得昌黎之賢，名士之畢收也；歐陽永叔知貢舉，退劉幾之怪，名士之見黜也。是豈好惡之相反邪？陸之考文精核，乃求賢之常法；而歐之欲革鈎棘軋茁之體，固不得不變以通之也。不然，則通經學古之習何由而成哉？吕希哲為侍講，荆公欲之也，而力辭其命；楊中立為祕書，蔡京薦之也，而遂就其官。是豈趨向之不同邪？吕之不比匪人，乃守身之常道；而楊之援而止之而止，則是憫時之多故，而欲以道易之也。不然，則新經學術之謬何由而正哉？當熈寧之時，張天祺請罷條例司，不從而去，儒者事道之常也；程明道用為條例司官而不去，大賢以上之作用也。行若不同矣，然以吾不可學柳下惠之可者，君子謂之善學。吾何敢疑其行不同哉？當元祐之日，范蜀公以尚書僕射起之而不出，廉貪立懦之節也；司馬温公以門下侍郎起之
translation_en:
…[?] supervised the examinations and obtained a worthy man in Changli: this was a case of gathering in all the eminent scholars. Ouyang Yongshu supervised the examinations and rejected Liu Ji for his bizarre writing: this was a case of an eminent scholar being excluded. Could their likes and dislikes really have been opposed? Lu’s precise scrutiny of compositions was the regular method of seeking worthy men. Ouyang, however, wished to reform a style as tangled as hooks and thorns and as contorted as cramped shoots; he therefore had no choice but to make changes so that progress could be made. Otherwise, how could the practice of comprehending the Classics and learning from antiquity have developed?

Lü Xizhe’s appointment as Expositor was desired by the Duke of Jing, yet he firmly declined the appointment. Yang Zhongli’s appointment as Secretary [?] was recommended by Cai Jing, and he duly assumed his office. Could their inclinations really have differed? Lü’s refusal to associate with unworthy men was the regular way of preserving one’s integrity. Yang’s allowing himself to be drawn in, then stopping when restrained [?], arose from his concern over the many troubles of the age and his desire to transform them through the Way. Otherwise, how could the errors of the new learning on the Classics have been corrected?

During the Xining era, Zhang Tianqi requested the abolition of the Finance Planning Commission. When his request was not accepted, he withdrew: this was the regular way in which a Confucian serves the Way. Cheng Mingdao was appointed an official of that commission and did not withdraw: this was conduct possible only for those of great worthiness or higher attainment. Their actions appear to have differed. Yet of the man who used what he himself could not permissibly do to emulate what Liu Xiahui could permissibly do, the gentleman said that he learned well. How could I dare question their differing conduct?

During the Yuanyou era, Fan, Duke of Shu, was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs but did not come forward. His integrity could make the greedy honest and the timid resolute. Sima, Duke of Wen, was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Chancellery …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而出旋乾轉坤之功也志若不同矣然顏
之修己禹稷之救民君子謂之同道吾何
敢疑其志不同哉至若王狄二公之去就
同一國家之變也陵守正不阿杜門不出
非為大臣者之典刑乎而梁公之事周則
亦非無謂者武暴如火禍斯烈矣逆長風
而孤騫遡大川以獨航廬陵既臣而皇天
下既周而唐非公之委曲感通則神器且
移于周矣是公之不去正所以為社稷計
===
而槩以縻官爵之常情譏之嗚呼則古之
五就桀者非邪又如劉許二賢之出處同
一世道之變也靜脩隱居教授累召不出
非學孔氏者之家法乎而魯齋之事元則
尤有可言者夷主中國亂斯極矣以農桑
學校導其君以小學大學教其臣彝倫賴
以少明生民賴以少康非魯齋周旋訓迪
則中國且將化于夷矣是魯齋之不隱正
所以為世道計而槩以事功名之常情詆
punctuated: 而出，旋乾轉坤之功也。志若不同矣，然顏之修己、禹稷之救民，君子謂之同道，吾何敢疑其志不同哉？至若王狄二公之去就，同一國家之變也。陵守正不阿，杜門不出，非為大臣者之典刑乎？而梁公之事周，則亦非無謂者。武暴如火，禍斯烈矣。逆長風而孤騫，遡大川以獨航。廬陵既臣而皇，天下既周而唐，非公之委曲感通，則神器且移于周矣。是公之不去，正所以為社稷計，而槩以縻官爵之常情譏之，嗚呼！則古之五就桀者非邪？又如劉許二賢之出處，同一世道之變也。靜脩隱居教授，累召不出，非學孔氏者之家法乎？而魯齋之事元，則尤有可言者。夷主中國，亂斯極矣。以農桑學校導其君，以小學大學教其臣，彝倫賴以少明，生民賴以少康。非魯齋周旋訓迪，則中國且將化于夷矣。是魯齋之不隱，正所以為世道計，而槩以事功名之常情詆
translation_en:
…and came forward to serve, accomplishing the work of turning Heaven and Earth around. Their intentions might seem different. Yet the gentleman regards Yan Hui’s cultivation of himself and Yu and Ji’s deliverance of the people as following the same Way. How would I dare question them for differing in their intentions?

As for the withdrawal or service of Lords Wang and Di, both confronted a crisis of the state. Wang Ling upheld what was right without yielding, shut his doors, and refused to come forth. Was this not an exemplary standard for a great minister? Yet the Duke of Liang, Di Renjie, also had his reasons for serving the Zhou. The violence of Wu blazed like fire, and the calamity was fierce indeed. He soared alone against a mighty wind and sailed alone upstream on a great river. That the Prince of Luling, once reduced to a subject, became emperor, and that the realm, having become Zhou, returned to Tang—without the duke’s tactful accommodation and persuasive influence, the sacred vessel of sovereignty would have passed to Zhou. His refusal to withdraw was precisely a means of safeguarding the state. Yet people indiscriminately criticize him as though he acted from the common attachment to office and rank. Alas! Would that also make the ancient worthy who five times entered Jie’s service wrong?

Likewise, the service and retirement of the two worthies Liu and Xu arose from the same upheaval in the moral order of their age. Jingxiu, Liu Yin, lived in retirement and taught, repeatedly declining summons to office. Was this not the established practice of those who study Confucius’s teachings? Yet there is still more to be said for Luzhai, Xu Heng, and his service to the Yuan. Foreign peoples ruled the Central Lands, and disorder had reached its utmost. He guided his ruler through agriculture, sericulture, and schools, and taught his ministers through the Elementary Learning and the Great Learning. Through these efforts, the enduring human relationships became somewhat clearer, and the people gained some measure of peace. Without Luzhai’s accommodating efforts to instruct and guide, the Central Lands would have been transformed into the ways of the foreign peoples. Luzhai’s refusal to retire was precisely a means of preserving the moral order of the age. Yet people indiscriminately revile him as though he acted from the common desire to pursue achievement and fame…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之嗚呼則孔子之欲赴公山佛肸之召者
非邪是則諸賢之人品固不能以皆同其
事業之造就亦不能以無異然守經行權
各盡其道則皆有足稱者矣所謂天下之
事變無常而理則有定者豈不然哉雖然
權者聖人之大用未易言也諸賢之事盖
亦姑就其一節取之孔子曰可與立未可
與權又曰旁行而不流此志于經濟者所
當服膺也愚雖不敏竊有志于斯矣惟執
===
事恕其狂斐而正之
第四問
楊灝
同考試官教諭鄒 批 昔人謂文不關世教雖工
無益此論敬天勤民極有警省人處具眼者當自識之
同考試官教諭王 批 此卷初場平順論表五判皆
奇策亦善答難成學可到惜不能盡錄其文耳健羨健羨
考試官左諭德靳 批 此策本典謨論治道學識出人
遠甚吾于中場已知子為佳士經之黜恐未足以盡子之蘊也
punctuated:
之。嗚呼！則孔子之欲赴公山、佛肸之召者非邪？是則諸賢之人品固不能以皆同，其事業之造就亦不能以無異。然守經行權，各盡其道，則皆有足稱者矣。所謂天下之事變無常，而理則有定者，豈不然哉？雖然，權者聖人之大用，未易言也。諸賢之事，盖亦姑就其一節取之。孔子曰：「可與立，未可與權。」又曰：「旁行而不流。」此志于經濟者所當服膺也。愚雖不敏，竊有志于斯矣。惟執事恕其狂斐而正之。

第四問
楊灝

同考試官教諭鄒批：昔人謂文不關世教，雖工無益。此論敬天勤民，極有警省人處，具眼者當自識之。

同考試官教諭王批：此卷初場平順，論、表、五判皆奇，策亦善，答難成學可到，惜不能盡錄其文耳。健羨，健羨！

考試官左諭德靳批：此策本典謨，論治道，學識出人遠甚。吾于中場已知子為佳士，經之黜恐未足以盡子之蘊也。
translation_en:
…him. Alas! Was Confucius then wrong to wish to answer the summons of Gongshan and Bi Xi? Thus, these worthies could not all have been identical in personal character, nor could their accomplishments have been without differences. Yet, in upholding constant principles and exercising discretion, each fulfilled his own proper course, and all therefore had something worthy of praise. Is this not what is meant by saying that affairs throughout the world change without constancy, while principle remains fixed? Nevertheless, discretion is a great capacity of the sage and cannot readily be discussed. In considering these worthies’ actions, we are provisionally taking just one aspect of each as deserving approval. Confucius said: “One may be fit to take a firm stand together with others, yet still be unfit to exercise discretion with them.” He also said: “Act beyond the ordinary course without drifting astray.” Those who aspire to order the world and aid its people should take these words to heart. Though I am slow of understanding, I too privately cherish this aspiration. I ask only that you pardon my rash and ill-considered words and correct them.

Fourth Question
Yang Hao 楊灝

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor: An earlier writer said that writing which has no bearing on the moral instruction of the age is of no benefit, however skillful it may be. This discussion of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people contains much that alerts readers and prompts reflection. Those with discernment should recognize this for themselves.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: This candidate’s first-session work is even and fluent; his discourse, memorial, and five legal judgments are all outstanding, and his policy essays are also good. His answers to difficult questions show learning capable of attainment [?]. It is regrettable only that we cannot reproduce all his writings. How greatly I admire him, how greatly I admire him!

Comment by Examiner Jin, Left Mentor: This policy essay draws on the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents to discuss the way of government. Its learning and insight far surpass those of others. Already in the middle session I knew you to be an excellent scholar. The rejection of your Classics essay [?], I fear, cannot adequately reflect the full extent of what you possess.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官學士江批此篇詳贍超詣非胸中素有抱
負者不能功業鳴世吾深有望於子矣
人皆曰格天之難也愚則曰格天非難敬
天而有要者為難也人皆曰安民之難也
愚則曰安民非難勤民而有方者為難也
何謂敬天之要不于其文于其實是也何
謂勤民之方不于其小于其大是也二者
兼盡則格天之功成而安民之績著矣嗚
呼孔孟之所以為學唐虞之所以為治其
===
皆存于茲乎方今
聖天子在上動遵
祖訓道契帝王
格天之宏功安民之偉績駕唐虞而邁三代
蓋已出于尋常萬萬矣而執事乃于秋闈
掄才之日復講求敬天勤民之學豈非以
有是君必當有是臣而畝畝之中亦或有
負堯舜君民之志如古人者乎愚也非其
人也然不敢不直述所聞以就正焉夫敬
punctuated:
考試官學士江批：此篇詳贍超詣，非胸中素有抱負者不能。功業鳴世，吾深有望於子矣。
人皆曰格天之難也，愚則曰格天非難，敬天而有要者為難也。人皆曰安民之難也，愚則曰安民非難，勤民而有方者為難也。何謂敬天之要？不于其文，于其實是也。何謂勤民之方？不于其小，于其大是也。二者兼盡，則格天之功成，而安民之績著矣。嗚呼！孔孟之所以為學，唐虞之所以為治，其皆存于茲乎？方今聖天子在上，動遵祖訓，道契帝王，格天之宏功、安民之偉績，駕唐虞而邁三代，蓋已出于尋常萬萬矣。而執事乃于秋闈掄才之日，復講求敬天勤民之學，豈非以有是君必當有是臣，而畝畝之中亦或有負堯舜君民之志如古人者乎？愚也非其人也，然不敢不直述所聞，以就正焉。夫敬
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: This essay is comprehensive, rich, and exceptionally accomplished. Only someone who has long cherished great aspirations could produce it. I have profound hopes that you will make your name in the world through your achievements.
Everyone says that moving Heaven is difficult. I, in my humble view, say that moving Heaven is not difficult; what is difficult is grasping the essentials of revering Heaven. Everyone says that bringing peace to the people is difficult. I say that bringing peace to the people is not difficult; what is difficult is having the proper method for diligently attending to their welfare. What are the essentials of revering Heaven? They lie in substance, rather than outward forms. What is the proper method for attending diligently to the people's welfare? It lies in addressing great matters rather than small ones. When both are fully realized, the work of moving Heaven will be accomplished, and the achievement of bringing peace to the people will become manifest. Ah! Were not the learning of Confucius and Mencius and the governance of Tang and Yu all grounded in this?
