Today our sagely Son of Heaven reigns above. In every action he follows the ancestral instructions, and his Way accords with that of the ancient emperors and kings. His magnificent accomplishments in moving Heaven and his great achievements in bringing peace to the people surpass Tang and Yu and outstrip the Three Dynasties; indeed, they already exceed the ordinary myriad times over. Yet you, honored examiners, on this occasion of selecting talent at the autumn Provincial Examination, once again investigate the learning of revering Heaven and diligently attending to the people. Is this not because such a ruler must have corresponding ministers, and because among those in the fields [?] there may also be men who, like the ancients, aspire to make their ruler a Yao or Shun and their people the people of Yao and Shun? In my ignorance, I am not such a man. Nevertheless, I dare not refrain from directly setting forth what I have learned, so as to submit it for your correction. Now, as for revering …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天勤民其事雖殊而其理出于心一也出
于心者雖同而達於政者則異請以見于
典謨者言之天聰明自我民聰明天明畏
自我民明威唐虞論天如此則敬天者豈
專在於執豆籩駿奔走以郊見上帝之時
哉一語默之順理皆天之對越也一念慮
之無私皆天之顧諟也天叙有典吾其惇
之天秩有禮吾其庸之天命有德吾其章
之天討有罪吾其用之卒之在我之天既
===
===
勅而天休至矣此則敬天之實也異時伊
尹告太甲有咸有一德克享天心之訓意
亦如此若傅說所謂黷于祭祀時謂弗欽
則正為徒事其文者發耳說豈不知所以
為敬而欲人之廢祀者哉若夫一日萬幾
天工人代唐虞之論治又如此則勤民者
亦豈在於勞一身侵庶職以日事叢脞為
哉庶官不必圖圖其所以擇庶官者而已
矣衆事不必謀謀其所以總衆事者而已
punctuated:
天勤民，其事雖殊，而其理出于心，一也。出于心者雖同，而達於政者則異。請以見于典謨者言之。「天聰明，自我民聰明；天明畏，自我民明威。」唐虞論天如此，則敬天者豈專在於執豆籩、駿奔走，以郊見上帝之時哉？一語默之順理，皆天之對越也；一念慮之無私，皆天之顧諟也。天叙有典，吾其惇之；天秩有禮，吾其庸之；天命有德，吾其章之；天討有罪，吾其用之。卒之，在我之天既勅，而天休至矣。此則敬天之實也。
異時伊尹告太甲，有「咸有一德，克享天心」之訓，意亦如此。若傅說所謂「黷于祭祀，時謂弗欽」，則正為徒事其文者發耳。說豈不知所以為敬，而欲人之廢祀者哉？
若夫「一日萬幾」、「天工人代」，唐虞之論治又如此，則勤民者亦豈在於勞一身、侵庶職，以日事叢脞為哉？庶官不必圖，圖其所以擇庶官者而已矣；衆事不必謀，謀其所以總衆事者而已
translation_en:
…revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people: although these activities differ, the principle underlying them issues from the heart and is one. Although they alike issue from the heart, their application in government differs. Allow me to explain this through what appears in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents. “Heaven’s hearing and sight come through the hearing and sight of our people; Heaven’s manifest authority comes through the manifest authority of our people.” Such was the account of Heaven in the ages of Tang and Yu. Can reverence for Heaven, then, be confined to those occasions when one holds sacrificial vessels and baskets and hastens forward to appear before the Lord on High at the suburban sacrifice? Every utterance or silence that accords with principle is an act of standing reverently before Heaven; every thought free of selfishness is an act of keeping Heaven constantly in view. Heaven has established the enduring norms: let me give them substantial effect. Heaven has ordered the rites: let me put them into practice. Heaven appoints the virtuous: let me distinguish them. Heaven punishes the guilty: let me carry out those punishments. Ultimately, once what belongs to Heaven within me has been set in order, Heaven’s blessings will arrive. This is the substance of revering Heaven.
In a later age, Yi Yin admonished Tai Jia with the teaching, “All possessing a single virtue, they could satisfy the heart of Heaven.” His meaning was likewise this. As for Fu Yue’s statement, “To be excessive in sacrifices is called irreverence,” it was directed precisely at those who attend merely to outward forms. Could Yue have failed to understand what constitutes reverence and wished people to abandon sacrifices?
As for the sayings, “In a single day there are ten thousand incipient affairs” and “Heaven’s work is performed by human beings acting in its stead,” such, again, was the account of government in the ages of Tang and Yu. Can diligent care for the people, then, consist in exhausting oneself, encroaching upon the duties of the various offices, and spending each day on petty details? One need not plan the work of every official; one need only consider how to select the officials. One need not deliberate upon every affair; one need only consider how to oversee all affairs…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣八元未登思有以登之也四凶未去思
有以去之也君子進矣而委任推誠之未
至思有以任之而勿貳也小人辨矣而遠
斥遏絕之未果思有以去之而勿疑也卒
之天下之賢畢集而庶績熈矣此安民之
方也異時周公戒成王有日昊不食用咸
和萬民之言意亦以此若立政所謂庶獄
庶慎文王罔敢知于正以人君不當兼事
其小耳周公豈不知所以為勤而教人以
===
不事事者哉然以帝堯之聖而猶有儆予
之嘆則堯雖能格天而固未嘗自以為能
格也以帝舜之仁而猶有阻飢之憂則舜
雖能安民而固未嘗自以為能安也克艱
之謨怠荒之戒君臣之間更相戒飭不自
滿假如此唐虞之治卓冠古今豈偶然哉
後世之君臣則異乎是唐太宗玄宗二宗
之首也太宗防患于未然雖賢于玄宗弭
患於已至然即其華夷之相雜而究其心
punctuated: 矣。八元未登，思有以登之也；四凶未去，思有以去之也。君子進矣，而委任推誠之未至，思有以任之而勿貳也；小人辨矣，而遠斥遏絕之未果，思有以去之而勿疑也。卒之，天下之賢畢集，而庶績熈矣。此安民之方也。異時周公戒成王，有「日昊不食，用咸和萬民」之言，意亦以此。若《立政》所謂「庶獄庶慎，文王罔敢知于」，正以人君不當兼事其小耳。周公豈不知所以為勤，而教人以不事事者哉？然以帝堯之聖，而猶有「儆予」之嘆，則堯雖能格天，而固未嘗自以為能格也；以帝舜之仁，而猶有「阻飢」之憂，則舜雖能安民，而固未嘗自以為能安也。「克艱」之謨、「怠荒」之戒，君臣之間更相戒飭，不自滿假如此。唐虞之治卓冠古今，豈偶然哉？後世之君臣則異乎是。唐太宗、玄宗，二宗之首也。太宗防患于未然，雖賢于玄宗弭患於已至，然即其華夷之相雜而究其心
translation_en:
…that is all. If the Eight Worthies have not yet been raised to office, he considers how to raise them; if the Four Villains have not yet been removed, he considers how to remove them. When gentlemen have advanced, but his delegation of responsibility and extension of trust remain incomplete, he considers how to entrust them with office without wavering. When petty men have been identified, but their banishment and exclusion have not been decisively accomplished, he considers how to remove them without hesitation. In the end, all the worthy men of the realm gather at court, and every undertaking flourishes. This is the way to bring peace to the people. In a later age, the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng with the words, “Until late in the day [?] he did not eat, seeking thereby to bring all the people into harmony.” His meaning was likewise this. As for the statement in “Establishing Government,” “In the many judicial cases and matters requiring care, King Wen did not presume to intervene,” it means precisely that a ruler should not also undertake the minor tasks himself. Could the Duke of Zhou have failed to understand what diligence meant, and taught a ruler to leave affairs unattended?

Yet even with Emperor Yao’s sageliness, he still uttered the appeal, “Admonish me.” Thus, although Yao could move Heaven, he certainly never presumed that he could do so. Even with Emperor Shun’s benevolence, he still worried about the people’s “distress and hunger.” Thus, although Shun could bring peace to the people, he certainly never presumed that he could do so. Through counsels to “recognize the difficulty” and warnings against “indolence and neglect,” ruler and ministers admonished one another in turn, so thoroughly avoiding complacency and self-satisfaction. Could it have been by chance that the government of Tang and Yu stood preeminent throughout antiquity and later times?

The rulers and ministers of later ages were different. Taizong and Xuanzong of the Tang were foremost among the two houses [?]. Although Taizong, who guarded against trouble before it arose, was superior to Xuanzong, who sought to quell trouble only after it had arrived, nevertheless, if we examine the intermingling of Chinese and non-Chinese under him and probe his intentions…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
則視夫一德之格天者何如也蓋所相者
房杜隨世以就功名之徒虞廷之所謂者
寂乎莫之聞也格天之功有愧於古何異
哉宋太宗仁宗諸君之冠也仁宗憂勤於
承平之後雖若難於太宗憂勤于草創之
時然即其邪正之並用而考其德則視夫
知人則哲者何如也蓋其所相者韓富血
氣用事之才虞廷之所學者杳乎未之聞
也安民之效有愧于古何恠哉雖然太宗
===
===
玄宗雖未盡格天之要而心猶可取也若
乃漢武信李少君而創太乙之祠真宗信
王欽若而崇天書之奉則既無其實而倂
失其文其敬天也祗所以為褻天也是固
無足論矣吾獨惜夫光武中興之賢君也
惟其偏信張純躬親封禪君子譏之亦與
二君並焉蓋既不知所以為敬則其得罪
於天同耳使能納桓譚之直諫寧至為盛
德之累如此哉太宗仁宗雖未盡安人之
punctuated:
則視夫一德之格天者何如也？蓋所相者，房、杜隨世以就功名之徒，虞廷之所謂者，寂乎莫之聞也。格天之功有愧於古，何異哉？宋太宗、仁宗，諸君之冠也。仁宗憂勤於承平之後，雖若難於太宗憂勤于草創之時，然即其邪正之並用而考其德，則視夫知人則哲者何如也？蓋其所相者，韓、富血氣用事之才，虞廷之所學者，杳乎未之聞也。安民之效有愧于古，何恠哉？

雖然，太宗、玄宗雖未盡格天之要，而心猶可取也。若乃漢武信李少君而創太乙之祠，真宗信王欽若而崇天書之奉，則既無其實而倂失其文，其敬天也，祗所以為褻天也，是固無足論矣。吾獨惜夫光武，中興之賢君也，惟其偏信張純，躬親封禪，君子譏之，亦與二君並焉。蓋既不知所以為敬，則其得罪於天同耳。使能納桓譚之直諫，寧至為盛德之累如此哉？太宗、仁宗雖未盡安人之
translation_en:
…then how does he compare with one whose undivided virtue moved Heaven? Those he appointed chief councilors, Fang and Du, were men who accommodated themselves to their times to attain achievement and renown; of what was spoken of at Shun’s court, nothing was heard. What wonder that his achievement in moving Heaven fell short of antiquity? Taizong and Renzong of the Song ranked foremost among rulers. Renzong’s anxious diligence after peace had been established might seem harder to sustain than Taizong’s anxious diligence during the dynasty’s founding. Yet if we examine his virtue in light of his employing the wicked and the upright together, how does he compare with one who was “discerning in his knowledge of men”? Those he appointed chief councilors, Han and Fu, were talented men who acted on impulse; of what was studied at Shun’s court, scarcely anything was heard. What wonder that his success in bringing peace to the people fell short of antiquity?

Nevertheless, although Taizong and Xuanzong of the Tang did not fully grasp the essentials of moving Heaven, their intentions were still commendable. But Emperor Wu of the Han trusted Li Shaojun and established a shrine to Taiyi, while Zhenzong trusted Wang Qinruo and exalted the veneration of the celestial writings. They lacked the substance and also forfeited the proper outward forms: their reverence for Heaven served only to profane Heaven. They are certainly not worth discussing. I regret especially the case of Guangwu, a worthy ruler who restored his dynasty. Simply because he placed undue trust in Zhang Chun and personally performed the feng and shan sacrifices, gentlemen censured him and ranked him alongside those two rulers. Since he did not understand what constituted reverence, his offense against Heaven was the same as theirs. Had he accepted Huan Tan’s forthright remonstrance, would he ever have brought such a blemish upon his great virtue? Although Taizong and Renzong of the Song did not fully grasp the means of bringing peace to the people…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
方而政猶可稱也若乃秦皇相李斯而衡
石程書隋文用高熲而衞士傳飡則徒事
其小而反遺其大其勤民也乃所以為厲
民也是固無足道矣吾獨惜夫神宗勵精
之英主也惟其偏信王安石而更為新法
君子非之亦與二君並焉蓋既不知所以
為勤則其播惡于衆一耳使能聽司馬光
之讜論寧至盡違其願治之心如此哉嗚
呼敬天一也或以之治而亦或以亂勤民
===
一也或以之盛而亦或以衰其毫釐之差
而天淵之判如此揆厥所由得非以其孔
孟之學不傳而唐虞之政不講故耶宜乎
執事拳拳于此也抑愚聞之二者之政出
于心而操心之要則不外於敬堯之欽舜
之恭禹之祗台德先湯之聖敬日躋文武
之小心翼翼皆是道也能乎此則敬天而
必知以勤民為務勤民而必知以敬天為
本也此則愚之誦法孔孟而自得者敢併
punctuated: 方，而政猶可稱也。若乃秦皇相李斯而衡石程書，隋文用高熲而衞士傳飡，則徒事其小而反遺其大，其勤民也，乃所以為厲民也，是固無足道矣。吾獨惜夫神宗勵精之英主也，惟其偏信王安石而更為新法，君子非之，亦與二君並焉。蓋既不知所以為勤，則其播惡于衆一耳。使能聽司馬光之讜論，寧至盡違其願治之心如此哉？嗚呼！敬天一也，或以之治，而亦或以亂；勤民一也，或以之盛，而亦或以衰。其毫釐之差，而天淵之判如此，揆厥所由，得非以其孔孟之學不傳，而唐虞之政不講故耶？宜乎執事拳拳于此也！抑愚聞之，二者之政出于心，而操心之要則不外於敬。堯之欽，舜之恭，禹之「祗台德先」，湯之「聖敬日躋」，文武之「小心翼翼」，皆是道也。能乎此，則敬天而必知以勤民為務，勤民而必知以敬天為本也。此則愚之誦法孔孟而自得者，敢併
translation_en:
…the means of bringing peace to the people, yet their government was still commendable. As for the Qin emperor, who appointed Li Si as his chief minister and set a daily quota of documents by weight, and Emperor Wen of the Sui, who employed Gao Jiong and had guards pass along his meals, they merely attended to minor matters while neglecting the great ones. Their diligence on behalf of the people thus became a means of afflicting them. These cases certainly merit no further discussion. I particularly regret the case of Emperor Shenzong, an able ruler who applied himself energetically to government. Simply because he placed undue trust in Wang Anshi and instituted the New Policies, gentlemen condemned him and ranked him alongside those two rulers. Since he did not understand how to exercise diligence, he was just like them in spreading harm among the people. Had he listened to Sima Guang’s forthright arguments, would he have so completely frustrated his own desire for good government?

Alas! Reverence for Heaven is one and the same undertaking, yet some achieve order through it while others bring disorder; diligence on behalf of the people is one and the same undertaking, yet some achieve prosperity through it while others bring decline. A deviation as slight as a hair’s breadth produces a divergence as great as that between heaven and the abyss. In considering the reason, could it not be that the learning of Confucius and Mencius has not been transmitted and the government of Tang and Yu has not been studied? It is fitting that you, honored examiners, should be so deeply concerned with this!

Yet I have heard that both these practices of government proceed from the mind, and that the essential means of keeping the mind under control lies wholly in reverent attentiveness. Yao’s reverence, Shun’s respectfulness, Yu’s resolve to “reverently put my virtue first,” Tang’s “sagacity and reverence rising daily,” and Kings Wen and Wu’s “careful vigilance”—all embody this Way. One who can achieve this will, in revering Heaven, necessarily know to make diligent care for the people his task, and, in diligently caring for the people, necessarily know to make reverence for Heaven his foundation. This is what I have understood for myself through studying and taking Confucius and Mencius as my models, and I venture also to…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
舉以為獻
第五問
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批此卷有才有識知古知今北方之學者未能或之先也卓冠多士孰曰不宜
同考試官教授王批不為問目所拘自是策手
考試官左諭德靳批論將一策奚足盡子之蘊然即是以觀其學識超卓亦自見之噫吾子出而冀北之群空矣
考試官學士江批觀此策與前二場俱稱宜置第一
===
有濟時之法必有用法之人而後可夫法
者人之所為也得其人則弊者更之利者
創之已善者行之不得而阻也已用者執
之不得而移也否則法雖具也豈不有視
為故事而應以虛文者哉盖凡任天下之
事者皆然矧兵戎國之大事可弗然乎傳
曰為政在人此不易之論也雖然執事以
論將之法策承學而承學以是對不亦迂
乎請先籌其所謂法者大都論將之策無
punctuated:
舉以為獻。

第五問
張璿
同考試官教諭姜批：此卷有才有識，知古知今，北方之學者未能或之先也。卓冠多士，孰曰不宜？
同考試官教授王批：不為問目所拘，自是策手。
考試官左諭德靳批：論將一策，奚足盡子之蘊？然即是以觀，其學識超卓，亦自見之。噫！吾子出而冀北之群空矣。
考試官學士江批：觀此策，與前二場俱稱，宜置第一。

有濟時之法，必有用法之人而後可。夫法者，人之所為也。得其人，則弊者更之，利者創之，已善者行之，不得而阻也；已用者執之，不得而移也。否則法雖具也，豈不有視為故事而應以虛文者哉？盖凡任天下之事者皆然，矧兵戎，國之大事，可弗然乎？傳曰：「為政在人。」此不易之論也。雖然，執事以論將之法策承學，而承學以是對，不亦迂乎？請先籌其所謂法者。大都論將之策無
translation_en:
…present these together as my offering.

Fifth Question
Zhang Xuan 張璿
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: This paper displays talent and discernment, with knowledge of both antiquity and the present. Among scholars of the north, none can surpass him. Who could say it is inappropriate that he should stand preeminent among the many candidates?
Associate Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: He is not constrained by the question’s particulars. Clearly he is an accomplished writer of policy essays.
Examiner Jin, Left Admonisher, comments: How could a single policy essay on assessing generals exhaust the learning you possess? Yet even from this, the exceptional quality of your learning and discernment is evident. Ah! With your emergence, the herds of northern Ji are emptied of their finest horses!
Examiner Jiang, Academician, comments: On examining this policy essay, I find it fully commensurate with his work in the preceding two sessions. He should be ranked first.

Even when there are methods for meeting the needs of the times, there must be people capable of applying them before they can succeed. Methods, after all, are devised by people. If the right people are obtained, they reform what is defective, institute what is beneficial, and implement what is already sound, allowing nothing to obstruct it; they uphold what has already been put into practice, allowing nothing to displace it. Otherwise, even if the methods are all in place, will there not be those who regard them merely as established precedents and respond with empty formalities? This holds true of all who undertake the affairs of the realm. How could it fail to apply to military affairs, a matter of great importance to the state? The commentary says: “The conduct of government depends on people.” This is an unalterable principle. Nevertheless, you, honored examiners, have questioned this student about methods for assessing generals. Is it not rather circuitous for me to reply in this way? Let me first consider what are called methods. Broadly speaking, the approach to assessing generals has no…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
他求之任之兩端而已以求之之道言之
非廣以致之於先精以擇之於後不可也
以任之之道言之非信之專以責其功馭
之嚴以警其心不可也盍觀之醫乎赤箭
青芝靡不素具於一囊夫然後卒遇奇疾
則吾得以擇其良者投之而功可計日奏
也使所蓄不豫則雖欲擇之曷從而擇之
求將者何以異此是故不以疏遠而遺不
以過誤而廢不以仇怨而黜不以親嫌而
===
避如范仲淹欲於諸班中搜羅智勇而試
以武藝可也如歐陽脩欲於軍伍間較其
技勇而抜為大將可也如富弼請令近臣
及藩鎮大臣各舉武畧可也如蘇軾請重
武舉而試以治軍可也故曰求將之道非
廣以致之於先精以擇之於後不可也又
不觀之良冶乎干將鏌鎁天下之重寶也
一聽其所為然後千金之器成否則雖良
工無能為也任將者獨不然邪且戰危事
punctuated:
他，求之、任之兩端而已。以求之之道言之，非廣以致之於先、精以擇之於後不可也。以任之之道言之，非信之專以責其功、馭之嚴以警其心不可也。盍觀之醫乎？赤箭、青芝，靡不素具於一囊，夫然後卒遇奇疾，則吾得以擇其良者投之，而功可計日奏也。使所蓄不豫，則雖欲擇之，曷從而擇之？求將者何以異此？是故不以疏遠而遺，不以過誤而廢，不以仇怨而黜，不以親嫌而避。如范仲淹欲於諸班中搜羅智勇而試以武藝，可也；如歐陽脩欲於軍伍間較其技勇而抜為大將，可也；如富弼請令近臣及藩鎮大臣各舉武畧，可也；如蘇軾請重武舉而試以治軍，可也。故曰：求將之道，非廣以致之於先、精以擇之於後不可也。

又不觀之良冶乎？干將、鏌鎁，天下之重寶也。一聽其所為，然後千金之器成；否則雖良工，無能為也。任將者獨不然邪？且戰，危事
translation_en:
…other than these two matters: finding commanders and employing them. As for finding them, one must first attract candidates widely and then select them carefully. As for employing them, one must give them undivided trust and hold them accountable for results, while controlling them strictly to keep them vigilant. Consider the physician: medicinal gastrodia and green lingzhi are always ready in his medicine bag. Only then, when an unusual illness suddenly arises, can he select and administer the appropriate remedy, with results achievable within a matter of days. If he has not laid in supplies beforehand, then even if he wishes to select a remedy, from what can he choose? How is finding commanders any different? Thus, do not overlook men because they are distant or little known, discard them because of mistakes, reject them because of enmities, or avoid them because their kinship ties might arouse suspicion of favoritism. One may follow Fan Zhongyan, who wished to seek out men of intelligence and courage among the various guard units and test their martial skills; Ouyang Xiu, who wished to compare the skills and courage of men in the ranks and promote them to high command; Fu Bi, who requested that close attendant officials and senior regional military authorities each recommend men versed in military strategy; or Su Shi, who requested that greater importance be attached to the military examinations and that candidates be tested in managing troops. Hence I say: to find commanders, one must first attract candidates widely and then select them carefully.

Consider also the skilled metalworker. Ganjiang and Moye are treasures of the highest order in the world. Only when the craftsman is given complete freedom in his work can an implement worth a thousand pieces of gold be fashioned; otherwise, even a skilled artisan can accomplish nothing. Is employing commanders alone any different? Moreover, warfare is a perilous undertaking…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也兵凶器也逗遛者無罰敗撓者無刑則
彼亦孰肯舍其父母妻孥仰賴之身而輕
爲吾用哉是故必結之以誠信必假之以
威權有功者必賞不以賤而遺有罪者必
刑不以親而貸如陸贄所謂專付任以息
苟且可也如張方平所謂責久任以觀能
效可也如王巖叟所謂勿輕加進退而重
謹之可也如胡寅所謂信賞必罰而虛文
之悉去可也故曰任將之道非信之專以
===
責其功馭之嚴以警其心不可也迂疎之
見所以為本兵者計不過如此而用是法
者竊以為則在乎有其人焉耳試以明問
所疑者證之搴旗斬將非武不可然有人
焉以擇之則如布如成者皆吾鷹犬也庸
何傷運籌决勝非文不能然有人焉以擇
之則如機如琯者皆吾記室也庸何害老
而才如伏波吾必舉之非舉其老也舉其
才也彼單之恃功而驕正坐無人以駕之
punctuated:
也，兵凶器也。逗遛者無罰，敗撓者無刑，則彼亦孰肯舍其父母妻孥仰賴之身，而輕爲吾用哉？是故必結之以誠信，必假之以威權。有功者必賞，不以賤而遺；有罪者必刑，不以親而貸。如陸贄所謂專付任以息苟且，可也；如張方平所謂責久任以觀能效，可也；如王巖叟所謂勿輕加進退而重謹之，可也；如胡寅所謂信賞必罰而虛文之悉去，可也。故曰：任將之道，非信之專以責其功，馭之嚴以警其心，不可也。

迂疎之見，所以為本兵者計，不過如此。而用是法者，竊以為則在乎有其人焉耳。試以明問所疑者證之：搴旗斬將，非武不可；然有人焉以擇之，則如布如成者皆吾鷹犬也，庸何傷？運籌决勝，非文不能；然有人焉以擇之，則如機如琯者皆吾記室也，庸何害？老而才如伏波，吾必舉之，非舉其老也，舉其才也。彼單之恃功而驕，正坐無人以駕之
translation_en:
…; weapons are instruments of ill omen. If those who delay their advance receive no punishment, and those who falter in defeat suffer no penalty, who among them would willingly risk the life upon which his parents, wife, and children depend, and readily enter our service? Thus we must bind them to us through sincerity and good faith, and entrust them with authority. Those who render meritorious service must be rewarded, none being overlooked because of low status; those who commit offenses must be punished, none being pardoned because of close personal ties. We may follow Lu Zhi’s proposal to entrust commanders fully with responsibility, thereby ending careless expediency; Zhang Fangping’s proposal to hold them accountable over long tenures, thereby observing their ability and results; Wang Yansou’s proposal to avoid casually promoting or dismissing them, treating such decisions seriously and cautiously; or Hu Yin’s proposal to make rewards trustworthy and punishments certain, eliminating all empty formalities. Thus I say: in employing generals, we must trust them fully and demand achievements, while controlling them strictly to keep them vigilant.

Such are the limits of the counsels that my impractical and ill-informed views can offer those in charge of military affairs. Yet I venture to think that putting these methods into practice depends upon having the right person. Let me demonstrate this through the doubts raised in your discerning question. Capturing standards and slaying enemy generals require martial prowess. Yet if there is someone capable of selecting such men, figures like Bu and Cheng [?] will all serve as our hawks and hounds: what harm could there be? Devising strategies and securing victory require literary learning. Yet if there is someone capable of selecting such men, figures like Ji and Guan [?] will all serve as our secretaries: what harm could there be? If a man is old but talented, like the General Who Calms the Waves, I will certainly recommend him—not for his age, but for his talent. As for Dan [?], who grew arrogant in reliance upon his achievements, this was precisely because there was no one capable of keeping him under control…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
耳少而才如淮陰吾必薦之非薦其少也
薦其才也彼括之虛譽而用正坐無人以
識之耳按圖索驥地産不可以得才也而
得才者亦有之惟有人焉則辛趙之徒出
矣肉食者鄙門望不可以得才也而得才
者亦有之惟有人焉則王謝之流出矣以
是論之則所謂求將之策材在本兵者之
有人而後舉乎漢高捐爵賞而功臣之不
保此則賞于無功之時啓之耳使有人焉
===
贊之則賞所當賞賞之適以作其趨事之
心功多難處非所患也宋祖吝使相而武
功之不競此則吝于有功之後以致之耳
使有人焉匡之則吝所當吝吝之適以鼓
其効力之志武事不競非所恤也雖曰專
其任以委之而操縱之幾實有人以總之
于廟堂豈與唐之事同哉雖曰分其權以
制之而戰陳之事實有人以責之于將領
豈與晉之事同哉非能不以聞而所用者
punctuated: 耳。少而才如淮陰，吾必薦之，非薦其少也，薦其才也。彼括之虛譽而用，正坐無人以識之耳。按圖索驥，地産不可以得才也，而得才者亦有之，惟有人焉，則辛趙之徒出矣。肉食者鄙，門望不可以得才也，而得才者亦有之，惟有人焉，則王謝之流出矣。以是論之，則所謂求將之策材，在本兵者之有人而後舉乎？漢高捐爵賞而功臣之不保，此則賞于無功之時啓之耳。使有人焉贊之，則賞所當賞，賞之適以作其趨事之心，功多難處非所患也。宋祖吝使相而武功之不競，此則吝于有功之後以致之耳。使有人焉匡之，則吝所當吝，吝之適以鼓其効力之志，武事不競非所恤也。雖曰專其任以委之，而操縱之幾，實有人以總之于廟堂，豈與唐之事同哉？雖曰分其權以制之，而戰陳之事，實有人以責之于將領，豈與晉之事同哉？非能不以聞，而所用者
translation_en:
…that is all. If a young man has talent like the Marquis of Huaiyin, I will certainly recommend him—not for his youth, but for his talent. That Kuo was employed on the strength of an empty reputation was precisely because no one was there to discern his true worth. Seeking a fine horse by consulting a picture: a man’s place of origin is no reliable means of finding talent. Yet talent has sometimes been found this way; provided the right person is there, men like Xin and Zhao will emerge. “Those who eat meat are narrow-minded”: family standing is no reliable means of finding talent. Yet talent has sometimes been found this way; provided the right person is there, men like Wang and Xie will emerge. Judged in this light, can the so-called strategy for seeking generals and assessing talent [?] be carried out only when the right person holds responsibility for military affairs?

Emperor Gao of the Han freely bestowed noble ranks and rewards, yet his meritorious ministers did not remain secure. This arose from rewarding them before they had performed meritorious service. Had the right person been there to assist him, he would have rewarded those who deserved rewards, thereby stirring their eagerness to serve. There would have been no need to worry that men with many achievements would become difficult to handle. The founding emperor of the Song was sparing in granting the title of military commissioner with honorary grand councilor status, and military achievement languished. This resulted from his withholding rewards after meritorious service had been performed. Had the right person been there to correct him, he would have withheld only what ought to be withheld, thereby encouraging their determination to exert themselves. There would have been no need to worry about a lack of military achievement.

Although a general is entrusted with sole responsibility, someone at court in fact oversees the crucial decisions about restraint and freedom of action. How could this be the same as what happened under the Tang? Although a general’s authority is divided to keep him in check, someone in fact holds the commanders accountable for matters of battle and deployment. How could this be the same as what happened under the Jin? Only capable men are brought to the throne’s attention, and those employed…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
皆去病其人則福將之說不禁而自息矣
非賢不以薦而所任皆祭遵其人則債帥
之請不却而自遠矣以是論之則所謂任
將之策又不在本兵者之有人而後舉乎
嗟夫必有蕭何而後能成韓信之名必有
魏相而後能用充國之議李愬淮西之功
裴度主之也狄青嶺南之功龐籍贊之也
此愚所以反復明問而始終必以本兵者
為言非敢強為大也攷之古驗之今計誠
===
無善于此者而尤有本焉未敢以遽布也
執事儻與其進使得立
玉階方寸地尚當為
明主陳之
punctuated:
皆去病其人，則福將之說不禁而自息矣。非賢不以薦，而所任皆祭遵其人，則債帥之請不却而自遠矣。以是論之，則所謂任將之策，又不在本兵者之有人而後舉乎？

嗟夫！必有蕭何而後能成韓信之名，必有魏相而後能用充國之議。李愬淮西之功，裴度主之也；狄青嶺南之功，龐籍贊之也。此愚所以反復明問，而始終必以本兵者為言，非敢強為大也。攷之古，驗之今，計誠無善于此者，而尤有本焉，未敢以遽布也。執事儻與其進，使得立玉階方寸地，尚當為明主陳之。
translation_en:
… are all men like Huo Qubing, then talk of “lucky generals” will cease of itself, without being prohibited. If only worthy men are recommended, and all those appointed are men like Ji Zun, then the petitions of “debt-burdened commanders”—those who borrow to purchase appointments—will disappear of themselves, without being rejected. Judged in this light, does not the policy of appointing generals likewise depend upon having the right man in charge of military affairs before it can be put into effect?

Alas! Only with Xiao He could Han Xin establish his reputation; only with Wei Xiang could Zhao Chongguo’s proposals be adopted. Li Su’s achievement in Huaixi had Pei Du directing it; Di Qing’s achievement in Lingnan had Pang Ji supporting it. This is why, in repeatedly considering your illuminating question, I have insisted from beginning to end on speaking of the man in charge of military affairs. I do not presume to magnify the issue unduly. Examined against antiquity and tested against the present, there is truly no better plan. Yet there is something still more fundamental, which I have not ventured to set forth hastily. If you, sir, should approve my advancement and enable me to stand upon even a tiny patch of ground before the imperial jade steps, I shall then lay it before our enlightened sovereign.

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
今年秋八月
上命臣瀾臣貴來考順天府鄉試既
畢事臣貴謹拜稽序其後曰嗚
呼文其盛甚矣哉所錄者雖僅
百三十五人然限於
制額而不能悉錄者尚倍蓰也竊
===
嘗求其故矣順天府今
京師也昔之人固有擬其形勢宜
為王者之居曰天府之國者亦
已得其一端矣而未覩其大也
蓋茲地於天文其次為紫微之
垣於禹貢為冀州之域於輿地
槩之則處北而南面之位也孔
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

今年秋八月，上命臣瀾、臣貴來考順天府鄉試。既畢事，臣貴謹拜稽，序其後曰：嗚呼！文其盛甚矣哉！所錄者雖僅百三十五人，然限於制額而不能悉錄者，尚倍蓰也。竊嘗求其故矣。順天府，今京師也。昔之人固有擬其形勢宜為王者之居，曰天府之國者，亦已得其一端矣，而未覩其大也。蓋茲地於天文，其次為紫微之垣；於禹貢，為冀州之域；於輿地槩之，則處北而南面之位也。孔
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn this year, His Majesty commanded us, his servants Lan and Gui, to come and examine candidates in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination. Once the work was completed, I, your servant Gui, respectfully bowed and kowtowed [?], and composed this postface:

Ah! How flourishing literary accomplishment has become! Although only 135 men were admitted, those who could not all be admitted because of the prescribed quota numbered several times as many. I have privately sought the reason for this abundance. Shuntian Prefecture is now the imperial capital. Among the men of earlier times, there were certainly those who judged its terrain and strategic situation suitable for a royal residence and called it a land of Heaven’s storehouse. They had grasped one aspect of it, but had not yet perceived its full greatness. In celestial geography, this land corresponds to the Purple Tenuity Enclosure; in the Tribute of Yu, it lies within the territory of Jizhou; and, viewed broadly in terrestrial geography, it occupies the position of one seated in the north and facing south. Confucius …

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
子於贊易之離亦曰聖人南面
而聽天下嚮明而治夫孔子奚
取於離哉重明麗正臨照天下
而無遠不被蓋人文之化之所
由成也故帝王之順天居正而
欲以文教經天下者莫此為宜
然自堯舜禹湯文武以來未之
===
居也乃或淪於左衽者數百年
蓋天使之為驅除以待于今耳
肆我
太宗文皇帝實弘丕承用光
天命乃始于此定都焉于時承平無
事日以右文圖治為務其大者
表章五經四書輯為大全頒示
punctuated:
子於贊易之離亦曰：「聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治。」夫孔子奚取於離哉？重明麗正，臨照天下而無遠不被，蓋人文之化之所由成也。故帝王之順天居正，而欲以文教經天下者，莫此為宜。然自堯舜禹湯文武以來，未之居也，乃或淪於左衽者數百年，蓋天使之為驅除，以待于今耳。
肆我太宗文皇帝實弘丕承，用光天命，乃始于此定都焉。于時承平無事，日以右文圖治為務。其大者，表章五經四書，輯為大全，頒示
translation_en:
…Confucius, too, in his commentary on the Li hexagram of the Book of Changes, said: “The sage faces south to attend to all under Heaven; he turns toward the light and governs.” What, then, did Confucius find in Li? Doubled brightness adheres to what is correct, shining down upon all under Heaven, reaching even the remotest places: this is how transformation through human culture is accomplished. Thus, for emperors and kings who accord with Heaven, occupy the proper position, and wish to order all under Heaven through cultural instruction, no place is more fitting than this. Yet from the time of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu onward, none had made his seat here. Indeed, at times it fell for hundreds of years under those who fastened their robes on the left—the non-Chinese. Heaven presumably employed them to clear the way in anticipation of our own age.
Then our Emperor Taizong Wen greatly carried forward the grand inheritance, thereby glorifying Heaven’s mandate, and first established the capital here. In that time of peace and tranquility, he devoted himself daily to honoring learning and seeking good government. Among his major undertakings, he exalted the Five Classics and Four Books, had them compiled into the Complete Compendia, and promulgated them…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天下學校以此講習科目以此
取士士大夫以此治心脩身而
達諸治凡昔聖賢相傳之學經
緯化成之文煥然而大明生斯
世為斯民者莫不自慶以為復
見堯舜禹湯文武之盛于
今也臣故曰順天居正以文教經
===
天下莫此為宜然則登仕于
朝者亦難乎其為臣也已故嘗極
其類而推之其必有益稷契臯
陶伊傅周召之疇而後可以為
公為孤為卿大夫為百執事以
共保我文明之盛治而無愧而
其人之果出于今者則亦不得
punctuated: 天下。學校以此講習，科目以此取士，士大夫以此治心脩身而達諸治。凡昔聖賢相傳之學、經緯化成之文，煥然而大明。生斯世、為斯民者，莫不自慶，以為復見堯舜禹湯文武之盛于今也。臣故曰：「順天居正，以文教經天下，莫此為宜。」然則登仕于朝者，亦難乎其為臣也已！故嘗極其類而推之，其必有益稷契臯陶伊傅周召之疇，而後可以為公、為孤、為卿大夫、為百執事，以共保我文明之盛治而無愧。而其人之果出于今者，則亦不得
translation_en: …throughout the realm. Schools use these works for instruction and study; the examinations use them to select men of talent; and scholar-officials use them to discipline their minds and cultivate themselves, extending this cultivation to government. All the learning transmitted by the sages and worthies of antiquity, and the literary culture through which they ordered the world and transformed its people, shine forth in full brilliance. Those born in this age and living among its people all rejoice in their good fortune, believing that they now witness once again the flourishing age of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Thus your servant says: “Shuntian occupies the proper central position; no place is more fitting for ordering the realm through cultural instruction.” Yet how difficult, then, is the duty of serving as a minister for those who enter office at court! I have therefore sought to pursue this reasoning to its fullest extent: there must be men of the company of Yi, Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. Only then can they serve as dukes, junior guardians, ministers, grand masters, and the various functionaries, together preserving the flourishing government of our cultural enlightenment without falling short. And if such men are indeed to emerge in our own day, then we cannot but…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不于科目焉求之然則科目之
文其所係不既重邪雖然彼益
稷契臯陶伊傅周召者固亦人
耳其生平所學與其經緯化成
之文具在今之士既講習之於
學校矣其無愧與否一為不為
之間亦何古今人之不相若乎
况爾諸士皆以天民之傑産首
善之地而又陶於
列聖重熈累洽之餘觀感於我
聖天子率循
祖訓誕敷文德之下最深且久安知
無若人者之出于今邪顧臣不
敏何足以仰稱
punctuated: 不于科目焉求之。然則科目之文，其所係不既重邪？雖然，彼益稷契臯陶伊傅周召者，固亦人耳。其生平所學，與其經緯化成之文，具在。今之士既講習之於學校矣，其無愧與否，一為不為之間，亦何古今人之不相若乎？况爾諸士皆以天民之傑，産首善之地，而又陶於列聖重熈累洽之餘，觀感於我聖天子率循祖訓、誕敷文德之下，最深且久。安知無若人者之出于今邪？顧臣不敏，何足以仰稱
translation_en:
…cannot but seek them through the examinations. Does this not mean that the writing produced in the examinations carries weighty consequences indeed? Nevertheless, Yi, Ji, Xie, Gaoyao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao were themselves only human. What they studied throughout their lives, together with the writings through which they ordered the world and brought its transformation to fruition, are all still extant. Today's scholars have already studied and discussed these in the schools. Whether they can stand without shame before these exemplars depends entirely on whether they act or fail to act. Why should people of antiquity and those of today be unequal to one another?
Moreover, all you scholars, outstanding among Heaven's people, were born in the place that leads the realm in goodness. You have also been nurtured by the enduring legacy of successive sage emperors, whose glorious and peaceful reigns built upon one another. Under our sage Son of Heaven, who follows the ancestral injunctions and widely spreads civil virtue, you have been inspired by what you have witnessed, most profoundly and for a long time. How can we know that men like those exemplars will not emerge today? Yet your servant is untalented: how could I adequately fulfill…

title: 弘治十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
明詔然敬事之心則不敢不自罄
也用是輒書簡末敢獻以為
賀且以為諸士告云
奉訓大夫左春坊左諭德兼翰
林院侍講靳貴謹序
punctuated:
明詔，然敬事之心，則不敢不自罄也。用是輒書簡末，敢獻以為賀，且以為諸士告云。
奉訓大夫、左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍講靳貴謹序。
translation_en:
…the enlightened imperial edict. Yet in my resolve to attend reverently to this duty, I dare not fail to exert myself to the utmost. Thus I have ventured to write these words at the end of the volume, respectfully offering them as congratulations and also as an admonition to the candidates.
Preface respectfully composed by Jin Gui, Grand Master for Instruction, Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
